items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 料（りょう）＋理（り）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You take raw <kanji>materials</kanji> and run them through the strict <kanji>logic</kanji> of a recipe, step after step. When that turns them into a hot meal, you <vocabulary>cook</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は台所で料理する。
example_sentences.english: My mother cooks in the kitchen.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は台[だい]所[どころ]で料[りょう]理[り]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は魚を料理する。
example_sentences.english: I cook fish today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は魚[さかな]を料[りょう]理[り]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は料理するのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: She likes cooking.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は料[りょう]理[り]するのが好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 仕（し）on'yomi ＋ 事（ごと）kun'yomi. Rendaku: 事 こと → ごと.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>matter</kanji> you loyally <kanji>attend</kanji> to day after day, sandals fetched and tea poured, is your <vocabulary>work / job</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は仕事があります。
example_sentences.english: I have work today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は仕[し]事[ごと]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事は難しいです。
example_sentences.english: This job is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: この仕[し]事[ごと]は難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は仕事を休みます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm taking the day off work.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は仕[し]事[ごと]を休[やす]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Tess never revises, so the pop quiz lands, she panics, kicks the desk leg, and jams her <reading>Tess toe</reading>. Her yelp of <reading>テスト</reading> is the sound of every surprise <vocabulary>test</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はテストがあります。
example_sentences.english: There's a test tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]はテストがあります。

example_sentences.japanese: このテストは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: This test is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: このテストは難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はテストを出しました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher handed out a test.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]はテストを出[だ]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 答（こた）＋え.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The hand that shoots up, the words that make the teacher stop scanning the room and nod, is the <vocabulary>answer</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 答 is 「こた」 from 答える, so the <vocabulary>answer</vocabulary> you fill the blank with is <reading>こたえ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 答えはこれです。
example_sentences.english: The answer is this one.
example_sentences.furigana: 答[こた]えはこれです。

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい答えを書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a difficult answer.
example_sentences.furigana: 難[むずか]しい答[こた]えを書[か]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 答えが分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand the answer.
example_sentences.furigana: 答[こた]えが分[わ]かりません。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Rumor goes that <reading>Hera gonna</reading> teach the soft, looping letters first, before anything with a sharp edge, and that rounded beginner script is <vocabulary>hiragana</vocabulary>. Say the goddess and her plan in one breath and you land on <reading>ひらがな</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はひらがなを書けます。
example_sentences.english: I can write hiragana.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はひらがなを書[か]けます。

example_sentences.japanese: ひらがなは読めますか。
example_sentences.english: Can you read hiragana?
example_sentences.furigana: ひらがなは読[よ]めますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日ひらがなを勉強します。
example_sentences.english: I study hiragana every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]ひらがなを勉[べん]強[きょう]します。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The letters look like someone took a ruler and decided to <reading>cut a corner</reading> on every curve, leaving nothing but sharp straight angles. That stiff script for foreign words is <vocabulary>katakana</vocabulary>, and <reading>カタカナ</reading> is that phrase said fast.

example_sentences.japanese: ノートにカタカナを書きます。
example_sentences.english: I write katakana in my notebook.
example_sentences.furigana: ノートにカタカナを書[か]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: カタカナは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Katakana is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: カタカナは難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: ひらがなとカタカナを覚えます。
example_sentences.english: I memorize hiragana and katakana.
example_sentences.furigana: ひらがなとカタカナを覚[おぼ]えます。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — にほん cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 日本.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>sun</kanji> clears the horizon here first, at the very <kanji>origin</kanji> of the day. That country is <vocabulary>Japan</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hiker at the top of the mountain trail watches the sunrise and raps her <reading>knee bone</reading> twice for the beats as she names the country it rises over, 「<reading>にほん</reading>」, and that country is <vocabulary>Japan</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like Japan.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は日本[にほん]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は日本に住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My older brother lives in Japan.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は日本[にほん]に住[す]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の食べ物はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: Japanese food is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]の食[た]べ物[もの]はおいしいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — お＋金（かね）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>money</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>money</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so they mean exactly the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane keeps her gold coins in a little roofed safe, and when she lifts the lid, visitors gasp '<reading>oh, Kane</reading>' at so much <vocabulary form="お金">money</vocabulary>: 「<reading>おかね</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布にお金がありません。
example_sentences.english: There's no money in my wallet.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]にお金[かね]がありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達にお金を借りました。
example_sentences.english: I borrowed money from a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]にお金[かね]を借[か]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行でお金を払います。
example_sentences.english: I'll pay the money at the bank.
example_sentences.furigana: 銀[ぎん]行[こう]でお金[かね]を払[はら]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 女（おんな）＋の＋子（こ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A costume shop sells a miniature <kanji>woman</kanji> outfit sized only for a <kanji>child</kanji>, and whoever fits into it is simply called a <vocabulary>girl</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの女の子は学生です。
example_sentences.english: That girl over there is a student.
example_sentences.furigana: あの女[おんな]の子[こ]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 女の子が公園で遊びます。
example_sentences.english: A girl plays in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 女[おんな]の子[こ]が公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 女の子と一緒に映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with a girl.
example_sentences.furigana: 女[おんな]の子[こ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 午（ご）＋後（ご）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once the clock falls <kanji>behind</kanji> <kanji>noon</kanji>, every hour left in the day counts as <vocabulary>afternoon</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 午後にコーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I'll have coffee in the afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 午[ご]後[ご]にコーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の午後は忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm busy this afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]の午[ご]後[ご]は忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 午後に公園で遊びます。
example_sentences.english: I'll hang out at the park in the afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 午[ご]後[ご]に公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]びます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 夫（おっと）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The one who groans the loudest fixing a leaky faucet at 2 AM is your <vocabulary>husband</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At 2 AM the leaky faucet sprays him in the face, and between groans your <vocabulary form="夫">husband</vocabulary> yelps <reading>おっと</reading>, a startled '<reading>oh, toe</reading>' as the wrench lands on his foot.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夫は毎日忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: My husband is busy every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の夫[おっと]は毎[まい]日[にち]忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫と一緒に映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch movies with my husband.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫はコーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: My husband drinks coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]はコーヒーを飲[の]みます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（だい）＋丈（じょう）＋夫（ぶ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>man</kanji> whose <kanji>measure</kanji> from heel to head is this <kanji>big</kanji> can take a hard knock and still walk away <vocabulary>all right / okay</vocabulary>. It works as a な adjective, so な sits before any noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 足は大丈夫ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is your foot okay?
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]は大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]ですか？

example_sentences.japanese: 私は大丈夫です。
example_sentences.english: I'm all right.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は大丈夫ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow is fine.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]ですよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 目（め）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>eye</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>eye</vocabulary> word are one and the same character, so there is nothing new to learn here.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>May</reading> the staring doll has one <vocabulary form="目">eye</vocabulary> painted on its side, a box of eyelid with two lines for a pupil, and when it stares back you shiver 「<reading>め</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の目はいいです。
example_sentences.english: My eyes are good.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の目[め]はいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 医者は私の目を見ます。
example_sentences.english: The doctor looks at my eyes.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]は私[わたし]の目[め]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 朝、目を開けます。
example_sentences.english: In the morning, I open my eyes.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]、目[め]を開[あ]けます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 安（やす）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>cheap</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>cheap</vocabulary> word are one and the same, so they mean the same thing. That final い is what turns it into an adjective, a marker every い adjective shares.
items.reading_mnemonic: The woman tucked under the snug roof pays almost nothing in rent, so it is <vocabulary form="安い">cheap</vocabulary> enough to keep a pig too, which she calls in at dusk with a happy <reading>ya, sooey!</reading>, <reading>やすい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This book is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 安いお茶を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought some cheap tea.
example_sentences.furigana: 安[やす]いお茶[ちゃ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの店は安いですか。
example_sentences.english: Is that shop cheap?
example_sentences.furigana: あの店[みせ]は安[やす]いですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 男（おとこ）＋の＋人（ひと）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone asks who that <kanji>person</kanji> is, still out in the field flexing all that power. It's simply the <kanji>man</kanji> you already know, nothing more than a <vocabulary>man</vocabulary>.
items.description: 男 alone can sound blunt when pointing at a specific man; 男の人 is the everyday, polite way to say it in conversation.

example_sentences.japanese: この男の人は医者です。
example_sentences.english: This man is a doctor.
example_sentences.furigana: この男[おとこ]の人[ひと]は医[い]者[しゃ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は男の人と話します。
example_sentences.english: She talks with a man.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は男[おとこ]の人[ひと]と話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で男の人が待ちます。
example_sentences.english: A man will wait at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が待[ま]ちます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 男（おとこ）＋の＋子（こ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>man</kanji> in the rice field has a <kanji>child</kanji> copying him, flexing a tiny arm, too small to plow anything. That miniature power alone is what makes a <vocabulary>boy</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男の子は学生です。
example_sentences.english: That boy over there is a student.
example_sentences.furigana: あの男[おとこ]の子[こ]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 男の子が公園で遊びます。
example_sentences.english: The boy plays in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 男[おとこ]の子[こ]が公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は男の子と話します。
example_sentences.english: I talk with the boy.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は男[おとこ]の子[こ]と話[はな]します。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 午（ご）＋前（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every hour that still stands <kanji>front</kanji> of <kanji>noon</kanji> counts as <vocabulary>morning</vocabulary>, before lunch begins.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は午前十時に会います。
example_sentences.english: Today we'll meet at ten a.m.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は午[ご]前[ぜん]十[じゅう]時[じ]に会[あ]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は午前にコーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: He drinks coffee in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は午[ご]前[ぜん]にコーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 映画は午前九時です。
example_sentences.english: The movie is at nine a.m.
example_sentences.furigana: 映[えい]画[が]は午[ご]前[ぜん]九[く]時[じ]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 家（いえ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every other door you have to be buzzed through or invited into. The one place you already own the key to is your <vocabulary>house / home</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A courier works the whole lane, asking at every door whether anyone truly lives there. At the last one a tired voice finally says <reading>「いえ」</reading>, which is just <reading>yeah</reading>, this is my <vocabulary>house / home</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 家に帰ります。
example_sentences.english: I'm going home.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]に帰[かえ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: この家はいいです。
example_sentences.english: This house is nice.
example_sentences.furigana: この家[いえ]はいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は家で映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: On weekends I watch movies at home.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は家[いえ]で映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 悪（わる）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Whatever noun you set this in front of, it drags the thing down. The い hanging off the end makes it an adjective, and the verdict it lands on is <vocabulary>bad</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Each time Rooey the puppy plants himself in front of something, a shoe or a cushion, he drags it down and chews it, and his owner groans <reading>wah, Rooey</reading>, <reading>わるい</reading>, delivering the verdict: <vocabulary form="悪い">bad</vocabulary> dog.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が悪いです。
example_sentences.english: I'm the one at fault.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]が悪[わる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は天気が悪いです。
example_sentences.english: The weather is bad today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は天[てん]気[き]が悪[わる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は悪かったです。
example_sentences.english: This movie was bad.
example_sentences.furigana: この映[えい]画[が]は悪[わる]かったです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 旅（りょ）＋行（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>trip</kanji> stays a daydream until the two of you follow the banner to the crossroads and actually <kanji>go</kanji>. Once your feet move, that is <vocabulary>trip / travel</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行は楽しかったです。
example_sentences.english: The trip was fun.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]は楽[たの]しかったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 来年家族と旅行に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Next year I'll go on a trip with my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]家[か]族[ぞく]と旅[りょ]行[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との旅行は楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: A trip with a friend is fun.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]との旅[りょ]行[こう]は楽[たの]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 買（か）＋い＋物（もの）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You sling your net over stall after stall and drop a shell on each counter to <kanji>buy</kanji> every <kanji>thing</kanji> that is not nailed down. Hauling that catch home is <vocabulary>shopping</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は友達と買い物に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Today I'm going shopping with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は友[とも]達[だち]と買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日デパートで買い物をしました。
example_sentences.english: I did some shopping at the department store yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]デパートで買[か]い物[もの]をしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は買い物が好きです。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister likes shopping.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は買[か]い物[もの]が好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The school field's mascot is an old whale in a tank who <reading>spouts</reading> once for every point scored, so the team has taken to calling the whole match 「<reading>スポーツ</reading>」, their word for <vocabulary>sports</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はスポーツが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like sports.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はスポーツが好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は毎週スポーツをします。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother does sports every week.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は毎[まい]週[しゅう]スポーツをします。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はどんなスポーツも上手です。
example_sentences.english: He's good at every kind of sport.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はどんなスポーツも上手[じょうず]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 歌（うた）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Words turn into a <vocabulary>song</vocabulary> the moment a tune picks them up and makes them rise and fall instead of lying flat.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already met this reading in 歌う, so a <vocabulary>song</vocabulary> is just <reading>うた</reading> again.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいつも楽しい歌を歌います。
example_sentences.english: She always sings fun songs.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はいつも楽[たの]しい歌[うた]を歌[うた]います。

example_sentences.japanese: この歌は好きですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you like this song?
example_sentences.furigana: この歌[うた]は好[す]きですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と一緒に歌を歌いました。
example_sentences.english: I sang a song together with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に歌[うた]を歌[うた]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 話（はなし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>talk</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>story</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so they carry the very same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: A parrot on the riverbank has memorised exactly one rambling <vocabulary>story</vocabulary> and retells it to every heron that lands, squawking <reading>はなし</reading> like <reading>'her Nashi pear'</reading> at the same spot each time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はよく友達と話します。
example_sentences.english: I often talk with my friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はよく友[とも]達[だち]と話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: その話は面白いですか？
example_sentences.english: Is that story interesting?
example_sentences.furigana: その話[はなし]は面[おも]白[しろ]いですか？

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は昨日、面白い話をしました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher told an interesting story yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は昨日[きのう]、面[おも]白[しろ]い話[はなし]をしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 物（もの）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>thing</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>thing (object)</vocabulary> word are exactly the same character, and they point at the same idea, a plain object and nothing more.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the farm the cow gets a sweet name, but the farmer calls every bucket and fork in one flat <reading>monotone</reading>: 「<reading>もの</reading>」, just a <vocabulary form="物">thing</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは私の物です。
example_sentences.english: This is my thing.
example_sentences.furigana: これは私[わたし]の物[もの]です。

example_sentences.japanese: その箱の物は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What are the things in that box?
example_sentences.furigana: その箱[はこ]の物[もの]は何[なに]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: その物を取ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please take that thing.
example_sentences.furigana: その物[もの]を取[と]ってください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 事（こと）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the shrine a lantern tips over and an offering goes missing the same morning. Grandma Kane writes each mishap on a slip and calls it one more <vocabulary>thing (matter)</vocabulary> to deal with.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane winds a <reading>cotton</reading> string round her finger for every unfinished <vocabulary>thing (matter)</vocabulary> on her mind. By noon her hand is a fat white ball she taps while muttering 「<reading>こと</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の言う事を聞いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please listen to what I say.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の言[い]う事[こと]を聞[き]いてください。

example_sentences.japanese: それは面白い事ですね。
example_sentences.english: That's an interesting thing, isn't it.
example_sentences.furigana: それは面[おも]白[しろ]い事[こと]ですね。

example_sentences.japanese: 好きな事をしました。
example_sentences.english: I did something I like.
example_sentences.furigana: 好[す]きな事[こと]をしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 所（ところ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A hiker on the mountain trail keeps one photo taped inside his hat. It marks the exact <vocabulary>place</vocabulary> where the path forks to the vending machine, and missing the fork costs him an hour back down.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the fork the hiker taps the photo in his hat and groans '<reading>took a road</reading> wrong here once,' so 「<reading>ところ</reading>」 marks the exact <vocabulary form="所">place</vocabulary> the path splits to the vending machine.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは静かな所です。
example_sentences.english: This is a quiet place.
example_sentences.furigana: ここは静[しず]かな所[ところ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は静かな所が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like quiet places.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は静[しず]かな所[ところ]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: あそこは有名な所です。
example_sentences.english: That place over there is famous.
example_sentences.furigana: あそこは有[ゆう]名[めい]な所[ところ]です。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 方（ほう）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The wooden signpost at the riverbank has spun loose on its post. Now every one of its four arrows points the same <vocabulary>direction / way</vocabulary>, and travellers stand there bickering over which arrow to trust.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、駅はどちらの方ですか。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, which way is the station?
example_sentences.furigana: すみません、駅[えき]はどちらの方[ほう]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便局はあちらの方です。
example_sentences.english: The post office is that way.
example_sentences.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]はあちらの方[ほう]です。

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの方が近いです。
example_sentences.english: This way is closer.
example_sentences.furigana: こちらの方[ほう]が近[ちか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 方（かた）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The new receptionist at the school is painfully formal. She greets every student, even the smallest, as an honoured <vocabulary>person (polite)</vocabulary>, bowing before she hands back a dropped pencil.
items.reading_mnemonic: The receptionist summons the school's gruff hedge <reading>cutter</reading> to shape the entrance bushes. Even he is welcomed as an honoured <vocabulary>person (polite)</vocabulary>, with a deep bow and a careful 「<reading>かた</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: あの方は先生です。
example_sentences.english: That person over there is a teacher.
example_sentences.furigana: あの方[ほう]は先[せん]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: この方は誰ですか。
example_sentences.english: Who is this person?
example_sentences.furigana: この方[ほう]は誰[だれ]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: その方はとても親切でした。
example_sentences.english: That person was very kind.
example_sentences.furigana: その方[ほう]はとても親[しん]切[せつ]でした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 間（あいだ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>between</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>between</vocabulary> word are the same character with the same meaning, so there is nothing new to learn here.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kids at the open gate dare each other, '<reading>I dare</reading> you,' to step into the sliver of low sun caught <vocabulary form="間">between</vocabulary> the two doors: 「<reading>あいだ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業の間、静かに座っていました。
example_sentences.english: I sat quietly during class.
example_sentences.furigana: 授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]の間[あいだ]、静[しず]かに座[すわ]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達を待っている間に、コーヒーを飲みました。
example_sentences.english: While I was waiting for my friend, I drank some coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]を待[ま]っている間[あいだ]に、コーヒーを飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 朝と晩の間に、宿題をしました。
example_sentences.english: I did my homework sometime between morning and evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]と晩[ばん]の間[あいだ]に、宿[しゅく]題[だい]をしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 近（ちか）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>near</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>nearby</vocabulary> word are the same, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 近 is 「ちか」 from 近い, so <vocabulary>nearby</vocabulary> is <reading>ちかく</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の近くに図書館があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a library near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くに図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家はこの近くです。
example_sentences.english: My house is near here.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の家[いえ]はこの近[ちか]くです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は公園の近くに住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: He lives near the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は公[こう]園[えん]の近[ちか]くに住[す]んでいます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 後（うし）＋ろ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: This word is just the <kanji>behind</kanji> kanji you already know, so <vocabulary>behind</vocabulary> is exactly what it means.
items.reading_mnemonic: '<reading>Ooh, she rowed</reading>!' cry the fans as a duck paddles hard with a tiny thread caught on her trailing foot, yet that foot still lands a beat <vocabulary form="後ろ">behind</vocabulary>: 「<reading>うしろ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 後ろに猫がいます。
example_sentences.english: There's a cat behind me.
example_sentences.furigana: 後[うし]ろに猫[ねこ]がいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私の後ろに立ちました。
example_sentences.english: He stood behind me.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]の後[うし]ろに立[た]ちました。

example_sentences.japanese: かばんは椅子の後ろにありました。
example_sentences.english: The bag was behind the chair.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんは椅[い]子[す]の後[うし]ろにありました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 前（まえ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>front</kanji> kanji standing on its own is the <vocabulary>front</vocabulary> word, meaning and all.
items.reading_mnemonic: Farmhand <reading>Mae</reading> crosses the moonlit yard and freezes right in <vocabulary form="前">front</vocabulary> of the cow guarding its dropped knife, whispering her own name, 「<reading>まえ</reading>」, to calm it.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前でともだちを待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for my friend in front of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]でともだちを待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 食事の前に手を洗います。
example_sentences.english: I wash my hands before meals.
example_sentences.furigana: 食[しょく]事[じ]の前[まえ]に手[て]を洗[あら]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 三日前、私はこの町に来ました。
example_sentences.english: Three days ago, I came to this town.
example_sentences.furigana: 三[みっ]日[か]前[まえ]、私[わたし]はこの町[まち]に来[き]ました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 中（なか）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Written alone, the <kanji>inside</kanji> kanji is simply the word for <vocabulary>inside</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shove the stick through the wide mouth until it stops dead in the <vocabulary form="中">middle</vocabulary>, then <reading>knock a</reading> knuckle on it, and whatever is pinned in there squeaks 「<reading>なか</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 箱の中に猫がいます。
example_sentences.english: There's a cat inside the box.
example_sentences.furigana: 箱[はこ]の中[なか]に猫[ねこ]がいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋の中は暗かったです。
example_sentences.english: The inside of the room was dark.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]の中[なか]は暗[くら]かったです。

example_sentences.japanese: かばんの中に財布がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a wallet inside the bag.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんの中[なか]に財[さい]布[ふ]がありました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 上（うえ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Standing by itself, the <kanji>up</kanji> kanji is just the <vocabulary>up</vocabulary> word, nothing added.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the mossy shrine steps, a monk follows the tortoise's crack from the ground line and gasps '<reading>ooh, eh?</reading>' at where it points: 「<reading>うえ</reading>」, straight <vocabulary form="上">up</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 本は机の上にあります。
example_sentences.english: The book is on the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 本[ほん]は机[つくえ]の上[うえ]にあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫は木の上にいます。
example_sentences.english: The cat is up in the tree.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]は木[き]の上[うえ]にいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上は寒いです。
example_sentences.english: It's cold at the top of the mountain.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の上[うえ]は寒[さむ]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 下（した）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: This is just the <kanji>down</kanji> kanji you have met, used on its own as the word <vocabulary>down</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Under the ground line, a <reading>cheetah</reading> crouches in the dark and bats at the divination mark dangling <vocabulary form="下">down</vocabulary> to it, purring 「<reading>した</reading>」 since nobody above ever reads it.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫はテーブルの下で寝ています。
example_sentences.english: The cat is sleeping under the table.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]はテーブルの下[した]で寝[ね]ています。

example_sentences.japanese: 財布を椅子の下で見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I found my wallet under the chair.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]を椅[い]子[す]の下[した]で見[み]つけました。

example_sentences.japanese: 山の下に川があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a river below the mountain.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の下[した]に川[かわ]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 半（はん）＋分（ぶん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>half</kanji> only counts as a real <vocabulary>half</vocabulary> once it is also a clean <kanji>part</kanji> you can lift away and hand to someone.

example_sentences.japanese: パンの半分を食べました。
example_sentences.english: I ate half of the bread.
example_sentences.furigana: パンの半[はん]分[ぶん]を食[た]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: 半分は私の物です。
example_sentences.english: Half of it is mine.
example_sentences.furigana: 半[はん]分[ぶん]は私[わたし]の物[もの]です。

example_sentences.japanese: お金の半分を弟にあげました。
example_sentences.english: I gave half the money to my younger brother.
example_sentences.furigana: お金[かね]の半[はん]分[ぶん]を弟[おとうと]にあげました。

items.word_type: な adjective, adverb, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A kid at the crossing counts cab after cab and loses count; "that's <reading>taxi, son</reading>," his grandfather says, meaning <reading>たくさん</reading>, <vocabulary>a lot</vocabulary>. Before the noun it describes, it takes な.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は本をたくさん買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a lot of books.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は本[ほん]をたくさん買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園に猫がたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of cats in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]に猫[ねこ]がたくさんいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は宿題がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There's a lot of homework today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は宿[しゅく]題[だい]がたくさんあります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 少（すこ）＋し.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>few</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>a little</vocabulary> word are the same character wearing a kana tail, so they point at the same small amount.
items.reading_mnemonic: After one slash through the small bundle of matchsticks, the cook has only a <reading>skosh</reading> left, 「<reading>すこし</reading>」, just <vocabulary form="少し">a little</vocabulary> to light the stove.

example_sentences.japanese: 水を少し飲みました。
example_sentences.english: I drank a little water.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[みず]を少[すこ]し飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーは少し熱いです。
example_sentences.english: This coffee is a little hot.
example_sentences.furigana: このコーヒーは少[すこ]し熱[あつ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 少し休みます。
example_sentences.english: I'll rest a little.
example_sentences.furigana: 少[すこ]し休[やす]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Koichi's till you ask for a <reading>shot of</reading> milk in your coffee and get <vocabulary>a little</vocabulary> splash, barely enough to cloud it. That thin splash is <reading>ちょっと</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと待って。
example_sentences.english: Wait a second.
example_sentences.furigana: ちょっと待[ま]って。

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーはちょっと熱いです。
example_sentences.english: This coffee is a bit hot.
example_sentences.furigana: このコーヒーはちょっと熱[あつ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はちょっと忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm a little busy today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]はちょっと忙[いそが]しいです。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 別（べつ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Twins show up in the exact same coat. The teacher makes them hang the coats on <vocabulary>separate</vocabulary> hooks so nobody mixes them up.

example_sentences.japanese: これは別の本です。
example_sentences.english: This is a different book.
example_sentences.furigana: これは別[べつ]の本[ほん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 別の店で靴を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought shoes at a different shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 別[べつ]の店[みせ]で靴[くつ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の部屋は別です。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother's room is separate.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の部屋[へや]は別[べつ]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 病（びょう）＋気（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>ill</kanji> body is one whose <kanji>spirit</kanji> got bumped down to third class. That drop is what an <vocabulary>illness</vocabulary> is.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は病気で病院にいます。

example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は病[びょう]気[き]で病[びょう]院[いん]にいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は病気で仕事を休みました。
example_sentences.english: He was sick, so he took the day off work.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は病[びょう]気[き]で仕[し]事[ごと]を休[やす]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 病気の人は医者に会います。
example_sentences.english: A sick person goes to see a doctor.
example_sentences.furigana: 病[びょう]気[き]の人[ひと]は医[い]者[しゃ]に会[あ]います。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — かぜ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 風邪.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>wind</kanji> strong enough to flick a bug off the picnic table turns <kanji>wicked</kanji> and slips down your collar. The chill it leaves behind is a <vocabulary>cold</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the picnic table Grandma Kane sneezes and names the wicked wind that slipped down her collar as the <reading>cause</reading> of her <vocabulary form="風邪">cold</vocabulary>: 「<reading>かぜ</reading>」.
items.description: Identical in sound to the everyday word for wind, and written with that same first character, so only context tells the two apart.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は風邪で学校を休みました。
example_sentences.english: She was absent from school because of a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は風邪[かぜ]で学[がっ]校[こう]を休[やす]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪で頭が痛いです。
example_sentences.english: My head hurts because of a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]で頭[あたま]が痛[いた]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は風邪です。
example_sentences.english: My mother has a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は風邪[かぜ]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 薬（くすり）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>medicine</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>medicine</vocabulary> word are the same character with the same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: The herbalist gives your sore knee one <reading>cursory</reading> glance, then brews grass until it hums its gentle music and hands you 「<reading>くすり</reading>」, the oldest <vocabulary form="薬">medicine</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝と晩に薬を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I take medicine in the morning and at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]と晩[ばん]に薬[くすり]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 薬を病院でもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got the medicine at the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 薬[くすり]を病[びょう]院[いん]でもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 薬をかばんに入れました。
