example_sentences.furigana: 薬[くすり]をかばんに入[い]れました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 電（でん）＋車（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Bolt a <kanji>vehicle</kanji> onto the <kanji>electricity</kanji> humming through the overhead wires and it rolls down the rails as a <vocabulary>train</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝電車で学校へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to school by train every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]電[でん]車[しゃ]で学[がっ]校[こう]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で電車を待ちました。
example_sentences.english: I waited for the train at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で電[でん]車[しゃ]を待[ま]ちました。

example_sentences.japanese: その電車はとても速いです。
example_sentences.english: That train is very fast.
example_sentences.furigana: その電[でん]車[しゃ]はとても速[はや]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 車（くるま）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>car</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>car</vocabulary> word are the same single character, meaning the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Seen from above, a little cart with a box body and bar wheels <reading>caroms</reading> off the curb, and its driver checks the bent axle, muttering 「<reading>くるま</reading>」 over his battered <vocabulary form="車">car</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は新しい車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new car.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は新[あたら]しい車[くるま]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の車は駅の近くにあります。
example_sentences.english: His car is near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の車[くるま]は駅[えき]の近[ちか]くにあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 車の中に犬がいます。
example_sentences.english: There is a dog inside the car.
example_sentences.furigana: 車[くるま]の中[なか]に犬[いぬ]がいます。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 回（かい）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Push a revolving door and count each full circle it carries you through before you step out. Every completed circle around is one <vocabulary>times (counter)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝三回犬と歩きます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning I walk with my dog three times.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]三[さん]回[かい]犬[けん]と歩[ある]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は二回コーヒーを飲みました。
example_sentences.english: Today I drank coffee twice.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は二[に]回[かい]コーヒーを飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に一回電話しました。
example_sentences.english: I called him once.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]に一[いっ]回[かい]電[でん]話[わ]しました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 個（こ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Tip a jar of buttons, beads and dice onto the table, then point at each <kanji>individual</kanji> one as you drop it back in. Anything small enough to pinch between two fingers is one <vocabulary>small objects (counter)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 卵を五個買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought five eggs.
example_sentences.furigana: 卵[たまご]を五[ご]個[こ]買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: パンを二個食べました。
example_sentences.english: I ate two pieces of bread.
example_sentences.furigana: パンを二[に]個[こ]食[た]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: かばんに卵が十個あります。
example_sentences.english: There are ten eggs in the bag.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんに卵[たまご]が十[じゅう]個[こ]あります。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 本（ほん）.
items.mnemonic_text: Count of long thin things: hon.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>book</kanji> is really a tree trunk pressed flat, and a trunk is the plainest long, straight thing there is. Stand pencils, bottles and roads next to it and you count each one as a <vocabulary>long objects (counter)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 傘を二本買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought two umbrellas.
example_sentences.furigana: 傘[かさ]を二[に]本[ほん]買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園に木が三本あります。
example_sentences.english: There are three trees in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]に木[き]が三[さん]本[ぼん]あります。

example_sentences.japanese: ペンを一本持っています。
example_sentences.english: I have one pen.
example_sentences.furigana: ペンを一[いっ]本[ぽん]持[も]っています。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 人（にん）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stand in a doorway and tap each <kanji>person</kanji> on the shoulder as they stride through on the two legs you already know. Every tap adds one more to your count of <vocabulary>people (counter)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族は四人です。
example_sentences.english: There are four people in my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]は四[よ]人[にん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と三人で公園に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went to the park with two friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と三[さん]人[にん]で公[こう]園[えん]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋に人が五人います。
example_sentences.english: There are five people in the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]に人[ひと]が五[ご]人[にん]います。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 台（だい）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A washing machine, a car, a printer are all heavy blocks that only run while squatting on their own <kanji>stand</kanji>. Count the bolted-down blocks in the room and you have that many <vocabulary>machines</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は車を二台持っています。
example_sentences.english: I have two cars.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は車[くるま]を二[に]台[だい]持[も]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋にテレビが三台あります。
example_sentences.english: There are three TVs in this room.
example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]にテレビが三[さん]台[だい]あります。

example_sentences.japanese: 会社にパソコンが何台ありますか。
example_sentences.english: How many computers are there at the company?
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]にパソコンが何[なに]台[だい]ありますか。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 番（ばん）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>turn</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>number</vocabulary> word are exactly the same character, so they carry the same meaning.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の番です。
example_sentences.english: It's my turn.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の番[ばん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの番ですよ。
example_sentences.english: It's your turn.
example_sentences.furigana: あなたの番[ばん]ですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: この電話は何番ですか。
example_sentences.english: What's this phone's number?
example_sentences.furigana: この電[でん]話[わ]は何[なん]番[ばん]ですか。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 年（ねん）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>year</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>year (counter)</vocabulary> word are exactly the same character, so they mean the same thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本語を三年勉強しました。
example_sentences.english: I studied Japanese for three years.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は日本[にほん]語[ご]を三[さん]年[ねん]勉[べん]強[きょう]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母はここに十年住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother has lived here for ten years.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]はここに十[じゅう]年[ねん]住[す]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は一年会社で働きました。
example_sentences.english: He worked at the company for one year.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は一[いち]年[ねん]会[かい]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]きました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 外（そと）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>outside</kanji> kanji by itself is the <vocabulary>outside</vocabulary> word, unchanged in meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shuffling <vocabulary form="外">outside</vocabulary> to catch the last evening sun, the divining tortoise stubs its toe on the step and grumbles '<reading>so, toe</reading>,' 「<reading>そと</reading>」, before reading its cracked shell.

example_sentences.japanese: 外は寒いです。
example_sentences.english: It's cold outside.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[そと]は寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬は外にいます。
example_sentences.english: The dog is outside.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]は外[そと]にいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 外で遊びましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's play outside.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[そと]で遊[あそ]びましょう。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 自（じ）＋分（ぶん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji>self</kanji> is the one <kanji>part</kanji> you can never hand off to someone else, which makes it entirely <vocabulary>oneself</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'll go myself.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]で行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の部屋で寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I sleep in my own room.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]の部屋[へや]で寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で本を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought the book myself.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]で本[ほん]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 早（はや）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>early</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>early</vocabulary> word are the very same character. The extra い on the end just makes it an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane sees the sun just ten finger-widths above the hills and is already calling <reading>hiya</reading> to the shrine cats. Being up that soon is <reading>はやい</reading>, which is <vocabulary form="早い">early</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝早く起きます。
example_sentences.english: I wake up early every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯は早いです。
example_sentences.english: Dinner is early.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]は早[はや]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日早く学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to school early tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]早[はや]く学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（ち）＋図（ず）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A drawing of the land: chizu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A drawing that presses the whole <kanji>ground</kanji> flat onto one sheet you can fold into a pocket is a <vocabulary>map</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 地図をかばんに入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put the map in my bag.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[ち]図[ず]をかばんに入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: この地図は古いです。
example_sentences.english: This map is old.
example_sentences.furigana: この地[ち]図[ず]は古[ふる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 地図で駅を見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I found the station on the map.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[ち]図[ず]で駅[えき]を見[み]つけました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 外（がい）＋国（こく）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Step <kanji>outside</kanji> the walled <kanji>country</kanji> that guards its one jewel, and any <kanji>person</kanji> you meet there is a <vocabulary>foreigner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は外国人です。
example_sentences.english: He is a foreigner.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人とお茶を飲みました。
example_sentences.english: I drank tea with a foreigner.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]とお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、公園で外国人に会いました。
example_sentences.english: Today I met a foreigner at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、公[こう]園[えん]で外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]に会[あ]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 外（がい）＋国（こく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every <kanji>country</kanji> is walls thrown up around the one jewel its people will not share. Any such enclosure <kanji>outside</kanji> your own is a <vocabulary>foreign country</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は外国に住みたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to live in a foreign country.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は外[がい]国[こく]に住[す]みたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は外国で日本語を教えました。
example_sentences.english: She taught Japanese in a foreign country.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は外[がい]国[こく]で日本[にほん]語[ご]を教[おし]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、外国へ旅行します。
example_sentences.english: Next year, I'll travel to a foreign country.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、外[がい]国[こく]へ旅[りょ]行[こう]します。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 意（い）＋味（み）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>idea</kanji> you can almost <kanji>taste</kanji> when a word is used just right is that word's <vocabulary>meaning</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題の意味が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand what this question means.
example_sentences.furigana: この問[もん]題[だい]の意[い]味[み]が分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: その意味を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me what that means.
example_sentences.furigana: その意[い]味[み]を教[おし]えてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 何の意味ですか。
example_sentences.english: What does that mean?
example_sentences.furigana: 何[なに]の意[い]味[み]ですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 子（こ）＋供（ども）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>child</kanji> you proudly <kanji>offer</kanji> up to the neighbors, freshly bathed and squirming, is simply your <vocabulary>child</vocabulary>.
items.description: Sometimes written partly in hiragana, since the second kanji once meant "servant."

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が公園で遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: A child plays in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]ぶ。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の子供は本を読む。
example_sentences.english: My child reads books.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の子[こ]供[ども]は本[ほん]を読[よ]む。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供と一緒に映画を見る。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with my child.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]る。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 空（そら）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>sky</kanji> kanji, the one you also met as 'empty', and the <vocabulary>sky</vocabulary> word are a single character doing both jobs, so one wide empty space overhead is all either of them means.
items.reading_mnemonic: The digging crew punches clean through the roof of the empty hollow in the hill, looks up at the endless blue <vocabulary form="空">sky</vocabulary>, and cheers 「<reading>そら</reading>」, <reading>so, rah</reading>!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の空はいい。
example_sentences.english: Today's sky looks nice.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]の空[そら]はいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から空を見る。
example_sentences.english: I look at the sky from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から空[そら]を見[み]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 空から雨が来る。
example_sentences.english: Rain comes from the sky.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[そら]から雨[あめ]が来[く]る。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 服（ふく）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A coat is fabric that has agreed to <kanji>obey</kanji> your body. It bends when your elbow bends, never argues, and a closet full of that obedient cloth is your <vocabulary>clothes</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この服は高いです。
example_sentences.english: These clothes are expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: この服[ふく]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで服を買います。
example_sentences.english: I'm buying clothes at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートで服[ふく]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、友達と服を見ます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'll look at clothes with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、友[とも]達[だち]と服[ふく]を見[み]ます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 面（おも）＋白（しろ）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A white-bright face of fun: omoshiroi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A clown's <kanji>mask</kanji>, painted flat <kanji>white</kanji>, is the thing the whole room turns to watch. Whatever pulls every eye in a room like that is <vocabulary>interesting / funny</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は面白いです。
example_sentences.english: This book is interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は面[おも]白[しろ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の映画は面白かった。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday's movie was interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]の映[えい]画[が]は面白[おもしろ]かった。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は面白い人です。
example_sentences.english: She's an interesting person.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は面[おも]白[しろ]い人[ひと]です。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — とけい cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 時計.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Back when the village told the <kanji>time</kanji> by the sun on the temple roof, someone built a pocket machine to <kanji>plot</kanji> the hours instead. That gadget is a <vocabulary>clock / watch</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>tokay</reading> gecko on the temple roof barks the hours as the sun moves, until the village trades it for a pocket <vocabulary form="時計">watch</vocabulary> and still calls that 「<reading>とけい</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は時計を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the clock.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は時計[とけい]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: この時計は高いです。
example_sentences.english: This watch is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: この時計[とけい]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 店で時計を買います。
example_sentences.english: I buy a watch at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[みせ]で時計[とけい]を買[か]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋便（べん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stick the <kanji>negative</kanji> prefix onto any <kanji>convenience</kanji> and what is left standing is <vocabulary>inconvenient</vocabulary>. It works as a な adjective, so な lands before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は不便です。
example_sentences.english: This town is inconvenient.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]は不[ふ]便[べん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: バスがなくて不便です。
example_sentences.english: It's inconvenient without a bus.
example_sentences.furigana: バスがなくて不[ふ]便[べん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅から遠い家は不便です。
example_sentences.english: A house far from the station is inconvenient.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]から遠[とお]い家[いえ]は不[ふ]便[べん]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 映（えい）＋画（が）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stack up a pile of <kanji>pictures</kanji> and <kanji>reflect</kanji> them onto a white wall one after another, fast. The moving image on the wall is a <vocabulary>movie</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は映画が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like movies.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は映[えい]画[が]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、友達と映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'll watch a movie with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、友[とも]達[だち]と映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: その映画は面白かったです。
example_sentences.english: That movie was interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: その映[えい]画[が]は面白[おもしろ]かったです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 星（ほし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every night the sky quietly sets out thousands of tiny lamps and never sends anyone the bill. Each cold pinprick of light hanging up there is a <vocabulary>star</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Each night a lamplighter climbs up to light the sky's thousands of tiny lamps. Asked if the sky ever sends a bill, he chuckles <reading>ho, she</reading> never does, <reading>ほし</reading>, and lights one more <vocabulary form="星">star</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から星を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the stars from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から星[ほし]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は星の本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: She reads a book about stars.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は星[ほし]の本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の夜、星を見に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow night I'll go see the stars.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の夜[よる]、星[ほし]を見[み]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 速（はや）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You blink at the riverbank and the paper boat that was at your feet is already a speck under the far bridge. Nothing that beats your own eyelids is anything but <vocabulary>fast</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A surfer paddles up the riverbank swearing she left <reading>Hawaii</reading> straight after breakfast this morning. Crossing an ocean before lunch is about as <reading>はやい</reading> as it gets, which is plain <vocabulary>fast</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このバスは速いです。
example_sentences.english: This bus is fast.
example_sentences.furigana: このバスは速[はや]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は話すのが速い。
example_sentences.english: She speaks quickly.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は話[はな]すのが速[はや]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は食べるのが速い。
example_sentences.english: My little brother eats fast.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は食[た]べるのが速[はや]い。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — へや cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 部屋.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Wall off one <kanji>section</kanji> of the <kanji>house</kanji>, hang a door on it, and that boxed-in piece is a <vocabulary>room</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane throws open a door at the shrine and barks 「<reading>へや</reading>」 at the cats hiding inside, which is just <reading>hey, you</reading> aimed at whoever will not come out of that <vocabulary>room</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は寒いです。
example_sentences.english: This room is cold.
example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]は寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I read a book in the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の部屋に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to my friend's room.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の部屋[へや]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 全（ぜん）＋部（ぶ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull together every single <kanji>section</kanji> of a thing, skip none, and what is left in your hands is the <vocabulary>whole</vocabulary> of it.

example_sentences.japanese: この本を全部読みました。
example_sentences.english: I read this whole book.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]読[よ]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: お金を全部使いました。
example_sentences.english: I used up all my money.
example_sentences.furigana: お金[かね]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]使[つか]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 全部おいしかったです。
example_sentences.english: Everything was delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: 全[ぜん]部[ぶ]おいしかったです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 自（じ）＋転（てん）＋車（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>car</kanji> with no engine leaves the pedalling to you. Your own legs make the wheels <kanji>revolve</kanji>, so the whole thing is <kanji>self</kanji>-propelled, which is what a <vocabulary>bicycle</vocabulary> is.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日自転車で学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to school by bicycle every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]で学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は新しい自転車が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother wants a new bicycle.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は新[あたら]しい自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]が欲[ほ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園に自転車がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of bicycles at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]に自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]がたくさんあります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 強（つよ）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the school sports day, one first-year on the tug-of-war rope drags the entire opposing team over the line by herself. Being able to move people who refuse to move is <vocabulary>strong</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A swamped rowboat slides off down the river until Sue wades in and drags it up the bank alone, the ferryman shouting <reading>'Sue, oi'</reading> after her. Hauling a full boat against the current is <reading>つよい</reading>, plain <vocabulary>strong</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は風が強いです。
example_sentences.english: The wind is strong today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は風[かぜ]が強[つよ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私より強いです。
example_sentences.english: He's stronger than me.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]より強[つよ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーは強いです。
example_sentences.english: This coffee is strong.
example_sentences.furigana: このコーヒーは強[つよ]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 勉（べん）＋強（きょう）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Force yourself to learn: benkyou suru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <vocabulary>study</vocabulary> is <kanji>exertion</kanji> made <kanji>strong</kanji> and held for hours on end. You keep wringing the same sweatband out over one textbook until the pages go limp.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日図書館で勉強する。
example_sentences.english: I study at the library every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で勉[べん]強[きょう]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜に家で勉強する。
example_sentences.english: I study at home at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]に家[いえ]で勉[べん]強[きょう]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟と一緒に勉強する。
example_sentences.english: I study together with my little brother.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に勉[べん]強[きょう]する。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 勉（べん）＋強（きょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pour in enough <kanji>exertion</kanji> to build a <kanji>strong</kanji> hold on a subject, sweatband wrung dry, and that grind is <vocabulary>study</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強は難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Studying is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 勉[べん]強[きょう]は難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝勉強をします。
example_sentences.english: I study every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]勉[べん]強[きょう]をします。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は勉強が好きです。
example_sentences.english: She likes studying.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は勉[べん]強[きょう]が好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 図（と）＋書（しょ）＋館（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pack a <kanji>building</kanji> with every <kanji>map</kanji> ever folded and everything a brush could <kanji>write</kanji>, and you have a <vocabulary>library</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the library?
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日図書館に行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to the library every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]に行[い]く。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と図書館で本を読む。
example_sentences.english: I read books at the library with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]む。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 映（えい）＋画（が）＋館（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The hall of moving pictures: eigakan.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Koichi rigs his konbini so the back wall <kanji>projects</kanji> a giant moving <kanji>picture</kanji>; once the whole <kanji>building</kanji> exists only to show that picture, he has opened a <vocabulary>cinema</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、映画館に行きます。
example_sentences.english: This weekend I'm going to the cinema.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、映[えい]画[が]館[かん]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館で映画を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I watched a movie at the cinema.
example_sentences.furigana: 映[えい]画[が]館[かん]で映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: この映画館は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This cinema is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この映[えい]画[が]館[かん]は安[やす]いです。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 月（がつ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>month</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>month</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so they mean the same thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は三月に日本へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to Japan in March.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は三[さん]月[がつ]に日本[にほん]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 来月は八月です。
example_sentences.english: Next month is August.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]は八[はち]月[がつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の十二月は忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: This December is busy.
example_sentences.furigana: 今年[ことし]の十[じゅう]二[に]月[がつ]は忙[いそが]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — かげつ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of ヶ月.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That small <kanji>month</kanji> kanji riding on the end is the whole word, so ticking these off just counts <vocabulary>months</vocabulary> of elapsed time.
items.reading_mnemonic: A heavy <reading>cargo jet</reading> grinds across the sky so slowly that one lap of its route eats a whole month. Count enough laps and the number you reach is how many <vocabulary>months</vocabulary> have gone by; every slow pass sounds like 「<reading>かげつ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は三ヶ月、日本語を勉強しました。
example_sentences.english: I studied Japanese for three months.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は三[さん]ヶ[か]月[げつ]、日本[にほん]語[ご]を勉[べん]強[きょう]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は一ヶ月、病気で休んでいます。
example_sentences.english: He has been on sick leave for a month.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は一[いっ]ヶ[か]月[げつ]、病[びょう]気[き]で休[やす]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは二ヶ月前にその家を買いました。
example_sentences.english: We bought that house two months ago.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは二[に]ヶ[か]月[げつ]前[まえ]にその家[いえ]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 日（にち）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>day</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>day (counter)</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so they mean the same thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 一年は三百六十五日です。
example_sentences.english: A year has three hundred sixty-five days.
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いち]年[ねん]は三[さん]百[びゃく]六[ろく]十[じゅう]五[ご]日[にち]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 今月は三十日です。
example_sentences.english: This month has thirty days.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[こん]月[げつ]は三[さん]十[じゅう]日[にち]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 二月は二十八日まであります。
example_sentences.english: February runs through the 28th.
example_sentences.furigana: 二[に]月[がつ]は二[に]十[じゅう]八[よう]日[か]まであります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 週（しゅう）＋間（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lay the <kanji>week</kanji> blocks end to end, leaving no blank calendar in the <kanji>interval</kanji> between them. That unbroken run is how many <vocabulary>weeks</vocabulary> long the stretch lasts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は一週間会社を休みました。
example_sentences.english: He took a week off from work.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]会[かい]社[しゃ]を休[やす]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は二週間旅行します。
example_sentences.english: I'm traveling for two weeks.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は二[に]週[しゅう]間[かん]旅[りょ]行[こう]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は三週間で日本語が分かるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: She came to understand Japanese in three weeks.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は三[さん]週[しゅう]間[かん]で日本[にほん]語[ご]が分[わ]かるようになりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 時（じ）＋間（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Measure everything that sits <kanji>between</kanji> one clock <kanji>time</kanji> and the next one. Stack those measured spans up and the total is so many <vocabulary>hours</vocabulary> of duration.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、勉強の時間があります。
example_sentences.english: I have time to study every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]、勉[べん]強[きょう]の時[じ]間[かん]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 授業の時間は九十分です。
example_sentences.english: Class time is ninety minutes.
example_sentences.furigana: 授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]の時[じ]間[かん]は九[きゅう]十[じゅう]分[ふん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 待つ時間が長いです。
example_sentences.english: The waiting time is long.
example_sentences.furigana: 待[ま]つ時[じ]間[かん]が長[なが]いです。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 時（じ）.
items.mnemonic_text: The hour on the clock: ji.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stop the <kanji>hour</kanji> hand dead on one mark of the dial and say the number it points at out loud. That spoken-aloud hour is what <vocabulary>o'clock</vocabulary> names.

example_sentences.japanese: 今何時ですか。
example_sentences.english: What time is it now?
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]何[なん]時[じ]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 授業は九時に始まります。
example_sentences.english: Class starts at nine o'clock.
example_sentences.furigana: 授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]は九[く]時[じ]に始[はじ]まります。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は七時に起きました。
example_sentences.english: I woke up at seven o'clock.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は七[しち]時[じ]に起[お]きました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 分（ふん）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>minute</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>minutes</vocabulary> counter are the very same character, so they mean the same thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議は三十分ぐらいでした。
example_sentences.english: The meeting was about thirty minutes long.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]は三[さん]十[じゅう]分[ふん]ぐらいでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 五分待ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please wait five minutes.
example_sentences.furigana: 五[ご]分[ふん]待[ま]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅まで五分歩きました。
example_sentences.english: I walked five minutes to the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]まで五[ご]分[ふん]歩[ある]きました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 上（あ）＋がる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>up</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>to go up</vocabulary> verb point the same way. The trailing kana just turn it into a verb where the thing rises on its own, with nobody lifting it.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the mossy shrine steps, <reading>a guru</reading> watches the tortoise's crack climb from the ground line on its own and whispers 「<reading>あがる</reading>」: no hand lifts it, yet it starts <vocabulary form="上がる">to rise</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、二階に上がって窓を開けます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning I go up to the second floor and open the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]、二[に]階[かい]に上[あ]がって窓[まど]を開[あ]けます。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が上がったら、公園を歩きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Once the rain stops, let's walk in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が上[あ]がったら、公[こう]園[えん]を歩[ある]きましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 家に上がる前に靴を脱ぎます。
example_sentences.english: I take off my shoes before entering the house.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]に上[あ]がる前[まえ]に靴[くつ]を脱[ぬ]ぎます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 下（さ）＋がる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>down</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>to go down</vocabulary> verb are one and the same direction. With the trailing kana it becomes the verb for that drop happening by itself, with no hand on it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Under the ground line the tortoise's divination mark droops lower by itself, like a sagging <reading>saguaro</reading> arm, and with a dry 「<reading>さがる</reading>」 it starts to <vocabulary form="下がる">go down</vocabulary> into the dark.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機が下がりました。
example_sentences.english: The airplane descended.
example_sentences.furigana: 飛[ひ]行[こう]機[き]が下[さ]がりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 声が少し下がりました。
example_sentences.english: The voice dropped a little.
example_sentences.furigana: 声[こえ]が少[すこ]し下[さ]がりました。

example_sentences.japanese: パンが百円に下がりました。
example_sentences.english: The bread's price dropped to 100 yen.
example_sentences.furigana: パンが百[ひゃく]円[えん]に下[さ]がりました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 上（あ）＋げる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Get both hands under a crate and shove it <kanji>up</kanji> until it rests higher than it began. Doing that on purpose to some object is to <vocabulary>raise</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 上 is read 「あ」 from 上がる, so <vocabulary>to raise</vocabulary> is simply <reading>あげる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は手を上げました。
example_sentences.english: I raised my hand.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は手[て]を上[あ]げました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は顔を上げました。
example_sentences.english: He looked up.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は顔[かお]を上[あ]げました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は声を上げました。
example_sentences.english: She raised her voice.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は声[こえ]を上[あ]げました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 下（お）＋ろす.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>down</kanji> kanji sits right inside <vocabulary>to lower</vocabulary>, the same downward move. The trailing kana add a pair of hands, so you take hold of a real object and bring it down yourself.
items.reading_mnemonic: Wally the <reading>walrus</reading> grips the tortoise's dangling divination mark in both flippers and, grunting 「<reading>おろす</reading>」, brings it down below the ground line himself, which is to <vocabulary form="下ろす">lower</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 机の上から本を下ろしました。
example_sentences.english: I took the book down from on top of the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]から本[ほん]を下[お]ろしました。

example_sentences.japanese: かばんを椅子の下に下ろしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put your bag down under the chair.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんを椅[い]子[す]の下[した]に下[お]ろしてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は荷物を車から下ろしました。
example_sentences.english: My father took the luggage down from the car.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は荷[に]物[もつ]を車[くるま]から下[お]ろしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 落（お）＋ちる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A ripe chestnut lets go of its branch above the mountain trail. It <vocabulary>falls</vocabulary> to the path on its own, with no hand anywhere near it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Under the chestnut tree on the mountain trail, a hiker hears one ripe nut let go and calls <reading>oh, cheerio</reading>, 「<reading>おちる</reading>」, as it is left to <vocabulary form="落ちる">fall</vocabulary> on its own.

example_sentences.japanese: 机から鉛筆が落ちました。
example_sentences.english: The pencil fell off the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 机[つくえ]から鉛[えん]筆[ぴつ]が落[お]ちました。

example_sentences.japanese: 秋に木から葉が落ちます。
example_sentences.english: In autumn, leaves fall from the trees.
example_sentences.furigana: 秋[あき]に木[き]から葉[は]が落[お]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 財布がかばんから落ちましたよ。
example_sentences.english: Your wallet fell out of your bag.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]がかばんから落[お]ちましたよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 落（お）＋とす.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You fumble your phone above the konbini counter and your fingers open. A hand let it go, so when you <vocabulary>drop</vocabulary> a thing, the fault is yours.
items.reading_mnemonic: You met this reading of 落 back in 落ちる, so when a hand is what lets the thing go, <vocabulary>to drop</vocabulary> it is <reading>おとす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は財布を落としました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped my wallet.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は財[さい]布[ふ]を落[お]としました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はかばんを駅で落としました。
example_sentences.english: She dropped her bag at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はかばんを駅[えき]で落[お]としました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は傘を公園で落としました。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother dropped his umbrella at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は傘[かさ]を公[こう]園[えん]で落[お]としました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 渡（わた）＋す.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>ferry</kanji> the parcel across the last stretch of counter. Passing it into the customer's open hands is to <vocabulary>hand it over</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 渡 from 渡る, where it means getting across, so passing a thing all the way into another hand, <vocabulary>to hand over</vocabulary>, is <reading>わたす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼に本を渡します。
example_sentences.english: I hand him a book.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は彼[かれ]に本[ほん]を渡[わた]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は毎朝私に弁当を渡します。
example_sentences.english: My mother hands me a boxed lunch every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]私[わたし]に弁[べん]当[とう]を渡[わた]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は駅員に切符を渡した。
example_sentences.english: She handed her ticket to the station staff.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は駅[えき]員[いん]に切[きっ]符[ぷ]を渡[わた]した。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 遅（おく）＋れる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The last train slides out of the station without you. Slipping behind the clock, with only your slow feet to blame, is to <vocabulary>be late</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei reaches the platform with a bag of <reading>okra</reading> just as the last train slides out, 「<reading>おくれる</reading>」. Missing it because of slow feet is to be <vocabulary form="遅れる">late</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、学校に遅れました。
example_sentences.english: I was late for school today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、学[がっ]校[こう]に遅[おく]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも会議に遅れる。
example_sentences.english: He is always late for meetings.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はいつも会[かい]議[ぎ]に遅[おく]れる。

example_sentences.japanese: バスが遅れて、駅で待ちました。
example_sentences.english: The bus was late, so I waited at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: バスが遅[おく]れて、駅[えき]で待[ま]ちました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 手（て）＋伝（つだ）＋う.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You put your own <kanji>hand</kanji> to someone else's job. Staying to <kanji>go along</kanji> with their work until it is done is to <vocabulary>help</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は忙しいので、私は料理を手伝いました。
example_sentences.english: My mother was busy, so I helped with the cooking.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は忙[いそが]しいので、私[わたし]は料[りょう]理[り]を手伝[てつだ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の宿題を手伝ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please help my younger brother with his homework.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の宿[しゅく]題[だい]を手伝[てつだ]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が掃除を手伝ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: My friend helped me clean.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]が掃[そう]除[じ]を手伝[てつだ]ってくれました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 無（な）＋くなる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You reach for the sugar and find the jar emptied to <kanji>nothingness</kanji> on its own. When the last of a thing quietly hits zero, it has <vocabulary>run out</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already learned this reading of 無 from 無くす, so a thing fading out of the world by itself, <vocabulary>to disappear</vocabulary>, is <reading>なくなる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布の中のお金が無くなりました。
example_sentences.english: The money in my wallet ran out.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]の中[なか]のお金[かね]が無[な]くなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 家の卵が無くなりました。
example_sentences.english: The eggs at home ran out.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]の卵[たまご]が無[な]くなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 机の上の鉛筆が無くなりました。
example_sentences.english: The pencil on the desk disappeared.
example_sentences.furigana: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]の鉛[えん]筆[ぴつ]が無[な]くなりました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 変（か）＋わる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A chameleon crosses a warm rock and drifts from green to brown, with nothing done to it. Turning into a new version of itself on its own is to <vocabulary>change</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A shy octopus at the riverbank seems to <reading>cower</reading> and shift colour every few seconds without deciding to, 「<reading>かわる</reading>」, and going from one state to another on its own is to <vocabulary>change</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気がよく変わります。
example_sentences.english: The weather changes a lot.
example_sentences.furigana: 天[てん]気[き]がよく変[か]わります。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は変わりました。
example_sentences.english: He has changed.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は変[か]わりました。

example_sentences.japanese: この町は変わりましたね。
example_sentences.english: This town has changed, hasn't it?
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]は変[か]わりましたね。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 変（か）＋える.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You swap the batteries, reset the clock, repaint the door. Making a thing become different by your own hand is to <vocabulary>change</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this reading of 変 from 変わる, so when it is your hand doing it, <vocabulary>to change</vocabulary> something, the word is <reading>かえる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は仕事を変えます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to change jobs.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は仕[し]事[ごと]を変[か]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋の色を変えました。
example_sentences.english: I changed the color of the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]の色[いろ]を変[か]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: 名前を変えてもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Is it okay to change my name?
example_sentences.furigana: 名[な]前[まえ]を変[か]えてもいいですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 降（ふ）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The grey sky over the mountain trail lets down a steady curtain onto every leaf, with nobody pouring it. Water coming out of the clouds like that is what it means to <vocabulary>fall</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hiker on the mountain trail pulls up her <reading>fur</reading> hood as the grey sky lets a steady curtain down onto every leaf, 「<reading>ふる</reading>」, water starting to <vocabulary form="降る">fall</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日雨が降ります。
example_sentences.english: It will rain tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 今雪が降っています。
example_sentences.english: It's snowing right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は雨が降りませんでした。
example_sentences.english: It didn't rain yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 動（うご）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>move</kanji> kanji and the word <vocabulary>to move</vocabulary> are the same character, so the meaning carries over. The trailing kana mark the intransitive one: the thing shifts on its own, with nobody pushing it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei leans on a stalled merry-go-round, mutters <reading>you go, cuckoo</reading>, and it lurches into a slow spin on its own, 「<reading>うごく</reading>」, that first shift from dead still being what it means to <vocabulary>move</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この時計は動きません。
example_sentences.english: This clock doesn't move.
example_sentences.furigana: この時計[とけい]は動[うご]きません。

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が動きました。
example_sentences.english: The train started moving.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]車[しゃ]が動[うご]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がベッドの上で動いています。
example_sentences.english: The cat is moving around on the bed.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]がベッドの上[うえ]で動[うご]いています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 動（うご）＋かす.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>move</kanji> kanji and the word <vocabulary>to move</vocabulary> are the same character, meaning unchanged. The かす ending makes it the transitive one: you are the one shoving something else into motion.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this reading of 動 from 動く, so when you are the one making something else move, <vocabulary>to move</vocabulary> it, the word is <reading>うごかす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達がテーブルを動かしました。
example_sentences.english: My friend moved the table.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]がテーブルを動[うご]かしました。

example_sentences.japanese: この椅子を動かしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please move this chair.
example_sentences.furigana: この椅[い]子[す]を動[うご]かしてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 父が車を動かしました。
example_sentences.english: My father moved the car.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]が車[くるま]を動[うご]かしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 止（と）＋める.
items.mnemonic_text: Bring it to a halt: tomeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>stop</kanji> kanji and the word <vocabulary>to stop</vocabulary> are the same character, meaning unchanged. The trailing kana make it the transitive one: you bring something else to a halt, it does not halt itself.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this reading of 止 from 止まる, so when it is you bringing something else to a halt, <vocabulary>to stop</vocabulary> it is <reading>とめる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はタクシーを止めた。
example_sentences.english: He stopped a taxi.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はタクシーを止[と]めた。

example_sentences.japanese: ここに車を止めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop the car here.
example_sentences.furigana: ここに車[くるま]を止[と]めてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 父はお酒を止めるつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: My father intends to quit drinking.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]はお酒[さけ]を止[と]めるつもりだ。

items.word_type: する verb, intransitive verb, adverb
items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You lift the lid off a plain little lunch and a <reading>big curry</reading> the size of a car tyre is steaming there instead. You jump back hard, and that is what it is <vocabulary>to be surprised</vocabulary>, 「<reading>びっくりする</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい声を聞くと、びっくりする。
example_sentences.english: When I hear a loud voice, I get surprised.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[おお]きい声[こえ]を聞[き]くと、びっくりする。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が走ってきたら、びっくりすると思う。
example_sentences.english: I think I'll be startled if the dog comes running over.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]が走[はし]ってきたら、びっくりすると思[おも]う。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の声が大きいので、学生はびっくりする。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's voice is loud, so the students get surprised.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の声[こえ]が大[おお]きいので、学[がく]生[せい]はびっくりする。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 説（せつ）＋明（めい）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hold your <kanji>theory</kanji> up and keep rephrasing it until it goes <kanji>bright</kanji> in the other person's head. Making it light up like that is how you <vocabulary>explain</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は漢字を説明する人です。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is someone who explains kanji.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は漢[かん]字[じ]を説[せつ]明[めい]する人[ひと]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は道を説明するのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like explaining the way.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は道[みち]を説[せつ]明[めい]するのが好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: これを説明するのは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Explaining this is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: これを説[せつ]明[めい]するのは難[むずか]しいです。

items.word_type: する verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 運（うん）＋転（てん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Give the wheels that only <kanji>revolve</kanji> some real road to bite, and the spin finally <kanji>carries</kanji> the whole car forward. Sitting up front making that happen is what it means <vocabulary>to drive</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日車を運転する。
example_sentences.english: I drive a car every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]車[くるま]を運[うん]転[てん]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はバスを運転することができる。
example_sentences.english: She can drive a bus.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はバスを運[うん]転[てん]することができる。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は運転するのが上手だ。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is good at driving.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は運[うん]転[てん]するのが上手[じょうず]だ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 食（しょく）＋事（じ）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When <kanji>eating</kanji> stops being a quick bite standing up and turns into a sat-down, several-course <kanji>affair</kanji>, you <vocabulary>dine</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは家で食事する。
example_sentences.english: We eat at home.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは家[いえ]で食[しょく]事[じ]する。

example_sentences.japanese: レストランで食事するのは好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like eating at restaurants.
example_sentences.furigana: レストランで食[しょく]事[じ]するのは好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は毎晩レストランで食事する。
example_sentences.english: He eats at a restaurant every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]レストランで食[しょく]事[じ]する。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 仕（し）on'yomi ＋ 事（ごと）kun'yomi ＋ 場（ば）kun'yomi. Rendaku: 事 こと → ごと.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>place</kanji> you show up to each day to <kanji>attend</kanji> to the <kanji>business</kanji> that pays you, fetching and carrying until closing, is your <vocabulary>workplace</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の仕事場は駅の近くです。
example_sentences.english: My workplace is near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の仕[し]事[ごと]場[ば]は駅[えき]の近[ちか]くです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は仕事場でコーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: She drinks coffee at her workplace.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は仕[し]事[ごと]場[ば]でコーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、自転車で仕事場に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning I go to my workplace by bicycle.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]、自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]で仕[し]事[ごと]場[ば]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 夢（ゆめ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The film that runs behind your eyes while you sleep, so real you talk back to it, then gone the instant the alarm goes, is a <vocabulary>dream</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane bends over the sleeping cats on the shrine steps and whispers 「<reading>ゆめ</reading>」. <reading>You may</reading> fly, you may be rich, she means, but only until dawn, because none of it is real, it is just a <vocabulary>dream</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夢は医者です。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to become a doctor.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の夢[ゆめ]は医[い]者[しゃ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、面白い夢を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I had an interesting dream yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、面[おも]白[しろ]い夢[ゆめ]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの夢は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What's your dream?
example_sentences.furigana: あなたの夢[ゆめ]は何[なに]ですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — お＋釣（つ）＋り.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pay with a note that is far too big and the cashier lets you <kanji>angle</kanji> a fistful of coins back out of the deal. That catch is your <vocabulary>change (money)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi at the konbini takes your big note and pushes a heap of coins back across the beeping till. You walk out not <reading>utterly</reading> broke, that heap in your palm being your <vocabulary>change (money)</vocabulary>, 「<reading>おつり</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: お釣りを忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my change.
example_sentences.furigana: お釣[つ]りを忘[わす]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: これはお釣りです。
example_sentences.english: This is your change.
example_sentences.furigana: これはお釣[つ]りです。

example_sentences.japanese: お釣りは要りません。
example_sentences.english: I don't need the change.
example_sentences.furigana: お釣[つ]りは要[い]りません。

example_sentences.japanese: 店でお釣りをもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got change at the store.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[みせ]でお釣[つ]りをもらいました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 旅（りょ）＋館（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>building</kanji> that fills only with people partway through a <kanji>trip</kanji>, then empties again the morning they move on, is an <vocabulary>inn</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは旅館に泊まりました。
example_sentences.english: We stayed at the inn.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは旅[りょ]館[かん]に泊[と]まりました。

example_sentences.japanese: その旅館の部屋はきれいでした。
example_sentences.english: That inn's room was clean.
example_sentences.furigana: その旅[りょ]館[かん]の部屋[へや]はきれいでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館の人は親切でした。
example_sentences.english: The people at the inn were kind.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]館[かん]の人[ひと]は親[しん]切[せつ]でした。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A bellhop wheels his cart past a hundred identical numbered doors. Say the English word <reading>hotel</reading> in three flat, clipped beats and it comes out as 「<reading>ホテル</reading>」, the place you rent a bed for one night, a <vocabulary>hotel</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこのホテルに泊まります。
example_sentences.english: I'm staying at this hotel.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はこのホテルに泊[と]まります。

example_sentences.japanese: そのホテルはきれいですか。
example_sentences.english: Is that hotel clean?
example_sentences.furigana: そのホテルはきれいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの部屋は広いです。
example_sentences.english: The hotel room is spacious.
example_sentences.furigana: ホテルの部屋[へや]は広[ひろ]いです。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — へやばんごう cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 部屋番号.
items.furigana: 部屋[へや]番[ばん]号[ごう]
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>section</kanji> of a building under its own <kanji>roof</kanji>, plus that room's <kanji>number in a series</kanji>, gives you the <vocabulary>room number</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: In a building under one roof, a bingo caller reads each door's number in the series and yells <reading>hey-ya-bingo</reading> at yours, 「<reading>へやばんごう</reading>」, your <vocabulary form="部屋番号">room number</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋番号は五です。
example_sentences.english: My room number is 5.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]番[ばん]号[ごう]は五[ご]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの部屋番号を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me your room number.
example_sentences.furigana: あなたの部屋[へや]番[ばん]号[ごう]を教[おし]えてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋番号を忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot the room number.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]番[ばん]号[ごう]を忘[わす]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの部屋番号はどれですか。
example_sentences.english: Which one is the hotel room number?
example_sentences.furigana: ホテルの部屋[へや]番[ばん]号[ごう]はどれですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 住（じゅう）＋所（しょ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <vocabulary>address</vocabulary> is the named <kanji>place</kanji> where you <kanji>live</kanji>, spelled out house, street and town.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の住所を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write down my address.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の住[じゅう]所[しょ]を書[か]いてください。

example_sentences.japanese: これは彼の住所です。
example_sentences.english: This is his address.
example_sentences.furigana: これは彼[かれ]の住[じゅう]所[しょ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 住所と名前を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me your address and name.
example_sentences.furigana: 住[じゅう]所[しょ]と名[な]前[まえ]を教[おし]えてください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 番（ばん）＋号（ごう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take your <kanji>place in the series</kanji> and write it down as a digit, and that digit is your <vocabulary>number</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは私の電話番号です。
example_sentences.english: This is my phone number.
example_sentences.furigana: これは私[わたし]の電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の番号を忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot his number.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の番[ばん]号[ごう]を忘[わす]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 番号を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me the number.
example_sentences.furigana: 番[ばん]号[ごう]を教[おし]えてください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 電（でん）＋話（わ）＋番（ばん）＋号（ごう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>electricity</kanji> line carries your <kanji>talk</kanji> to one <kanji>number in a series</kanji> and nobody else. That string of digits is your <vocabulary>phone number</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは私の電話番号です。
example_sentences.english: This is my phone number.
example_sentences.furigana: これは私[わたし]の電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の電話番号を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me his phone number.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]を教[おし]えてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 電話番号を忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot the phone number.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]を忘[わす]れました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 都（つ）＋合（ごう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lay <kanji>all</kanji> of your commitments in a row and check whether a new plan will <kanji>fit</kanji> among them. How easily it fits is its <vocabulary>convenience</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は都合が悪いです。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow doesn't work for me.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は都[つ]合[ごう]が悪[わる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 土曜日の都合はどうですか。
example_sentences.english: How does Saturday work for you?
example_sentences.furigana: 土[ど]曜[よう]日[び]の都[つ]合[ごう]はどうですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の都合を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked the teacher about their availability.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の都[つ]合[ごう]を聞[き]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 理（り）＋由（ゆう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A toddler shoves a plant pot off the sill, meets your eyes, and plainly had a <vocabulary>reason</vocabulary>. You are never going to find out what it was.

example_sentences.japanese: 理由が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand the reason.
example_sentences.furigana: 理[り]由[ゆう]が分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れた理由を説明しました。
example_sentences.english: I explained the reason I was late.
example_sentences.furigana: 遅[おく]れた理[り]由[ゆう]を説[せつ]明[めい]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は理由も言わずに帰りました。
example_sentences.english: He went home without saying why.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は理[り]由[ゆう]も言[い]わずに帰[かえ]りました。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 気（き）on'yomi ＋ 持（も）kun'yomi ＋ ち.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>spirit</kanji> you happen to be <kanji>holding</kanji> onto at any given moment, good or bad, is your <vocabulary>feeling</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は気持ちがいい。
example_sentences.english: Today feels good.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は気[き]持[も]ちがいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の気持ちが分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand his feelings.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の気[き]持[も]ちが分[わ]からない。

example_sentences.japanese: 暖かいお茶を飲むと気持ちがいい。
example_sentences.english: Drinking warm tea feels nice.
example_sentences.furigana: 暖[あたた]かいお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]むと気[き]持[も]ちがいい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 気（き）＋分（ぶん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Check one <kanji>part</kanji> of the <kanji>spirit</kanji> you are running on today, and that single slice of it is your <vocabulary>mood</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は気分がいいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm in a good mood today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は気[き]分[ぶん]がいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は気分が悪いと言いました。
example_sentences.english: He said he felt sick.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は気[き]分[ぶん]が悪[わる]いと言[い]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩したら気分がよくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Taking a walk made me feel better.
example_sentences.furigana: 散[さん]歩[ぽ]したら気[き]分[ぶん]がよくなりました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 席（せき）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Grandma Kane's shrine has one dry step among twenty wet ones. Whoever loses the dawn scramble for it loses their <vocabulary>seat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の席はここです。
example_sentences.english: My seat is here.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の席[せき]はここです。

example_sentences.japanese: その席に座ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please sit in that seat.
example_sentences.furigana: その席[せき]に座[すわ]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: あの席に誰がいますか。
example_sentences.english: Who is in that seat over there?
example_sentences.furigana: あの席[せき]に誰[だれ]がいますか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 力（ちから）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>power</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>power</vocabulary> word are the exact same single character, so of course they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>chick</reading> flexes one tiny arm, elbow bent and muscle bulging, then lands a <reading>karate</reading> chop, 「<reading>ちから</reading>」, and you can feel the <vocabulary form="力">strength</vocabulary> straining in it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、力がありません。
example_sentences.english: I have no strength right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]、力[ちから]がありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は力が強いです。
example_sentences.english: He is very strong.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は力[ちから]が強[つよ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は力を使いました。
example_sentences.english: The child used their strength.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]は力[ちから]を使[つか]いました。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 火（か）on'yomi ＋ 曜（よう）on'yomi ＋ 日（び）kun'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Fire</kanji> catches on the next <kanji>weekday</kanji> <kanji>day</kanji> it can reach and burns straight through it, leaving <vocabulary>Tuesday</vocabulary> scorched.

example_sentences.japanese: 火曜日に映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I'll watch a movie on Tuesday.
example_sentences.furigana: 火[か]曜[よう]日[び]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は火曜日です。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow is Tuesday.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は火[か]曜[よう]日[び]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 来週の火曜日に友達と会います。
example_sentences.english: I'll meet a friend next Tuesday.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]週[しゅう]の火[か]曜[よう]日[び]に友[とも]達[だち]と会[あ]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — ご＋主（しゅ）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The master of the house: goshujin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>main</kanji> <kanji>person</kanji> running a household is what you call someone's <vocabulary>husband</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: ご主人は今日、忙しいですか。
example_sentences.english: Is your husband busy today?
example_sentences.furigana: ご主[しゅ]人[じん]は今日[きょう]、忙[いそが]しいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のご主人に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met her husband.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]のご主[しゅ]人[じん]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: ご主人と一緒にご飯を食べます。
example_sentences.english: We're having a meal with your husband.
example_sentences.furigana: ご主[しゅ]人[じん]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]にご飯[はん]を食[た]べます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 名（な）＋前（まえ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The evening hides your face, so your <kanji>name</kanji> is the one word you send out in <kanji>front</kanji> of you. A word carried ahead like that, so strangers know who just spoke, is your <vocabulary>name</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の名前はユキです。
example_sentences.english: My name is Yuki.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の名[な]前[まえ]はユキです。

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの名前は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What is your name?
example_sentences.furigana: あなたの名[な]前[まえ]は何[なに]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の名前を忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot his name.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の名[な]前[まえ]を忘[わす]れました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 耳（みみ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>ear</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>ear</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so they mean the very same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Seen from the side, the cat <reading>Mimi</reading> is all tall outer rim and folded lines, one huge <vocabulary form="耳">ear</vocabulary> that swivels whenever you whisper 「<reading>みみ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫の耳を見る。
example_sentences.english: I look at the cat's ears.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]の耳[みみ]を見[み]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は耳で聞く。
example_sentences.english: I listen with my ears.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は耳[みみ]で聞[き]く。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の耳はいい。
example_sentences.english: Dogs have good ears.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の耳[みみ]はいい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 便（べん）＋利（り）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A gadget that hands you real <kanji>convenience</kanji> and a clear <kanji>advantage</kanji> at the same time is exactly what <vocabulary>convenient</vocabulary> means. Handle it as a な adjective, so な comes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: このコンビニは便利です。
example_sentences.english: This convenience store is convenient.
example_sentences.furigana: このコンビニは便[べん]利[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅に近い家は便利です。
example_sentences.english: A house near the station is convenient.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]に近[ちか]い家[いえ]は便[べん]利[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 便利な辞書を使います。
example_sentences.english: I use a convenient dictionary.
example_sentences.furigana: 便[べん]利[り]な辞[じ]書[しょ]を使[つか]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 返（かえ）＋す.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You borrowed the umbrella, so now you carry it back to its owner. Putting a thing back in the hand it came from is to <vocabulary>return</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei borrows Kai's spare gym shoes, then walks the whole way back to leave <reading>Kai's shoes</reading> at his locker, 「<reading>かえす</reading>」, and handing them straight back is to <vocabulary>return</vocabulary> them.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で本を返します。
example_sentences.english: I return the book at the library.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で本[ほん]を返[かえ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達にペンを返しました。
example_sentences.english: I returned the pen to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]にペンを返[かえ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にお金を返します。
example_sentences.english: I'll pay him back the money.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]にお金[かね]を返[かえ]します。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 花（はな）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>flower</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>flower</vocabulary> word are one and the same character, so the bloom it draws is the bloom it means.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hen named <reading>Hannah</reading> pecks through the green grass until one blade changes its top into bright colour, then clucks <reading>はな</reading> and guards that new <vocabulary form="花">flower</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で花を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the flowers in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で花[はな]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 母に花を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought flowers for my mother.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]に花[はな]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この花は高いです。
example_sentences.english: This flower is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: この花[はな]は高[たか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 飛（と）＋ぶ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your feet push off and for one long second the air holds your whole weight. That hanging second is what it means to <vocabulary>fly / jump</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your <reading>toe</reading> pushes off, a ghost shouts <reading>boo</reading>, and for one long second the air holds your whole weight as you yelp 「<reading>とぶ</reading>」 and <vocabulary form="飛ぶ">jump</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の帽子が風で飛びます。
example_sentences.english: My hat blows away in the wind.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の帽[ぼう]子[し]が風[かぜ]で飛[と]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい鳥が空を飛びます。
example_sentences.english: A big bird flies through the sky.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[おお]きい鳥[とり]が空[そら]を飛[と]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供がベッドで飛びます。
example_sentences.english: The child jumps on the bed.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]がベッドで飛[と]びます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 音（おん）＋楽（がく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take the kind of <kanji>sound</kanji> that makes you sit up in a silent room and string it along a branch like ice beads until sitting and listening is pure <kanji>comfort</kanji>. That is <vocabulary>music</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は音楽が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like music.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は音[おん]楽[がく]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は毎朝音楽を聞きます。
example_sentences.english: She listens to music every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]音[おん]楽[がく]を聞[き]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この音楽は面白いですね。
example_sentences.english: This music is interesting, isn't it.
example_sentences.furigana: この音[おん]楽[がく]は面[おも]白[しろ]いですね。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 残（のこ）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Everyone clears out of the classroom at the bell. The one bag still by the window, after the rest are gone, is what <vocabulary>remains</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: As the bell empties the classroom, a kid spots Coral's bag still by the window and yells <reading>no, Coral</reading>, 「<reading>のこる</reading>」, since that bag is all that <vocabulary form="残る">remains</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: パンが少し残った。
example_sentences.english: A little bread was left over.
example_sentences.furigana: パンが少[すこ]し残[のこ]った。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は部屋に残った。
example_sentences.english: He stayed behind in the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は部屋[へや]に残[のこ]った。

example_sentences.japanese: 時間が少し残っています。
example_sentences.english: There's a little time left.
example_sentences.furigana: 時[じ]間[かん]が少[すこ]し残[のこ]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 習（なら）＋う.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You sit beside someone who can already do the thing and copy them move for move until your hands pick the skill up on their own. Taking it straight off another person that way is what it means to <vocabulary>learn (from)</vocabulary> them.
items.reading_mnemonic: A tame deer in <reading>Nara</reading> trails a calligraphy student all afternoon, scratching a copy of every stroke he makes into the dust. He watches it ape him and mutters 「<reading>ならう</reading>」, which is what it means to <vocabulary>learn (from)</vocabulary> someone.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は先生に習います。
example_sentences.english: I learn from my teacher.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は先[せん]生[せい]に習[なら]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹はお茶を習う。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister is learning tea ceremony.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]はお茶[ちゃ]を習[なら]う。

example_sentences.japanese: 来週から料理を習う。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to start learning cooking next week.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]週[しゅう]から料[りょう]理[り]を習[なら]う。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 遠（とお）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: From the top of the mountain trail, Koichi's konbini is one bright dot you can hide behind your thumb. Only real distance shrinks a shop like that, so it must be <vocabulary>far</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A barefoot hiker on the mountain trail lifts one <reading>toe</reading> and it completely blots out the vending machine at the summit. Anything a bare toe can blot out has to be <reading>とおい</reading>, plain <vocabulary>far</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 病院はここから遠い。
example_sentences.english: The hospital is far from here.
example_sentences.furigana: 病[びょう]院[いん]はここから遠[とお]い。

example_sentences.japanese: あのスーパーは遠いですか。
example_sentences.english: Is that supermarket far?
example_sentences.furigana: あのスーパーは遠[とお]いですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 遠い町へ明日行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'll go to a far town tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 遠[とお]い町[まち]へ明日[あした]行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 飛（ひ）＋行（こう）＋機（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.

example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]で飛[ひ]行[こう]機[き]を見[み]ました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 会（かい）＋議（ぎ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Trap eight people around one table in slow formal <kanji>deliberation</kanji>, refill the coffee twice, and what you are left with is a <vocabulary>meeting</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]会[かい]議[ぎ]があります。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 場（ば）kun'yomi ＋ 所（しょ）on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The mountain trail has exactly one flat ledge wide enough to stand on. Hikers guard that <vocabulary>place</vocabulary> because there is nowhere else to plant your feet.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館は静かな場所です。

example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]は静[しず]かな場[ば]所[しょ]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（ち）＋下（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>ground</kanji> keeps going <kanji>down</kanji> well past your feet, and any room dug into that dark counts as <vocabulary>underground</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 真（ま）＋ん＋中（なか）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Find the one <kanji>true</kanji>, exact point of a shape, the spot equally far from every edge. That <kanji>middle</kanji> point is its <vocabulary>center</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sei steps onto a moving staircase that quietly <reading>escalates</reading> her to the next floor with no walking at all. Her class calls that gliding staircase the <reading>エスカレーター</reading>, the <vocabulary>escalator</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Irregular — いりぐち cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 入口.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single <kanji>mouth</kanji> in a building's front wall that people <kanji>enter</kanji> through is its <vocabulary>entrance</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi stands at the front door chanting <reading>ee-ree-goo-chee</reading> at everyone who walks past. That doorway is the <reading>いりぐち</reading>, the one <vocabulary>entrance</vocabulary> into his konbini.

example_sentences.japanese: 入口はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the entrance?
example_sentences.furigana: 入[いり]口[ぐち]はどこですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 出（で）＋口（ぐち）. Rendaku: 口 くち → ぐち.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Follow the arrows to the <kanji>mouth</kanji> in the far wall you <kanji>leave</kanji> the building by, and that gap is the <vocabulary>exit</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 出口はどこですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 窓（まど）＋口（ぐち）. Rendaku: 口 くち → ぐち.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>mouth</kanji>-shaped slot cut in a counter, where a clerk leans through to take your papers, is a <vocabulary>service window</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 引（ひ）＋き＋出（だ）＋し.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Give the desk-front a <kanji>pull</kanji> and the whole tray slides forward until it almost <kanji>exits</kanji> the desk. That tray you haul out and push back is a <vocabulary>drawer</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 歯（は）＋ブラシ.

example_sentences.furigana: その書[しょ]類[るい]をかばんに入[い]れました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 続（つづ）＋き.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The stretch where something that <kanji>continues</kanji> picks up again, right after it looked finished, is its <vocabulary>continuation</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Just when the zoo tour looks finished, Sue the keeper jangles her <reading>zoo key</reading>, 「<reading>つづき</reading>」, and it picks up again through one more gate, the <vocabulary form="続き">continuation</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 終（お）＋わり.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 危（あぶ）＋ない.

items.meaning: to rest / take a day off
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 休（やす）＋む.

accepted_answers.answer_text: to rest / take a day off
