items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The night baker leaves one leftover <reading>cone bun</reading> on the counter and says <reading>こんばんは</reading> to whoever comes in last. That after-dark greeting is <vocabulary>good evening</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: こんばんは。今日は忙しかったです。
example_sentences.english: Good evening. Today was busy.
example_sentences.furigana: こんばんは。今日[きょう]は忙[いそが]しかったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生、こんばんは。
example_sentences.english: Good evening, teacher.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]、こんばんは。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はこんばんはと言いました。
example_sentences.english: She said good evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はこんばんはと言[い]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Draw it out on the platform as the train pulls away, the way you would a slow <reading>so long</reading>. That heavy, drawn-out <reading>さようなら</reading> is the <vocabulary>goodbye</vocabulary> that means a good while.
items.description: Heavier than the English 'bye'. It suggests a long separation, so to family or coworkers you will see tomorrow it can sound oddly final; day-to-day partings use lighter phrases.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はさようならと言いました。
example_sentences.english: She said goodbye.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はさようならと言[い]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に「さようなら」と言って、駅を出ました。
example_sentences.english: I said goodbye to my friend and left the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に「さようなら」と言[い]って、駅[えき]を出[で]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: さようなら、また来週。
example_sentences.english: Goodbye, see you next week.
example_sentences.furigana: さようなら、また来[らい]週[しゅう]。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand an <reading>alligator</reading> a warm towel and even it will grunt out a grudging <reading>ありがとう</reading>. Stripped of the manners it is simply <vocabulary>thank you</vocabulary>, favour noted.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thanks for helping me.
example_sentences.furigana: 手伝[てつだ]ってくれてありがとう。

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙をありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for the letter.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[て]紙[がみ]をありがとう。

example_sentences.japanese: 本当にありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much.
example_sentences.furigana: 本[ほん]当[とう]にありがとう。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <reading>sumo</reading> wrestler treads on your foot on the packed train and, without turning round, breathes <reading>すみません</reading>. It is the all-day <vocabulary>excuse me</vocabulary> that carries a small apology folded inside it.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、今何時ですか。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, what time is it now?
example_sentences.furigana: すみません、今[いま]何[なん]時[じ]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、駅はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, where is the station?
example_sentences.furigana: すみません、駅[えき]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れてすみません。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for being late.
example_sentences.furigana: 遅[おく]れてすみません。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sei knocks Grandma Kane's teacup off the mossy step and blurts <reading>ごめんなさい</reading> before it even hits the ground, a rushed <reading>go-men-nah-sigh</reading>. It is the full, please-forgive-me <vocabulary>I'm sorry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れてごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for being late.
example_sentences.furigana: 遅[おく]れてごめんなさい。

example_sentences.japanese: 忘れてごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry, I forgot.
example_sentences.furigana: 忘[わす]れてごめんなさい。

example_sentences.japanese: 本当にごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: I'm really sorry.
example_sentences.furigana: 本[ほん]当[とう]にごめんなさい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — お＋願（ねが）＋いします.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>request</kanji> held out flat in both hands, with <vocabulary>please</vocabulary> set on top like a bow on a box. That polite wrapping around the ask is the whole word.
items.reading_mnemonic: You hold your request out flat in both hands, a bow on top like a gift box, and murmur <reading>oh, need I ask</reading>, 「<reading>おねがいします</reading>」, the polite wrapping that means <vocabulary form="お願いします">please</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 水をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Water, please.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[みず]をお願[ねが]いします。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生、質問をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Teacher, I have a question, please.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]、質[しつ]問[もん]をお願[ねが]いします。

example_sentences.japanese: 領収書をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: A receipt, please.
example_sentences.furigana: 領[りょう]収[しゅう]書[しょ]をお願[ねが]いします。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You shake hands with a man called <reading>Jimmy</reading> who instantly <reading>mashes</reading> your knuckles flat, and out falls <reading>はじめまして</reading>. It is the fixed opening line for a first meeting, <vocabulary>nice to meet you</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: はじめまして。私は学生です。
example_sentences.english: Nice to meet you. I'm a student.
example_sentences.furigana: はじめまして。私[わたし]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 「はじめまして」「こちらこそ、はじめまして」
example_sentences.english: "Nice to meet you." "Nice to meet you too."
example_sentences.furigana: 「はじめまして」「こちらこそ、はじめまして」

example_sentences.japanese: はじめまして、田中さん。お名前は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: Nice to meet you, Mr. Tanaka. What's your name?
example_sentences.furigana: はじめまして、田中[たなか]さん。お名[な]前[まえ]は何[なに]ですか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At lights-out Sei mumbles <reading>おやすみなさい</reading> into the pillow, a slurred <reading>oh-yah-soo-me-nah-sigh</reading> that trails off into a yawn. It is the <vocabulary>good night</vocabulary> you say heading to sleep, not the one you say leaving a room.

example_sentences.japanese: 母におやすみなさいと言いました。
example_sentences.english: I said good night to my mother.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]におやすみなさいと言[い]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: もう遅いです。おやすみなさい。
example_sentences.english: It's already late. Good night.
example_sentences.furigana: もう遅[おそ]いです。おやすみなさい。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供たちはおやすみなさいと言って、寝ました。
example_sentences.english: The children said good night and went to sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]たちはおやすみなさいと言[い]って、寝[ね]ました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lift your chopsticks over a steaming bowl and say <reading>いただきます</reading>, close enough to <reading>eat-a-duck-ee</reading> to stick. It is the set phrase you say before eating, <vocabulary>let's eat</vocabulary>, with a nod of thanks for the food.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯です。いただきます。
example_sentences.english: Dinner's ready. Let's eat.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]です。いただきます。

example_sentences.japanese: みんなでいただきます。
example_sentences.english: Let's all eat together.
example_sentences.furigana: みんなでいただきます。

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんが作った料理をいただきます。
example_sentences.english: I'll eat the dish my mother made.
example_sentences.furigana: お母[かあ]さんが作[つく]った料[りょう]理[り]をいただきます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Too stuffed to move after dinner, you flop onto the <reading>Gucci sofa, Ma</reading> and let out a long groan. That groan, 「<reading>ごちそうさま</reading>」, is exactly how you say <vocabulary>thanks for the meal</vocabulary> once your plate is clean.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、ごちそうさまでした。
example_sentences.english: Mom, thank you for the meal.
example_sentences.furigana: お母[かあ]さん、ごちそうさまでした。

example_sentences.japanese: レストランでごちそうさまでした。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for the meal at the restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: レストランでごちそうさまでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の家でご飯を食べて、ごちそうさまと言いました。
example_sentences.english: I ate at my friend's house and said thanks for the meal.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の家[いえ]でご飯[はん]を食[た]べて、ごちそうさまと言[い]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 行（い）＋ってきます.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You pause at the <kanji>go</kanji> crossroads and call back to the house before you step out. That call is <vocabulary>I'm off (going and coming back)</vocabulary>, and the crossroads is your promise to walk back through it by evening.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 行 is 「い」 from 行く, so <vocabulary>I'm off (going and coming back)</vocabulary> is <reading>いってきます</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から学校に行ってきます。
example_sentences.english: I'm off to school now.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]から学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]ってきます。

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとコンビニに行ってきます。
example_sentences.english: I'm just going to the convenience store.
example_sentences.furigana: ちょっとコンビニに行[い]ってきます。

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行に行ってきます。
example_sentences.english: I'm off to the bank.
example_sentences.furigana: 銀[ぎん]行[こう]に行[い]ってきます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You fling open the front door with a magician's <reading>ta-da, I'm a</reading> wizard flourish. That same sound, 「<reading>ただいま</reading>」, is exactly how you call out <vocabulary>I'm home</vocabulary> the moment you step inside.

example_sentences.japanese: ただいま。今日は忙しかったです。
example_sentences.english: I'm home. Today was busy.
example_sentences.furigana: ただいま。今日[きょう]は忙[いそが]しかったです。

example_sentences.japanese: ただいま、お父さん。
example_sentences.english: I'm home, Dad.
example_sentences.furigana: ただいま、お父[とう]さん。

example_sentences.japanese: ただいま。家族はまだ晩ご飯を食べていません。
example_sentences.english: I'm home. My family hasn't eaten dinner yet.
example_sentences.furigana: ただいま。家[か]族[ぞく]はまだ晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べていません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — お＋帰（かえ）＋りなさい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hand the sweeper to whoever just <kanji>returned</kanji> through the front door, and the greeting that goes with it is <vocabulary>welcome back</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 帰 is 「かえ」 from 帰る, so <vocabulary>welcome back</vocabulary> is <reading>おかえりなさい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、お帰りなさい。
example_sentences.english: Welcome home, Dad.
example_sentences.furigana: お父[とう]さん、お帰[かえ]りなさい。

example_sentences.japanese: お帰りなさい。晩ご飯を作りました。
example_sentences.english: Welcome back. I made dinner.
example_sentences.furigana: お帰[かえ]りなさい。晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を作[つく]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はうちに帰って、お帰りなさいと言いました。
example_sentences.english: She came home, and I said welcome back to her.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はうちに帰[かえ]って、お帰[かえ]りなさいと言[い]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 意（い）＋見（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A meaning (意) that you see (見): your opinion.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>idea</kanji> stuck on loop in your heart only turns into an <vocabulary>opinion</vocabulary> once you make other people <kanji>see</kanji> it too.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議で自分の意見を言うのは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: It's hard to give your own opinion in a meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]で自[じ]分[ぶん]の意[い]見[けん]を言[い]うのは難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はみんなの意見を聞いてから、答えを教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher heard everyone's opinions first, then told us the answer.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]はみんなの意[い]見[けん]を聞[き]いてから、答[こた]えを教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉に電話して、意見を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I called my older sister and asked for her opinion.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]に電[でん]話[わ]して、意[い]見[けん]を聞[き]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 社（しゃ）＋会（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A shrine (社) gathering (会) of people: society.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every <kanji>company</kanji> and shrine keeps its gates open, and the crowds who <kanji>meet</kanji> and mingle between them are what we call a <vocabulary>society</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は春から社会に出ます。
example_sentences.english: My son goes out into the working world this spring.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は春[はる]から社[しゃ]会[かい]に出[で]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 社会はだんだん便利になりました。
example_sentences.english: Society has gradually become more convenient.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]会[かい]はだんだん便[べん]利[り]になりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 社会のために働く人になりたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to become someone who works for the good of society.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]会[かい]のために働[はたら]く人[ひと]になりたいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 新（しん）＋聞（ぶん）＋社（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>company</kanji> whose one job is to <kanji>hear</kanji> what happened overnight and rush it into print while the news is still <kanji>new</kanji> is a <vocabulary>newspaper company</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は新聞社で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother works at a newspaper company.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は新[しん]聞[ぶん]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]いています。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉はその新聞社で働きたいです。
example_sentences.english: My older sister wants to work at that newspaper company.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]はその新[しん]聞[ぶん]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]きたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞社の人が学校に来ました。
example_sentences.english: Someone from the newspaper company came to the school.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[しん]聞[ぶん]社[しゃ]の人[ひと]が学[がっ]校[こう]に来[き]ました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 輸（ゆ）＋出（しゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Transport (輸) that exits (出): to export.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Goods you <kanji>transport</kanji> to the country's <kanji>exit</kanji> and push out across the border are an <vocabulary>export</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社は野菜を輸出しています。
example_sentences.english: This company exports vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]は野[や]菜[さい]を輸[ゆ]出[しゅつ]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は車をたくさん輸出します。
example_sentences.english: Japan exports a lot of cars.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]は車[くるま]をたくさん輸[ゆ]出[しゅつ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 貿易には輸出も輸入もあります。
example_sentences.english: Trade includes both exports and imports.
example_sentences.furigana: 貿[ぼう]易[えき]には輸[ゆ]出[しゅつ]も輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]もあります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 輸（ゆ）＋入（にゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Transport (輸) that enters (入): to import.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a cargo ship <kanji>send</kanji>s foreign goods across the sea and they <kanji>enter</kanji> your shops, what just landed is an <vocabulary>import</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は米をあまり輸入しません。
example_sentences.english: Japan doesn't import much rice.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]は米[べい]をあまり輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]しません。

example_sentences.japanese: この店ではコーヒーを輸入しています。
example_sentences.english: This shop imports coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]ではコーヒーを輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 輸入の服は高いです。
example_sentences.english: Imported clothes are expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: 輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]の服[ふく]は高[たか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 市（し）＋場（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The city's (市) open place (場): a market.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand the awning-covered <kanji>market</kanji> one permanent <kanji>place</kanji> to set up, the same square every single day, and that fixed trading ground is a <vocabulary>market</vocabulary>.
items.description: Read this way, the word means an abstract market — a stock market, an export market, the whole arena of buyers and sellers. It is not a physical hall of stalls; that sense is a different reading of the same two characters.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は魚を市場に売りに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to the market to sell fish.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は魚[さかな]を市[し]場[じょう]に売[う]りに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この市場は野菜が安いです。
example_sentences.english: Vegetables are cheap at this market.
example_sentences.furigana: この市[し]場[じょう]は野[や]菜[さい]が安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい市場が町にできました。
example_sentences.english: A new market was built in the town.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい市[し]場[じょう]が町[まち]にできました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 結（けっ）＋果（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 結 けつ → けっ.
items.mnemonic_text: Tying together (結) a fruit (果): the result.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Tie</kanji> off the last knot of a long job and cut open whatever <kanji>fruit</kanji> it grew; that payoff is the <vocabulary>result</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験の結果を心配しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried about the exam results.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]の結[けっ]果[か]を心[しん]配[ぱい]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 結果はまだ分かりません。
example_sentences.english: The results aren't known yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 結[けっ]果[か]はまだ分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: いい結果がほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a good result.
example_sentences.furigana: いい結[けっ]果[か]がほしいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 夫（ふう）＋婦（ふ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Husband (夫) and wife (婦): a couple.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Put a <kanji>husband</kanji> and a <kanji>wife</kanji> under one roof, rings on, and the pair of them together make a <vocabulary>married couple</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣に住んでいる夫婦はとても親切です。
example_sentences.english: The couple living next door is very kind.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]に住[す]んでいる夫[ふう]婦[ふ]はとても親[しん]切[せつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あの夫婦は公園で散歩しています。
example_sentences.english: That couple is taking a walk in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: あの夫[ふう]婦[ふ]は公[こう]園[えん]で散[さん]歩[ぽ]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは去年結婚して、夫婦になりました。
example_sentences.english: We got married last year and became a couple.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは去[きょ]年[ねん]結[けっ]婚[こん]して、夫[ふう]婦[ふ]になりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 男（だん）＋性（せい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>man</kanji> straight from the rice field, ticked into one column of the <kanji>gender</kanji> box on the form, is <vocabulary>male (gender)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男性は先生です。
example_sentences.english: That man is a teacher.

example_sentences.english: The money is zero.
example_sentences.furigana: お金[かね]は零[れい]です。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 僕（ぼく）.
items.mnemonic_text: A boy says boku when he means I.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In the thicket, the one figure still visible always answers as <kanji>me</kanji>, and when a man says it, that answer is exactly <vocabulary>I (male)</vocabulary>.
items.description: Used mainly by men and boys speaking casually or semi-formally; women rarely use it for themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は学生です。
example_sentences.english: I'm a student.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は今日映画を見る。
example_sentences.english: I'm watching a movie today.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は今日[きょう]映[えい]画[が]を見[み]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 僕と一緒に公園に行く？
example_sentences.english: Want to go to the park with me?
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に公[こう]園[えん]に行[い]く？

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 少（しょう）＋女（じょ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Few (少) years, a woman (女): a girl.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>woman</kanji> with only a <kanji>little</kanji> of her growing behind her, still barely elbow-high, is a <vocabulary>girl</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓の外で少女が雪を見ています。
example_sentences.english: A girl is outside the window, watching the snow.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]の外[そと]で少[しょう]女[じょ]が雪[ゆき]を見[み]ています。

example_sentences.japanese: 少女は赤い帽子を探していました。
example_sentences.english: The girl was looking for her red hat.
example_sentences.furigana: 少[しょう]女[じょ]は赤[あか]い帽[ぼう]子[し]を探[さが]していました。

example_sentences.japanese: この本は十歳の少女が書きました。
example_sentences.english: A ten-year-old girl wrote this book.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は十[じゅっ]歳[さい]の少[しょう]女[じょ]が書[か]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 友（ゆう）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A friend (友) person (人): a friend.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>person</kanji> you would call a <kanji>friend</kanji>, named in the stiff wording you would put on a form, is a <vocabulary>friend (formal)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学の友人が来月結婚します。
example_sentences.english: A friend from university is getting married next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]の友[ゆう]人[じん]が来[らい]月[げつ]結[けっ]婚[こん]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 友人に紹介してもらった旅館は、静かできれいでした。
example_sentences.english: The inn a friend told me about was quiet and clean.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[ゆう]人[じん]に紹[しょう]介[かい]してもらった旅[りょ]館[かん]は、静[しず]かできれいでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 困ったとき、友人が一番に電話をくれました。
example_sentences.english: When I was in trouble, a friend was the first to call me.
example_sentences.furigana: 困[こま]ったとき、友[ゆう]人[じん]が一[いち]番[ばん]に電[でん]話[わ]をくれました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 個（こ）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A single (個) person (人): an individual.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull one <kanji>person</kanji> out of the crowd and weigh them on their own, and what you are looking at is an <vocabulary>individual</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは会社のパソコンで、個人のものではありません。
example_sentences.english: This is the company's computer, not a personal one.
example_sentences.furigana: これは会[かい]社[しゃ]のパソコンで、個[こ]人[じん]のものではありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 個人の電話番号は書かなくてもいいです。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to write your personal phone number.
example_sentences.furigana: 個[こ]人[じん]の電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]は書[か]かなくてもいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私個人の意見ですが、この店のパンが一番おいしいと思います。
example_sentences.english: That's just my personal opinion, but I think this shop's bread is the best.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]個[こ]人[じん]の意[い]見[けん]ですが、この店[みせ]のパンが一[いち]番[ばん]おいしいと思[おも]います。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 客（きゃく）.
items.mnemonic_text: A visitor sheltered under a roof: a guest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anyone who comes through your door expecting to be seated, served and fussed over before they leave again is a <vocabulary>guest / customer</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、喫茶店に客があまり来ません。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, not many customers come to the coffee shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]に客[きゃく]があまり来[き]ません。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は客が泊まるので、部屋を準備します。
example_sentences.english: Guests are staying over this weekend, so I'm getting the room ready.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は客[きゃく]が泊[と]まるので、部屋[へや]を準[じゅん]備[び]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員は客に傘を貸しました。
example_sentences.english: The clerk lent the customer an umbrella.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]は客[きゃく]に傘[かさ]を貸[か]しました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — お＋客（きゃく）＋さん.
items.mnemonic_text: Polite form of guest: a customer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That same visitor, but bowed to on the way in, thanked on the way out, and spoken of only in the polite words staff keep for people they serve, is a <vocabulary>customer (polite)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さん、財布を忘れていますよ。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, you're forgetting your wallet!
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さん、財[さい]布[ふ]を忘[わす]れていますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はお客さんが多くて、昼ご飯を食べる時間がありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: We had so many customers today that I had no time to eat lunch.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]はお客[きゃく]さんが多[おお]くて、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べる時[じ]間[かん]がありませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんにお釣りを渡してください。
example_sentences.english: Please hand the customer their change.
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さんにお釣[つ]りを渡[わた]してください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 店（てん）＋員（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A shop's (店) staff member (員): a clerk.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A roadside <kanji>shop</kanji> so small it keeps just one <kanji>employee</kanji> behind the counter, and that person is the <vocabulary>shop clerk</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員に日本語で話しました。
example_sentences.english: I spoke to the shop clerk in Japanese.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]に日本[にほん]語[ご]で話[はな]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの店員はとても親切です。
example_sentences.english: That shop clerk is very kind.
example_sentences.furigana: あの店[てん]員[いん]はとても親[しん]切[せつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員に道を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked the shop clerk for directions.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]に道[みち]を聞[き]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 主（しゅ）＋婦（ふ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The main (主) woman (婦) of the house.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The household <kanji>lord</kanji> whose word everyone follows, who also happens to be the <kanji>wife</kanji>, is the <vocabulary>housewife</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は主婦です。
example_sentences.english: My mother is a housewife.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は主[しゅ]婦[ふ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 主婦は毎日忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: Housewives are busy every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 主[しゅ]婦[ふ]は毎[まい]日[にち]忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の主婦に野菜をもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got some vegetables from the housewife next door.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の主[しゅ]婦[ふ]に野[や]菜[さい]をもらいました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 学（がく）＋者（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (者) of learning (学): a scholar.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>person</kanji> stacked so high with days of <kanji>study</kanji> that they grumble about it has turned into a <vocabulary>scholar</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は有名な学者です。
example_sentences.english: He is a famous scholar.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は有[ゆう]名[めい]な学[がく]者[しゃ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: その学者は歴史を教えています。
example_sentences.english: That scholar teaches history.
example_sentences.furigana: その学[がく]者[しゃ]は歴[れき]史[し]を教[おし]えています。

example_sentences.japanese: 学者になるのは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a scholar is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 学[がく]者[しゃ]になるのは難[むずか]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 成（せい）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One who has become (成) a person (人): an adult.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>person</kanji> the law finally counts as having <kanji>turned into</kanji> a full-grown one is an <vocabulary>adult</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は今年成人しました。
example_sentences.english: My older sister came of age this year.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は今年[ことし]成[せい]人[じん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘はまだ成人していません。
example_sentences.english: My daughter is not yet an adult.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]はまだ成[せい]人[じん]していません。

example_sentences.japanese: 成人したら、一人で旅行できます。
example_sentences.english: Once you become an adult, you can travel alone.
example_sentences.furigana: 成[せい]人[じん]したら、一人[ひとり]で旅[りょ]行[こう]できます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 親（おや）.
items.mnemonic_text: Standing by a tree, watching over you: a parent.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>parent</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>parent</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean exactly the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: From the highest branch of the tree by Sei's school field, a figure craning to see every kick shouts <reading>oh, ya</reading>, 「<reading>おや</reading>」, at each goal, and only a <vocabulary form="親">parent</vocabulary> would.

example_sentences.japanese: 親に電話しました。
example_sentences.english: I called my parent.
example_sentences.furigana: 親[おや]に電[でん]話[わ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 親は子供の名前を考えます。
example_sentences.english: Parents think about their child's name.
example_sentences.furigana: 親[おや]は子[こ]供[ども]の名[な]前[まえ]を考[かんが]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 親と一緒に旅行しました。
example_sentences.english: I traveled together with my parent.
example_sentences.furigana: 親[おや]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に旅[りょ]行[こう]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 太（ふと）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A big extra drop of size: thick.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You have already met the kanji <kanji form="太">thick</kanji>, so the word <vocabulary form="太い">thick / fat</vocabulary> is nothing new: it is the same character with the same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: That one extra drop of fat lands on a <reading>foot</reading> already stretched as big as it can stand, and now no shoe fits. A foot gone that wide is <reading>ふとい</reading>, <vocabulary form="太い">fat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 庭に太い木が一本あります。
example_sentences.english: There's one thick tree in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 庭[にわ]に太[ふと]い木[き]が一[いっ]本[ぽん]あります。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は首が太くて、力が強いです。
example_sentences.english: My older brother has a thick neck and is really strong.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は首[くび]が太[ふと]くて、力[ちから]が強[つよ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 黒板にチョークで太く書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write in thick strokes on the blackboard with the chalk.
example_sentences.furigana: 黒[こく]板[ばん]にチョークで太[ふと]く書[か]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Louie pours you a coffee that has sat out so long it is neither hot nor cold. A drink stuck at room temperature like that is <vocabulary form="ぬるい">lukewarm</vocabulary>, and hearing <reading>new Louie</reading> pour another one is how you keep hold of 「<reading>ぬるい</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: お茶がぬるくなったので、もう一度入れました。
example_sentences.english: My tea had gone lukewarm, so I made a fresh cup.
example_sentences.furigana: お茶[ちゃ]がぬるくなったので、もう一[いち]度[ど]入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: このビール、ぬるくてまずいよ。
example_sentences.english: This beer is lukewarm and tastes awful.
example_sentences.furigana: このビール、ぬるくてまずいよ。

example_sentences.japanese: ぬるい牛乳は飲みたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to drink lukewarm milk.
example_sentences.furigana: ぬるい牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]は飲[の]みたくない。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A tight fit that pinches: tight, harsh.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The zip-tie on that parcel is pulled so <vocabulary form="きつい">tight / harsh</vocabulary> it <reading>cuts you</reading> when you lift it. That bite into your fingers is what <reading>きつい</reading> means.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年のシャツを着たら、きつかった。
example_sentences.english: I put on last year's shirt, and it was tight.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]のシャツを着[き]たら、きつかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝六時から働くのはきついね。
example_sentences.english: Working from six every morning is rough, isn't it?
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]六[ろく]時[じ]から働[はたら]くのはきついね。

example_sentences.japanese: 父に「遅い」ときつく言われました。
example_sentences.english: My father told me sharply, "You're late."
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]に「遅[おそ]い」ときつく言[い]われました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In this town you can <reading>sue a guy</reading> for looking at you wrong and still collect a payout. That the courts work that way is both <vocabulary form="すごい">amazing / terrible</vocabulary>, so onlookers just breathe <reading>すごい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 見て、すごい雪だよ。
example_sentences.english: Look at all that snow!
example_sentences.furigana: 見[み]て、すごい雪[ゆき]だよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 三歳の娘がカタカナを全部書けて、すごいと思いました。
example_sentences.english: My three-year-old daughter can write all the katakana. I thought that was amazing.
example_sentences.furigana: 三[さん]歳[さい]の娘[むすめ]がカタカナを全[ぜん]部[ぶ]書[か]けて、すごいと思[おも]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前はすごい人でした。
example_sentences.english: There was a huge crowd in front of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]はすごい人[ひと]でした。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every Sunday a kid runs the same <reading>zoo ruse</reading> and slips through a gap in the fence without paying. Beating the queue that way is <vocabulary form="ずるい">sly / unfair</vocabulary>, and the gate guard just sighs <reading>ずるい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分だけお菓子を二つ取るのはずるいよ。
example_sentences.english: It's not fair to take two sweets just for yourself.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]だけお菓[か]子[し]を二[ふた]つ取[と]るのはずるいよ。

example_sentences.japanese: テストで友達の答えを見るのはずるいです。
example_sentences.english: Looking at a friend's answers during a test is cheating.
example_sentences.furigana: テストで友[とも]達[だち]の答[こた]えを見[み]るのはずるいです。

example_sentences.japanese: あの猫はずるいから、よく犬の席に座ります。
example_sentences.english: That cat is sly, so it often sits in the dog's spot.
example_sentences.furigana: あの猫[ねこ]はずるいから、よく犬[いぬ]の席[せき]に座[すわ]ります。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — まじめ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 真面目.
items.mnemonic_text: A true (真) face (面) and eye (目): serious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hold a <kanji form="真">true</kanji> <kanji form="面">face</kanji>, no act, with your <kanji form="目">eye</kanji> fixed on the work in front of you. That is what <vocabulary form="真面目">serious / diligent</vocabulary> looks like, and it takes な before the noun it describes.
items.reading_mnemonic: Jimmy wears a true face, no act, his eye fixed on the homework in front of him. His sister yells <reading>Ma, Jimmy</reading> is all <reading>まじめ</reading> again, so <vocabulary form="真面目">diligent</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は真面目な学生で、毎晩勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: My son is a diligent student who studies every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は真面目[まじめ]な学[がく]生[せい]で、毎[まい]晩[ばん]勉[べん]強[きょう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議では、みんな真面目な顔をしていました。
example_sentences.english: At the meeting, everyone had a serious look on their face.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]では、みんな真面目[まじめ]な顔[かお]をしていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 真面目に練習すれば、上手になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you practice seriously, you'll get good at it.
example_sentences.furigana: 真面目[まじめ]に練[れん]習[しゅう]すれば、上手[じょうず]になりますよ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 熱（ねっ）＋心（しん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 熱 ねつ → ねっ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A steady <kanji form="熱">heat</kanji> kept burning in the <kanji form="心">heart</kanji> is what being <vocabulary form="熱心">enthusiastic</vocabulary> about something feels like. It is a な adjective, so な goes before the noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は熱心に日本の歴史の本を読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: He is eagerly reading a book on Japanese history.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は熱[ねっ]心[しん]に日本[にほん]の歴[れき]史[し]の本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 熱心なお客さんが、朝から店の前で待っていた。
example_sentences.english: Keen customers were waiting in front of the shop from the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねっ]心[しん]なお客[きゃく]さんが、朝[あさ]から店[みせ]の前[まえ]で待[ま]っていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は熱心に説明してくれましたが、よく分かりませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The teacher explained it with real enthusiasm, but I didn't really understand.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は熱[ねっ]心[しん]に説[せつ]明[めい]してくれましたが、よく分[わ]かりませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 十（じゅう）＋分（ぶん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Ten <kanji form="分">part</kanji>s out of <kanji form="十">ten</kanji> make up the whole, and having the whole of something is having <vocabulary form="十分">sufficient / enough</vocabulary> of it. As a な adjective, な comes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この弁当は大きいので、一つで十分です。
example_sentences.english: This boxed lunch is big, so one is plenty.
example_sentences.furigana: この弁[べん]当[とう]は大[おお]きいので、一[ひと]つで十[じゅう]分[ぶん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の山に行くなら、このコートでは十分じゃないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are going up a mountain in winter, this coat won't be enough.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]の山[やま]に行[い]くなら、このコートでは十[じゅう]分[ぶん]じゃないよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は十分に練習したので、試験は大丈夫でしょう。
example_sentences.english: My little brother practiced plenty, so he should be fine on the exam.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は十[じゅう]分[ぶん]に練[れん]習[しゅう]したので、試[し]験[けん]は大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]でしょう。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋安（あん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set the <kanji form="不">negative</kanji> mark against <kanji form="安">peaceful</kanji> and the calm drains out, and a mind left without calm is <vocabulary form="不安">anxious / uneasy</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な lands before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で外国へ行くのは、ちょっと不安です。
example_sentences.english: I'm a bit nervous about going abroad on my own.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で外[がい]国[こく]へ行[い]くのは、ちょっと不[ふ]安[あん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜の道が暗くて、娘は不安な顔をしていた。
example_sentences.english: The road was dark at night, and my daughter looked uneasy.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]の道[みち]が暗[くら]くて、娘[むすめ]は不[ふ]安[あん]な顔[かお]をしていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が説明してくれたので、不安がなくなりました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher explained it to me, so my worries went away.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]が説[せつ]明[めい]してくれたので、不[ふ]安[あん]がなくなりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 安（あん）＋全（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji form="安">Peaceful</kanji> across the <kanji form="全">whole</kanji> of a place, with no corner left unguarded, is what makes it <vocabulary form="安全">safe</vocabulary>. As a な adjective, it wants な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この橋は古いですが、まだ安全です。
example_sentences.english: This bridge is old, but it's still safe.
example_sentences.furigana: この橋[はし]は古[ふる]いですが、まだ安[あん]全[ぜん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が公園の安全な場所で遊んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The kids are playing in a safe spot in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]の安[あん]全[ぜん]な場[ば]所[しょ]で遊[あそ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 雪の日は、ゆっくり運転したほうが安全ですよ。
example_sentences.english: On snowy days, it's safer to drive slowly.
example_sentences.furigana: 雪[ゆき]の日[ひ]は、ゆっくり運[うん]転[てん]したほうが安[あん]全[ぜん]ですよ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 危（き）＋険（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="険">precipitous</kanji> place is all sheer drops and loose footing, so setting foot on one is plainly <vocabulary form="危険">dangerous</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な goes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯を見ながら自転車に乗るのは危険です。
example_sentences.english: Riding a bike while looking at your phone is dangerous.
example_sentences.furigana: 携[けい]帯[たい]を見[み]ながら自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]るのは危[き]険[けん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 警官が危険な場所を教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: A police officer told us which places were dangerous.
example_sentences.furigana: 警[けい]官[かん]が危[き]険[けん]な場[ば]所[しょ]を教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫にはこの薬は危険かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: This medicine might be dangerous for cats.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]にはこの薬[くすり]は危[き]険[けん]かもしれない。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <reading>wagon mama</reading> drags the family cart to whatever shop she fancies and never asks where anyone else wants to go. Putting your own way ahead of everyone else's is <vocabulary form="わがまま">selfish</vocabulary>, and that pushy <reading>わがまま</reading> sound carries the same trait.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子がわがままを言うので、スーパーに行くのは大変です。
example_sentences.english: My son throws fits, so going to the supermarket is a real ordeal.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]がわがままを言[い]うので、スーパーに行[い]くのは大[たい]変[へん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人はわがままで、いつもレストランを自分で選ぶ。
example_sentences.english: My partner is selfish and always picks the restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 恋[こい]人[びと]はわがままで、いつもレストランを自[じ]分[ぶん]で選[えら]ぶ。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日だけは私のわがままを聞いてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Just for today, could you let me have my way?
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]だけは私[わたし]のわがままを聞[き]いてくれませんか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 無（む）＋理（り）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A demand with <kanji form="無">nothing</kanji> behind it in the way of <kanji form="理">logic</kanji> cannot be argued for and cannot be met, which makes it <vocabulary form="無理">unreasonable / impossible</vocabulary>. As a な adjective, it needs な before any noun it modifies.

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間で漢字を三百覚えるのは無理だよ。
example_sentences.english: Memorizing three hundred kanji in one week is impossible.
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]で漢[かん]字[じ]を三[さん]百[びゃく]覚[おぼ]えるのは無[む]理[り]だよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪のときは無理して働かないほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: When you have a cold, you shouldn't push yourself to work.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]のときは無[む]理[り]して働[はたら]かないほうがいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 車が欲しいと言ったら、父に「無理だ」と言われた。
example_sentences.english: When I said I wanted a car, my dad told me, "No way."
example_sentences.furigana: 車[くるま]が欲[ほ]しいと言[い]ったら、父[ちち]に「無[む]理[り]だ」と言[い]われた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 苦（にが）＋手（て）.
items.mnemonic_text: A bitter (苦) hand (手): a weak point.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A task that brings your <kanji form="手">hand</kanji> nothing but <kanji form="苦">suffering</kanji> every time you try it is one you are <vocabulary form="苦手">bad at</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は朝早く起きるのが苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I'm bad at getting up early in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きるのが苦[にが]手[て]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は野菜が苦手だから、母は小さく切ってご飯に入れる。
example_sentences.english: My little brother doesn't like vegetables, so Mom cuts them small and hides them in his rice.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は野[や]菜[さい]が苦[にが]手[て]だから、母[はは]は小[ちい]さく切[き]ってご飯[はん]に入[い]れる。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い冬が苦手なので、来年は南の町に住みたい。
example_sentences.english: I can't stand cold winters, so next year I want to live in a town down south.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い冬[ふゆ]が苦[にが]手[て]なので、来[らい]年[ねん]は南[みなみ]の町[まち]に住[す]みたい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 自（じ）＋由（ゆう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When your <kanji form="自">self</kanji> is the only <kanji form="由">reason</kanji> you need for what you do, you have <vocabulary form="自由">freedom</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この図書館の本は自由に読んでもいいです。
example_sentences.english: You're free to read any of the books in this library.
example_sentences.furigana: この図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]の本[ほん]は自[じ]由[ゆう]に読[よ]んでもいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は予定がないので、自由な時間がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: I have no plans this weekend, so I have lots of free time.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は予[よ]定[てい]がないので、自[じ]由[ゆう]な時[じ]間[かん]がたくさんあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に入ってから、自由に旅行に行けるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: Since starting university, I've been able to travel wherever I like.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]に入[はい]ってから、自[じ]由[ゆう]に旅[りょ]行[こう]に行[い]けるようになりました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 届（とど）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="届">reach</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="届く">to reach</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean the same thing. With く on the end it is intransitive, so the parcel arrives on its own with no one delivering it.
items.reading_mnemonic: The runner tosses the parcel from the doorway and it skids across the tatami alone, stopping like a boat bumping <reading>to a dock</reading> right beside the body. That is <reading>とどく</reading>, a parcel managing <vocabulary form="届く">to reach</vocabulary> its place by itself.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の友人から大きい荷物が届きました。
example_sentences.english: A big package arrived from a friend abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の友[ゆう]人[じん]から大[おお]きい荷[に]物[もつ]が届[とど]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の上の箱に手が届かない。
example_sentences.english: I can't reach the box on top of the fridge.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の上[うえ]の箱[はこ]に手[て]が届[とど]かない。

example_sentences.japanese: 後ろの席まで先生の声が届かなかった。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's voice didn't carry to the back seats.
example_sentences.furigana: 後[うし]ろの席[せき]まで先[せん]生[せい]の声[こえ]が届[とど]かなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 届（とど）＋ける.
items.mnemonic_text: Reaching it out to someone: todokeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="届">deliver</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="届ける">to deliver</vocabulary> word are the same character with the same meaning. The ける ending makes it transitive, so now someone is carrying a parcel and handing it to you.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already learned 「とど」 from 届く, this word's intransitive partner, so its transitive form is simply <reading>とどける</reading> for <vocabulary form="届ける">to deliver</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 落とした財布を交番に届けました。
example_sentences.english: I took the wallet someone dropped to the police box.
example_sentences.furigana: 落[お]とした財[さい]布[ふ]を交[こう]番[ばん]に届[とど]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母の家に果物を届けに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to take some fruit over to my aunt's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]の家[いえ]に果物[くだもの]を届[とど]けに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この店は昼ご飯を会社まで届けてくれます。
example_sentences.english: This shop delivers lunch right to your office.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]は昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を会[かい]社[しゃ]まで届[とど]けてくれます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 治（なお）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: The body governing itself back to health: naoru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a fever or a sore throat <kanji form="治">calms down</kanji> and goes quiet on its own, with no one treating it, the body is starting to <vocabulary form="治る">recover</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Nao was stuck in bed a week with fever, then jogs onto the sports field and out-runs the whole class. The cheer of <reading>Nao rules</reading> again is <reading>なおる</reading>, the sound of a body that gets better on its own and <vocabulary form="治る">recovers</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 足が治ったら、また公園を走りたいです。
example_sentences.english: Once my leg heals, I want to run in the park again.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]が治[なお]ったら、また公[こう]園[えん]を走[はし]りたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の病気が治って、また元気に歩けるようになった。
example_sentences.english: The dog got over its illness and can walk around happily again.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の病[びょう]気[き]が治[なお]って、また元[げん]気[き]に歩[ある]けるようになった。

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間休んだのに、風邪がまだ治りません。
example_sentences.english: I rested for a whole week, but my cold still hasn't gone away.
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]休[やす]んだのに、風邪[かぜ]がまだ治[なお]りません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 伝（つた）＋わる.
items.mnemonic_text: The message passing along on its own: tsutawaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A message that will <kanji form="伝">go along</kanji> by itself, passed from mouth to mouth with no one carrying it, is one that comes <vocabulary form="伝わる">to be conveyed</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 伝 is 「つた」 from 伝える, so for a word <vocabulary form="伝わる">to be conveyed</vocabulary> across a crowd is <reading>つたわる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の気持ちは彼女に伝わったと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think my feelings got through to her.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の気[き]持[も]ちは彼[かの]女[じょ]に伝[つた]わったと思[おも]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 英語で話したのに、意味が全然伝わらなかった。
example_sentences.english: I spoke in English, but the meaning didn't come across at all.
example_sentences.furigana: 英[えい]語[ご]で話[はな]したのに、意[い]味[み]が全[ぜん]然[ぜん]伝[つた]わらなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: この町の伝統は親から子供に伝わります。
example_sentences.english: In this town, traditions are passed down from parents to children.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]の伝[でん]統[とう]は親[おや]から子[こ]供[ども]に伝[つた]わります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 見（み）＋つかる.
items.mnemonic_text: Something turns up to the eye: mitsukaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A missing sock drifts out into the open until a wandering eye on legs happens to <kanji form="見">see</kanji> it, and with no one searching for it that sock has come <vocabulary form="見つかる">to be found</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 見 is 「み」 from 見る, so for a lost thing <vocabulary form="見つかる">to be found</vocabulary> at last is <reading>みつかる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 無くした財布が交番で見つかりました。
example_sentences.english: The wallet I lost turned up at the police box.
example_sentences.furigana: 無[な]くした財[さい]布[ふ]が交[こう]番[ばん]で見[み]つかりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に泊まる安いホテルが見つからなくて困っています。
example_sentences.english: I can't find a cheap hotel for the weekend, and I'm stuck.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に泊[と]まる安[やす]いホテルが見[み]つからなくて困[こま]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄にいい仕事が見つかったらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard my older brother found a good job.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]にいい仕[し]事[ごと]が見[み]つかったらしい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 決（き）＋まる.
items.mnemonic_text: The levee breaks on its own: kimaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="決">decide</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="決まる">to be decided</vocabulary> word are the same word. This form just means the matter settles on its own, with nobody there to make the call.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kiki</reading> the tree spirit watches the water drop leave the brush and the hooked stroke swing. Once neither can be pulled back, she sighs <reading>きまる</reading>, for the matter has come <vocabulary form="決まる">to be decided</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月の旅行の場所がまだ決まらない。
example_sentences.english: We still haven't settled where next month's trip is going.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]の旅[りょ]行[こう]の場[ば]所[しょ]がまだ決[き]まらない。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議は金曜日の午後に決まりました。
example_sentences.english: The meeting has been set for Friday afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]は金[きん]曜[よう]日[び]の午[ご]後[ご]に決[き]まりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験の結果で、入る大学が決まる。
example_sentences.english: Your exam results decide which university you get into.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]の結[けっ]果[か]で、入[はい]る大[だい]学[がく]が決[き]まる。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 肉（にく）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Overnight, every shelf in Koichi's konbini is restocked with nothing but <vocabulary>meat</vocabulary>. Cold steaks fill the onigiri rack, sausages crowd the drinks fridge, and a slab of ribs beeps through the till.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は肉を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat meat.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は肉[にく]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: この肉はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: This meat is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: この肉[にく]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は肉を買いました。
example_sentences.english: My mother bought meat.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は肉[にく]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 米（こめ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The hard little grains straight from the sack, before a drop of water or any heat reaches them, are <vocabulary>uncooked rice</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Old Mei pours the hard grains straight from the sack and drags a bamboo <reading>comb</reading> through them, muttering 「<reading>こめ</reading>」 before any water or heat touches her <vocabulary form="米">uncooked rice</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は米を買います。
example_sentences.english: My mother buys rice.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は米[こめ]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: この米は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This rice is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この米[こめ]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 料理に米を使います。
example_sentences.english: I use rice for cooking.
example_sentences.furigana: 料[りょう]理[り]に米[こめ]を使[つか]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 机（つくえ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Shove a plain table into the corner and aim a lamp at it, and now people only sit there to write, never to eat. A table you work at instead of dine at is a <vocabulary>desk</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A pigeon wanders into Sei's school, heads straight for the one flat surface with drawers and a lamp, and settles down <reading>to coo, eh</reading>. The writing table it picked is a <vocabulary>desk</vocabulary>, and it has left feathers all across the <reading>つくえ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は机に座ります。
example_sentences.english: I sit on the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は机[つくえ]に座[すわ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 机で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I read a book at the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 机[つくえ]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: この机は高いです。
example_sentences.english: This desk is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: この机[つくえ]は高[たか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 足（あし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>foot / leg</kanji> kanji is exactly the <vocabulary>foot / leg</vocabulary> word, one character doing both jobs, so the meaning never changes.
items.reading_mnemonic: The legs skid to such a hard stop that the <vocabulary form="足">foot</vocabulary> at the end comes up grey and <reading>ashy</reading> with dust, and the mouth on top yelps 「<reading>あし</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 足で学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to school on foot.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]で学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫の足を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the cat's paws.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]の足[あし]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 足が寒いです。
example_sentences.english: My feet are cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]が寒[さむ]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 声（こえ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A ventriloquist's dummy sits alone on the stage and starts talking. The sound has to come from somewhere, and that somewhere, a throat pushing air, is a <vocabulary>voice</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The dummy alone on the stage calls <reading>cooee</reading> to the empty seats, one long 「<reading>こえ</reading>」 with no throat behind it, and still the hall fills with a <vocabulary form="声">voice</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の声を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I heard his voice.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の声[こえ]を聞[き]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の声がいいです。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's voice is nice.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の声[こえ]がいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜、猫の声を聞きます。
example_sentences.english: At night, I hear a cat's voice.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]、猫[ねこ]の声[こえ]を聞[き]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 卵（たまご）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The smooth white thing in the carton that cracks if you look at it wrong and turns into breakfast the moment it hits a hot pan is an <vocabulary>egg</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The cook cracks a smooth white <vocabulary form="卵">egg</vocabulary> from the carton into the hot pan and yells 「<reading>たまご</reading>」, <reading>tomato, go</reading>, as the red slices slide in beside it.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ごはんに卵を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat eggs for breakfast.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]ごはんに卵[たまご]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: この卵はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: This egg is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: この卵[たまご]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は卵を三つ買いました。
example_sentences.english: My mom bought three eggs.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は卵[たまご]を三[みっ]つ買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 町（まち）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>town</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>town</vocabulary> word are one and the same, so the meaning carries straight over.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei strikes a <reading>match</reading> on the dark mountain trail, and the flame shows her she is standing in the main square of a whole <vocabulary>town</vocabulary> that was empty fields at dusk. She keeps the 「<reading>まち</reading>」 lit so it cannot slip back into the dark.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に町へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to town this weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に町[まち]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 町でパンを買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought bread in town.
example_sentences.furigana: 町[まち]でパンを買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この町の公園は楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: The park in this town is fun.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]の公[こう]園[えん]は楽[たの]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 角（かど）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every <vocabulary>corner</vocabulary> in the house is the spot where two walls give up going straight and slam into each other at a hard right angle.
items.reading_mnemonic: Movers swing an old <reading>car door</reading> through the house and jam it where two walls slam together at a hard right angle, and it sticks with a 「<reading>かど</reading>」 in that <vocabulary form="角">corner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の角で友達を待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I wait for my friend at the station corner.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の角[かど]で友[とも]達[だち]を待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 角の店でパンを買います。
example_sentences.english: I buy bread at the shop on the corner.
example_sentences.furigana: 角[かど]の店[みせ]でパンを買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園の角に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the corner of the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]の角[かど]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 牛（ぎゅう）＋乳（にゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>cow</kanji> makes far more of the white stuff than her one calf could ever drink, so the rest gets bottled and sold as <vocabulary>milk</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯に牛乳を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink milk with breakfast.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]に牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: この牛乳はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: This milk is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: この牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は牛乳を買いました。
example_sentences.english: My mom bought milk.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 生（せい）＋徒（と）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>life</kanji> still in its <kanji>junior</kanji> stage, trailing a few steps behind the teacher, is a <vocabulary>pupil</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の弟は生徒です。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother is a pupil.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の弟[おとうと]は生[せい]徒[と]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒と話します。
example_sentences.english: The teacher talks with the pupils.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は生[せい]徒[と]と話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒は毎朝学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: The pupils go to school every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 生[せい]徒[と]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — お＋酒（さけ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Leave cooked rice and clean river water together in a warm, dark cupboard for a few weeks. The mixture quietly ferments into <vocabulary>alcohol / sake</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Old <reading>O'Sakey</reading> opens the warm dark cupboard after three weeks, sniffs the fermented rice and river water inside, and raises a cup to 「<reading>おさけ</reading>」, his <vocabulary form="お酒">sake</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達とお酒を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink alcohol with my friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]とお酒[さけ]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought some alcohol.
example_sentences.furigana: お酒[さけ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: このお酒はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: This sake is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: このお酒[さけ]はおいしいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 魚（さかな）.
items.mnemonic_text: The swimmer on your plate: sakana.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>fish</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>fish</vocabulary> word are the same, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ana wades into the flooded rice field and scoops the crouching <vocabulary form="魚">fish</vocabulary> up in her wet <reading>sock</reading>, so <reading>sock-Ana</reading>'s catch, 「<reading>さかな</reading>」, goes straight into the pan over the fire.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は魚を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I'm eating fish today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は魚[さかな]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: この魚はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: This fish is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: この魚[さかな]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は魚を買いました。
example_sentences.english: My mother bought fish.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は魚[さかな]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — お＋菓（か）＋子（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Cakes</kanji> come in adult size, but shrink each one to <kanji>child</kanji> size and you can eat twelve without comment. A bowl of those miniatures is <vocabulary>sweets / snacks</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このお菓子はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: These sweets are delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: このお菓[か]子[し]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はお菓子を買います。
example_sentences.english: I'll buy some snacks today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]はお菓[か]子[し]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹とお菓子を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat snacks with my younger sister.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]とお菓[か]子[し]を食[た]べます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 郵（ゆう）＋便（びん）＋局（きょく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>facility</kanji> that handles <kanji>mail</kanji> and refuses to handle anything else is a <vocabulary>post office</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、郵便局に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the post office today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便局はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the post office?
example_sentences.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便局で彼女を待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for her at the post office.
example_sentences.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]で彼[かの]女[じょ]を待[ま]ちます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 友（とも）＋達（だち）. Rendaku: 達 たち → だち.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two hands closing together as a <kanji>friend</kanji> finally <kanji>reach</kanji> each other, and that arrival is what makes a <vocabulary>friend</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は友達と映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は友[とも]達[だち]と映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいい友達です。
example_sentences.english: She is a good friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はいい友[とも]達[だち]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に友達と遊びます。
example_sentences.english: I hang out with friends on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に友[とも]達[だち]と遊[あそ]びます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 喫（きっ）＋茶（さ）＋店（てん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 喫 きつ → きっ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set aside a whole room where the only thing to do is <kanji>drink</kanji> from a steaming <kanji>tea</kanji> cup and watch the afternoon crawl past. That room is a <vocabulary>coffee shop</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は喫茶店でコーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink coffee at a coffee shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]でコーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と喫茶店に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went to a coffee shop with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: この喫茶店のお茶はおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: The tea at this coffee shop is delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: この喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]のお茶[ちゃ]はおいしいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 空（くう）＋港（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Swap the sea out of a <kanji>harbor</kanji> for a stretch of <kanji>empty</kanji> sky, and the boats that dock there become planes at an <vocabulary>airport</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the airport?
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、空港に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the airport tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、空[くう]港[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 空港でお茶を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I'll drink tea at the airport.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]でお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 道（みち）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>road</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>road / street</vocabulary> word are the exact same character, so they mean the exact same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Mitch</reading> cranes his long neck to stare down the <vocabulary form="道">road</vocabulary> before his feet will advance a single step, and only then mutters 「<reading>みち</reading>」 and walks it.

example_sentences.japanese: この道を行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'll take this road.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]を行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 道はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the road?
example_sentences.furigana: 道[みち]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と道で会います。
example_sentences.english: I'll meet my friend on the street.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と道[みち]で会[あ]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 傘（かさ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pop open a dome of cloth on a thin pole and hold it overhead, and the rain drums on the fabric instead of on you. That portable roof is an <vocabulary>umbrella</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The old angler at the riverbank refuses to <reading>cast a</reading> line in the rain until he has popped open his patched <vocabulary>umbrella</vocabulary>. He calls that leaky dome on a stick his <reading>かさ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は傘を使います。
example_sentences.english: I'll use an umbrella today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は傘[かさ]を使[つか]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 店で傘を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought an umbrella at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[みせ]で傘[かさ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: その傘は安いです。
example_sentences.english: That umbrella is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: その傘[かさ]は安[やす]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 椅（い）＋子（す）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Shrink a grand throne until it seats just one ordinary person and what is left is the throne's <kanji>child</kanji>. That small single seat with a back is a <vocabulary>chair</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこの椅子に座ります。
example_sentences.english: I sit in this chair.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はこの椅[い]子[す]に座[すわ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 店で椅子を二つ買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought two chairs at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[みせ]で椅[い]子[す]を二[ふた]つ買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの椅子は高いです。
example_sentences.english: That chair over there is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: あの椅[い]子[す]は高[たか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — おなか cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of お腹.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The soft drum you pat after a big lunch, the part that growls in a silent room, is your <vocabulary>stomach / belly</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: One more dumpling drifts toward the sumo trainee and he waves it off, both palms flat on his <vocabulary>stomach / belly</vocabulary>: <reading>oh, not a</reading>nother bite. The groan lands as 「<reading>おなか</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: ここが私のお腹です。
example_sentences.english: This is my stomach.
example_sentences.furigana: ここが私[わたし]のお腹[なか]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんのお腹を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the baby's belly.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんのお腹[なか]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫のお腹はいいです。
example_sentences.english: The cat's belly feels nice.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]のお腹[なか]はいいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 塩（しお）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One shake of the white grit makes hot chips worth eating. The same pinch stings like fire in a small cut, because it is <vocabulary>salt</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A girl shakes <vocabulary form="塩">salt</vocabulary> over her hot chips, a pinch lands in the cut on her thumb, and the sting pulls a sharp 「<reading>しお</reading>」 out of her, <reading>she-oh</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 塩を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought some salt.
example_sentences.furigana: 塩[しお]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この塩は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This salt is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この塩[しお]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は毎日塩を使います。
example_sentences.english: My mom uses salt every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は毎[まい]日[にち]塩[しお]を使[つか]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 辞（じ）＋書（しょ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When you <kanji>write</kanji> down every <kanji>word</kanji> there is and put them in order, the book you end up with is a <vocabulary>dictionary</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は辞書を使います。
example_sentences.english: I use a dictionary.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は辞[じ]書[しょ]を使[つか]います。

example_sentences.japanese: この辞書は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This dictionary is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この辞[じ]書[しょ]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は辞書を買いました。
example_sentences.english: My friend bought a dictionary.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]は辞[じ]書[しょ]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 鼻（はな）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single vending machine at the top of the mountain trail sells nothing but tissues, because everyone who finishes that climb arrives with a streaming <vocabulary>nose</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, a hiker with a <reading>banana</reading>-sized <vocabulary form="鼻">nose</vocabulary> buys every tissue in the vending machine and honks 「<reading>はな</reading>」 into each one.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の鼻はいい。
example_sentences.english: Dogs have a good nose.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の鼻[はな]はいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の鼻が寒い。
example_sentences.english: My nose is cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の鼻[はな]が寒[さむ]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの鼻を見る。
example_sentences.english: I look at the baby's nose.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんの鼻[はな]を見[み]る。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 髪（かみ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The stuff that clogs the shower drain and slips out of every ponytail by noon is <vocabulary>hair</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Cammy</reading> fishes a fat wet clump of <vocabulary form="髪">hair</vocabulary> out of the clogged shower drain, then feels her ponytail slipping loose again and sighs 「<reading>かみ</reading>」.
items.description: 髪 is specifically the hair on your head. Hair elsewhere on the body, or an animal's coat, is a different word, so do not stretch 髪 to cover it.

example_sentences.japanese: 母の髪はいいです。
example_sentences.english: My mother's hair looks nice.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]の髪[かみ]はいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は妹の髪を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at my little sister's hair.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は妹[いもうと]の髪[かみ]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は髪はどうですか。
example_sentences.english: How does your hair look today?
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は髪[かみ]はどうですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 銀（ぎん）＋行（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When you run low on <kanji>silver</kanji>, you <kanji>go</kanji> to one particular crossroads in town. That corner building is the <vocabulary>bank</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は銀行に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the bank.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は銀[ぎん]行[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the bank?
example_sentences.furigana: 銀[ぎん]行[こう]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は明日銀行で待ちます。
example_sentences.english: He's waiting at the bank tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は明日[あした]銀[ぎん]行[こう]で待[ま]ちます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 頭（あたま）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single body part that holds every thought you have, sits highest of all, and takes the worst sunburn every summer is your <vocabulary>head</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Basking upright on a sunny rock all summer, an <reading>otter mama</reading> burns only her 「<reading>あたま</reading>」, the highest spot on her body, her peeling <vocabulary form="頭">head</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫の頭を見た。
example_sentences.english: I looked at the cat's head.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]の頭[あたま]を見[み]た。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の頭は寒い。
example_sentences.english: My head is cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の頭[あたま]は寒[さむ]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は毎日頭を使う。
example_sentences.english: He uses his head every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は毎[まい]日[にち]頭[あたま]を使[つか]う。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 砂（さ）＋糖（とう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Tip the bag and it hisses out like dry <kanji>sand</kanji>. A spoonful of that pale grit turns your coffee sweet, so it has to be <vocabulary>sugar</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーと砂糖を買います。
example_sentences.english: I'll buy coffee and sugar.
example_sentences.furigana: コーヒーと砂[さ]糖[とう]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: この砂糖は安いです。
example_sentences.english: This sugar is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この砂[さ]糖[とう]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は砂糖を使います。
example_sentences.english: She uses sugar.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は砂[さ]糖[とう]を使[つか]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 橋（はし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The left riverbank and the right riverbank are tired of shouting across the water, so a long plank gets laid from one to the other. You walk over on that plank, and it is a <vocabulary>bridge</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A ferryman on the riverbank keeps warning that the current is <reading>harsh</reading>, so the villagers stop listening and build <reading>はし</reading> to cross on dry feet. That word now means the <vocabulary>bridge</vocabulary> that ended his job.

example_sentences.japanese: あの橋は高いです。
example_sentences.english: That bridge over there is tall.
example_sentences.furigana: あの橋[はし]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 橋で友達を待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for my friend at the bridge.
example_sentences.furigana: 橋[はし]で友[とも]達[だち]を待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、公園の橋に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Today I'm going to the bridge in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、公[こう]園[えん]の橋[はし]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 顔（かお）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Koichi hangs a mirror by the onigiri shelf so no customer walks past the beeping till without seeing their own <vocabulary>face</vocabulary> first.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>cow</reading> wanders into Koichi's konbini, stops at the mirror by the onigiri shelf and moos 「<reading>かお</reading>」 at the big hairy <vocabulary form="顔">face</vocabulary> staring back.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の顔を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw my friend's face.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の顔[かお]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: この写真は誰の顔ですか。
example_sentences.english: Whose face is in this photo?
example_sentences.furigana: この写[しゃ]真[しん]は誰[だれ]の顔[かお]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの顔はいいです。
example_sentences.english: The baby's face is lovely.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんの顔[かお]はいいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 決（き）＋める.
items.mnemonic_text: Breaking through to a decision: kimeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="決">decide</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="決める">to decide</vocabulary> word are the same word. This form adds a person to the scene: you are the one who makes the call and fixes the outcome.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 決 is 「き」 from 決まる, so for you <vocabulary form="決める">to decide</vocabulary> the outcome yourself is <reading>きめる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯に何を作るか、まだ決めていません。
example_sentences.english: I haven't decided what to make for dinner yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]に何[なに]を作[つく]るか、まだ決[き]めていません。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は長い時間考えて、黒い靴に決めました。
example_sentences.english: After thinking for ages, my little sister went with the black shoes.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は長[なが]い時[じ]間[かん]考[かんが]えて、黒[くろ]い靴[くつ]に決[き]めました。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫と話して、息子の名前を決めました。
example_sentences.english: My husband and I talked it over and chose our son's name.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]と話[はな]して、息子[むすこ]の名[な]前[まえ]を決[き]めました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 続（つづ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Thread sold onward without a break: tsuzuku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="続">continue</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="続く">to continue</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form that runs on by itself, the thread unrolling off the spool with no one feeding it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 続 is 「つづ」 from 続き, so for a spell of good weather <vocabulary form="続く">to continue</vocabulary> on its own is <reading>つづく</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話の話が二時間も続いて、耳が痛くなった。
example_sentences.english: The phone call went on for two whole hours, and my ear started to hurt.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]の話[はなし]が二[に]時[じ]間[かん]も続[つづ]いて、耳[みみ]が痛[いた]くなった。

example_sentences.japanese: この道は海まで続きます。
example_sentences.english: This road runs all the way to the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は海[うみ]まで続[つづ]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日が続くので、冷たいお茶をたくさん飲んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The hot days keep coming, so I'm drinking lots of cold tea.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]い日[ひ]が続[つづ]くので、冷[つめ]たいお茶[ちゃ]をたくさん飲[の]んでいます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 続（つづ）＋ける.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="続">continue</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="続ける">to continue</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form with a hand on the spool, someone pulling more thread off on purpose.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 続 is 「つづ」 from 続き, so for a worker <vocabulary form="続ける">to continue</vocabulary> a task without a break is <reading>つづける</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は八十歳ですが、今も仕事を続けています。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother is eighty, but she's still working.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は八[はち]十[じゅう]歳[さい]ですが、今[いま]も仕[し]事[ごと]を続[つづ]けています。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強は毎日続けたほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should keep up your Japanese study every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]の勉[べん]強[きょう]は毎[まい]日[にち]続[つづ]けたほうがいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが朝まで泣き続けて、誰も寝られなかった。
example_sentences.english: The baby kept crying until morning, and nobody got any sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんが朝[あさ]まで泣[な]き続[つづ]けて、誰[だれ]も寝[ね]られなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 増（ふ）＋える.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="増">increase</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="増える">to increase</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form that climbs on its own, the mound rising past the signpost with no one piling it up.
items.reading_mnemonic: The mound beside the signpost began as only a <reading>few</reading> loads of earth, yet each dawn it stands taller with no one piling it on. Watching it <vocabulary form="増える">increase</vocabulary> by itself, you whisper <reading>ふえる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏になると、公園に来る人が増えます。
