items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 乗（の）＋れる.
items.mnemonic_text: The potential form of noru: able to ride.
items.meaning_mnemonic: This word adds nothing to its kanji: <vocabulary form="乗れる">can ride</vocabulary> is the <kanji form="乗">ride</kanji> kanji you have already met, unchanged.
items.reading_mnemonic: The 「の」 in this word comes straight from 乗る, so <vocabulary form="乗れる">can ride</vocabulary> simply becomes <reading>のれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は六歳で自転車に乗れるようになった。
example_sentences.english: My little sister learned to ride a bike at six.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は六[ろく]歳[さい]で自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]れるようになった。

example_sentences.japanese: 荷物が多くて、バスに乗れませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I had too much luggage to get on the bus.
example_sentences.furigana: 荷[に]物[もつ]が多[おお]くて、バスに乗[の]れませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: この車は七人乗れます。
example_sentences.english: This car seats seven people.
example_sentences.furigana: この車[くるま]は七[なな]人[にん]乗[の]れます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 行（い）＋かせる.
items.mnemonic_text: The causative of iku: making someone go.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At its core this word is still the <kanji form="行">go</kanji> kanji. The tail added on means you <vocabulary form="行かせる">make or let someone go</vocabulary>, whether they want to or not.
items.reading_mnemonic: Same 「い」 as in 行く, so <vocabulary form="行かせる">to make/let go</vocabulary> keeps that opening sound and becomes <reading>いかせる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が強いので、子供を一人で学校に行かせたくない。
example_sentences.english: The rain is heavy, so I don't want to let my kid go to school alone.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が強[つよ]いので、子[こ]供[ども]を一人[ひとり]で学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]かせたくない。

example_sentences.japanese: 会社は来年、夫を外国の工場に行かせるそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear the company is sending my husband to a factory abroad next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]は来[らい]年[ねん]、夫[おっと]を外[がい]国[こく]の工[こう]場[じょう]に行[い]かせるそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 気分が悪いなら、娘を病院に行かせましょう。
example_sentences.english: If she feels sick, let's send our daughter to the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 気[き]分[ぶん]が悪[わる]いなら、娘[むすめ]を病[びょう]院[いん]に行[い]かせましょう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 食（た）＋べさせる.
items.mnemonic_text: The causative of taberu: making someone eat.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Underneath, this is only the <kanji form="食">eat</kanji> kanji again. The extra endings shift it to mean you <vocabulary form="食べさせる">make or let another person eat</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The 「た」 is the one 食べる gave you, so <vocabulary form="食べさせる">to make/let eat</vocabulary> starts the same and runs on to <reading>たべさせる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は毎朝、弟に野菜を食べさせます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning, my mother makes my little brother eat vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]、弟[おとうと]に野[や]菜[さい]を食[た]べさせます。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫に人の食べ物を食べさせないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't feed the cat people food.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]に人[ひと]の食[た]べ物[もの]を食[た]べさせないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんにスプーンでご飯を食べさせた。
example_sentences.english: I fed the baby rice with a spoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんにスプーンでご飯[はん]を食[た]べさせた。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: The causative of yaru: making someone do it.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Run a <reading>yard sale</reading> and you get one afternoon to <vocabulary form="やらせる">make or let someone else do</vocabulary> every bit of the lifting and pricing. Handing the whole driveway to other hands like that is <reading>やらせる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒に同じ問題を三回やらせた。
example_sentences.english: The teacher made the students do the same problem three times.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は生[せい]徒[と]に同[おな]じ問[もん]題[だい]を三[さん]回[かい]やらせた。

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい仕事ですが、新しい店員にやらせることにしました。
example_sentences.english: It's a hard job, but I've decided to let the new clerk do it.
example_sentences.furigana: 難[むずか]しい仕[し]事[ごと]ですが、新[あたら]しい店[てん]員[いん]にやらせることにしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は自分の宿題をいつも僕にやらせる。
example_sentences.english: My big brother always makes me do his homework.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は自[じ]分[ぶん]の宿[しゅく]題[だい]をいつも僕[ぼく]にやらせる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 待（ま）＋たされる.
items.mnemonic_text: The causative-passive of matsu: being kept waiting.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="待">wait</kanji> kanji sits at the centre of this word unchanged. The endings stacked after it turn plain waiting into <vocabulary form="待たされる">being made to wait</vocabulary> by someone who will not hurry.
items.reading_mnemonic: You learned 「ま」 back in 待つ, so the drawn-out <vocabulary form="待たされる">to be made to wait</vocabulary> is still just <reading>またされる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行の窓口で一時間も待たされた。
example_sentences.english: I was kept waiting a whole hour at the bank counter.
example_sentences.furigana: 銀[ぎん]行[こう]の窓[まど]口[ぐち]で一[いち]時[じ]間[かん]も待[ま]たされた。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は約束に遅れるから、私はよく待たされる。
example_sentences.english: She's always late for our plans, so I often end up waiting.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は約[やく]束[そく]に遅[おく]れるから、私[わたし]はよく待[ま]たされる。

example_sentences.japanese: 雪で電車が止まって、寒い外で待たされた。
example_sentences.english: The snow stopped the trains, and we were left waiting out in the cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 雪[ゆき]で電[でん]車[しゃ]が止[と]まって、寒[さむ]い外[そと]で待[ま]たされた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 叱（しか）＋られる.
items.mnemonic_text: The passive of shikaru: on the receiving end of a scolding.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Knock a jar off Grandma Kane's shelf and every cat goes still while she turns and scolds you in a long, rising voice. Standing there and taking all of it is what it means <vocabulary form="叱られる">to be scolded</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 「しか」 from 叱る, so the version done to you, <vocabulary form="叱られる">to be scolded</vocabulary>, is <reading>しかられる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜遅く帰ったら、父に叱られた。
example_sentences.english: I got home late at night and got scolded by my dad.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]遅[おそ]く帰[かえ]ったら、父[ちち]に叱[しか]られた。

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で大きい声で話して、叱られました。
example_sentences.english: I talked loudly in the library and got told off.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で大[おお]きい声[こえ]で話[はな]して、叱[しか]られました。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬がテーブルの肉を食べて、叱られている。
example_sentences.english: The dog ate the meat off the table and is getting scolded.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]がテーブルの肉[にく]を食[た]べて、叱[しか]られている。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 褒（ほ）＋められる.
items.mnemonic_text: The passive of homeru: receiving praise.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand a drawing to the teacher and she holds it up to the whole class, naming every good line in it. Having your work lifted up for the whole room to see is what it means <vocabulary form="褒められる">to be praised</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 「ほ」 from 褒める, so the same thing coming back at you, <vocabulary form="褒められる">to be praised</vocabulary>, is <reading>ほめられる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理が上手だと、祖母に褒められた。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother praised me for being a good cook.
example_sentences.furigana: 料[りょう]理[り]が上手[じょうず]だと、祖[そ]母[ぼ]に褒[ほ]められた。

example_sentences.japanese: 褒められたら、誰でも嬉しいです。
example_sentences.english: Anyone is happy when they're praised.
example_sentences.furigana: 褒[ほ]められたら、誰[だれ]でも嬉[うれ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の絵が美術の授業で褒められた。
example_sentences.english: My painting got praised in art class.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の絵[え]が美[び]術[じゅつ]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]で褒[ほ]められた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 泣（な）＋かれる.
items.mnemonic_text: The passive of naku: suffering from someone's crying.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The person beside you suddenly bursts out <kanji form="泣">crying</kanji>, and now their misery is your problem to deal with. Being left holding someone else's tears like that is being <vocabulary form="泣かれる">cried at</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 「な」 from 泣く, so that same crying aimed at you, <vocabulary form="泣かれる">to be cried at (adversity)</vocabulary>, is <reading>なかれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の中で赤ちゃんに泣かれて、困りました。
example_sentences.english: A baby started crying right next to me on the train, and I didn't know what to do.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]車[しゃ]の中[なか]で赤[あか]ちゃんに泣[な]かれて、困[こま]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹に泣かれたので、お菓子を半分あげました。
example_sentences.english: My little sister burst into tears, so I gave her half my snacks.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]に泣[な]かれたので、お菓[か]子[し]を半[はん]分[ぶん]あげました。

example_sentences.japanese: 空港で母に泣かれて、少し恥ずかしかったです。
example_sentences.english: My mom cried at the airport, and I was a little embarrassed.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]で母[はは]に泣[な]かれて、少[すこ]し恥[は]ずかしかったです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 殺（ころ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: A blow (殳) striking down: to kill.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Yank the wrong lever on the old mower and the motor goes quiet for good under your hands. Ending a running thing on purpose like that is what it means <vocabulary form="殺す">to kill</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Yank the wrong lever on the old mower in the middle of its roaring <reading>chorus</reading>, and the motor goes quiet under your hands for good: <reading>ころす</reading>, to <vocabulary form="殺す">kill</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で声を殺して笑いました。
example_sentences.english: I laughed in the library, trying not to make a sound.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で声[こえ]を殺[ころ]して笑[わら]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋の蚊を殺すまで、寝ることができなかった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't sleep until I'd killed the mosquito in my room.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]の蚊[か]を殺[ころ]すまで、寝[ね]ることができなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は「動物を殺してはいけない」とよく言っていました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather often said you must never kill animals.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は「動[どう]物[ぶつ]を殺[ころ]してはいけない」とよく言[い]っていました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 殺（ころ）＋される.
items.mnemonic_text: The passive of korosu: to be killed.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A beetle wanders onto the train track at exactly the wrong second. The 8:15 does not slow down, and being the one it happens to is <vocabulary form="殺される">to be killed</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 殺 is 「ころ」 from 殺す, the verb you first met it in, so <vocabulary form="殺される">to be killed</vocabulary> is <reading>ころされる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日見た映画では、最初に医者が殺されました。
example_sentences.english: In the movie I saw yesterday, the doctor is the first one killed.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]見[み]た映[えい]画[が]では、最[さい]初[しょ]に医[い]者[しゃ]が殺[ころ]されました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄のカメラを壊したので、殺されるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: I broke my brother's camera, so he might just kill me.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]のカメラを壊[こわ]したので、殺[ころ]されるかもしれません。

example_sentences.japanese: その男の人は殺されたと警官が言いました。
example_sentences.english: The police officer said the man had been killed.
example_sentences.furigana: その男[おとこ]の人[ひと]は殺[ころ]されたと警[けい]官[かん]が言[い]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 出（で）＋かける.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Climbing out over the box rim is only the <kanji form="出">exit</kanji>. Once your feet hit the road and you keep walking, that is <vocabulary form="出かける">to go out / head out</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 出 is 「で」 from 出る, the verb it first showed up in, so <vocabulary form="出かける">to go out / head out</vocabulary> is <reading>でかける</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日は雨だったので、どこにも出かけませんでした。
example_sentences.english: It rained on Sunday, so I didn't go out anywhere.
example_sentences.furigana: 日[にち]曜[よう]日[び]は雨[あめ]だったので、どこにも出[で]かけませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は毎朝、近くの公園へ出かけます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning my grandmother heads out to the park nearby.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]、近[ちか]くの公[こう]園[えん]へ出[で]かけます。

example_sentences.japanese: 出かける前に、窓を閉めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please close the windows before you head out.
example_sentences.furigana: 出[で]かける前[まえ]に、窓[まど]を閉[し]めてください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 取（と）＋り＋掛（か）＋かる.
items.mnemonic_text: Taking (取り) hold (掛かる) of a task: to begin work.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You get a grip on the job and <kanji form="掛">hang</kanji> your whole weight from it, the rude fast way you would <kanji form="取">take</kanji> hold of someone by the ear. Latching on and leaning in like that is <vocabulary form="取り掛かる">to set about (a task)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯の後で、すぐ宿題に取り掛かりました。
example_sentences.english: Right after dinner, I got straight to work on my homework.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]の後[あと]で、すぐ宿[しゅく]題[だい]に取[と]り掛[か]かりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 来週から新しい本に取り掛かるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I'm planning to start on a new book next week.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]週[しゅう]から新[あたら]しい本[ほん]に取[と]り掛[か]かるつもりです。

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来るので、夫は午後から料理に取り掛かりました。
example_sentences.english: Guests were coming, so my husband started on the cooking in the afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さんが来[く]るので、夫[おっと]は午[ご]後[ご]から料[りょう]理[り]に取[と]り掛[か]かりました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 持（も）＋ち＋帰（かえ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Holding (持ち) and returning (帰る): to take away.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="持">hold</kanji> on the warm food box never loosens the whole walk home, right up to the moment you <kanji form="帰">return</kanji> through your own door. Carrying your meal back that way is <vocabulary form="持ち帰る">to take home / take out</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 残った食べ物を持ち帰ってもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Is it okay if I take the leftover food home?
example_sentences.furigana: 残[のこ]った食[た]べ物[もの]を持[も]ち帰[かえ]ってもいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は家に持ち帰らないようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I try not to bring work home.
example_sentences.furigana: 仕[し]事[ごと]は家[いえ]に持[も]ち帰[かえ]らないようにしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 山で使った物は、全部持ち帰りましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's take everything we used on the mountain back home with us.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]で使[つか]った物[もの]は、全[ぜん]部[ぶ]持[も]ち帰[かえ]りましょう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 連（つ）＋れて＋行（い）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Bringing (連れて) someone along as you go (行く).
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="行">go</kanji> off down the crossroads with your little brother gripped by the sleeve so he cannot peel away. Setting out with a person fastened to your side like that is <vocabulary form="連れて行く">to take (a person) along</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏になったら、娘を海へ連れて行くと約束しました。
example_sentences.english: I promised my daughter I'd take her to the sea when summer comes.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]になったら、娘[むすめ]を海[うみ]へ連[つ]れて行[い]くと約[やく]束[そく]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬を店の中に連れて行くことはできません。
example_sentences.english: You can't take dogs inside the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]を店[みせ]の中[なか]に連[つ]れて行[い]くことはできません。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達を駅の近くのいい喫茶店に連れて行くことにしました。
example_sentences.english: I've decided to take my friend to a nice coffee shop near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]を駅[えき]の近[ちか]くのいい喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]に連[つ]れて行[い]くことにしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 連（つ）＋れて＋来（く）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Bringing (連れて) someone as you come (来る).
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="連">lead</kanji> a nervous friend up the path by the hand as the two of you <kanji form="来">come</kanji> toward the house. Turning up with an extra person beside you is <vocabulary form="連れて来る">to bring (a person)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が恋人を家に連れて来ることになりました。
example_sentences.english: It turns out my son is bringing his girlfriend home.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]が恋[こい]人[びと]を家[いえ]に連[つ]れて来[く]ることになりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議に、他の会社の人を連れて来るつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I'm planning to bring someone from another company to tomorrow's meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の会[かい]議[ぎ]に、他[た]の会[かい]社[しゃ]の人[ひと]を連[つ]れて来[く]るつもりです。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の猫は、よく小さい猫を三匹連れて来る。
example_sentences.english: The neighbor's cat often shows up trailing three little kittens.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の猫[ねこ]は、よく小[ちい]さい猫[ねこ]を三[さん]匹[ひき]連[つ]れて来[く]る。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 持（も）＋って＋来（く）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Holding (持って) something as you come (来る).
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="持">hold</kanji> stays locked around the umbrella as you <kanji form="来">come</kanji> back in through the door. Arriving with the thing still in your hand is <vocabulary form="持って来る">to bring (a thing)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の授業に、自分のパソコンを持って来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring your own computer to tomorrow's class.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]に、自[じ]分[ぶん]のパソコンを持[も]って来[き]てください。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄が台所から冷たい水を持って来てくれました。
example_sentences.english: My older brother brought me cold water from the kitchen.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]が台[だい]所[どころ]から冷[つめ]たい水[みず]を持[も]って来[き]てくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫が庭から小さい花を持って来ました。
example_sentences.english: The cat brought a small flower in from the garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]が庭[にわ]から小[ちい]さい花[はな]を持[も]って来[き]ました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 持（も）＋って＋行（い）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Holding (持って) something as you go (行く).
items.meaning_mnemonic: You clamp your <kanji form="持">hold</kanji> around the lunchbox and <kanji form="行">go</kanji> straight out through the crossroads with it. Carrying the thing away from the house is <vocabulary form="持って行く">to take (a thing)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、祖父の家へ果物を持って行くつもりです。
example_sentences.english: This weekend I plan to take some fruit to my grandfather's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、祖[そ]父[ふ]の家[いえ]へ果物[くだもの]を持[も]って行[い]くつもりです。

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館に辞書を持って行ってもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Is it okay to take a dictionary into the library?
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]に辞[じ]書[しょ]を持[も]って行[い]ってもいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行には軽いかばんを持って行ったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You'd better take a light bag on the trip.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]には軽[かる]いかばんを持[も]って行[い]ったほうがいいですよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 話（はな）＋し＋合（あ）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: Talking (話し) together (合う): to discuss.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Each side <kanji form="話">talk</kanji>s, story after story, until the two accounts finally <kanji form="合">fit</kanji> together. Talk that both sides work at until it matches is <vocabulary form="話し合う">to discuss / talk over</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫と来年の旅行の予定を話し合いました。
example_sentences.english: My husband and I talked over our plans for next year's trip.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]と来[らい]年[ねん]の旅[りょ]行[こう]の予[よ]定[てい]を話[はな]し合[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄弟で、親にあげる物を話し合っています。
example_sentences.english: The siblings are discussing what to give their parents.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[きょう]弟[だい]で、親[おや]にあげる物[もの]を話[はな]し合[あ]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 困ったことがあったら、家族でよく話し合いましょう。
example_sentences.english: When something's wrong, let's talk it through properly as a family.
example_sentences.furigana: 困[こま]ったことがあったら、家[か]族[ぞく]でよく話[はな]し合[あ]いましょう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 見（み）＋送（おく）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Watching (見) someone off (送る): to see off.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You keep your <kanji form="見">see</kanji>ing eye locked on your friend while the platform <kanji form="送">send</kanji>s her off down a track you may not follow. Watching a person go until she is out of sight is <vocabulary form="見送る">to see off</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港で娘を見送ったとき、少し泣いてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: When I saw my daughter off at the airport, I cried a little.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]で娘[むすめ]を見送[みおく]ったとき、少[すこ]し泣[な]いてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが帰るときは、外まで出て見送りましょう。
example_sentences.english: When guests leave, let's go outside and see them off.
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さんが帰[かえ]るときは、外[そと]まで出[で]て見[み]送[おく]りましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬は毎朝、窓から祖母を見送ります。
example_sentences.english: Every morning the dog watches Grandma leave from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]、窓[まど]から祖[そ]母[ぼ]を見[み]送[おく]ります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 見（み）＋回（まわ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Turning (回す) one's view (見): to look around.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="見">see</kanji>ing eye travels one full <kanji form="回">round</kanji> of the room, past every wall and back to where it started. Sweeping your gaze in a circle like that is <vocabulary form="見回す">to look around</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車を降りてから、駅の中を見回しました。
example_sentences.english: After getting off the train, I looked around the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]車[しゃ]を降[お]りてから、駅[えき]の中[なか]を見回[みまわ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は知らない町で、不安そうに見回していました。
example_sentences.english: In the unfamiliar town, my little brother was looking around nervously.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は知[し]らない町[まち]で、不[ふ]安[あん]そうに見回[みまわ]していました。

example_sentences.japanese: 教室を見回したが、先生はまだ来ていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I looked around the classroom, but the teacher hadn't come yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 教[きょう]室[しつ]を見回[みまわ]したが、先[せん]生[せい]はまだ来[き]ていなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 見（み）＋つけ＋出（だ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Finding (見つけ) something and drawing it out (出す).
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="見">see</kanji>ing eye catches the hidden thing, and you haul it up over the box rim until it <kanji form="出">exit</kanji>s into daylight. Dragging a buried fact into the open is <vocabulary form="見つけ出す">to discover / find out</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 警官は、無くなった自転車を二日で見つけ出しました。
example_sentences.english: The police officer tracked down the missing bicycle in two days.
example_sentences.furigana: 警[けい]官[かん]は、無[な]くなった自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]を二日[ふつか]で見[み]つけ出[だ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い地図で、叔母が生まれた場所を見つけ出した。
example_sentences.english: I found the place where my aunt was born on an old map.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い地[ち]図[ず]で、叔母[おば]が生[う]まれた場[ば]所[しょ]を見[み]つけ出[だ]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は、たくさんの写真の中から自分の顔を見つけ出した。
example_sentences.english: My little sister picked out her own face from among lots of photos.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は、たくさんの写[しゃ]真[しん]の中[なか]から自[じ]分[ぶん]の顔[かお]を見[み]つけ出[だ]した。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 考（かんが）＋え＋出（だ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Thinking (考え) something into being (出す): to devise.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="考">think</kanji>, tracing one old thought down its kinked track until a new idea works loose. Forcing that idea to <kanji form="出">exit</kanji> into the open is <vocabulary form="考え出す">to think up / devise</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は、朝早く起きない理由をいろいろ考え出す。
example_sentences.english: My son thinks up all sorts of reasons not to get up early in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は、朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きない理[り]由[ゆう]をいろいろ考[かんが]え出[だ]す。

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は、叔父が考え出したものです。
example_sentences.english: This dish is one my uncle came up with.
example_sentences.furigana: この料[りょう]理[り]は、叔父[おじ]が考[かんが]え出[だ]したものです。

example_sentences.japanese: 会社のみんなで、新しい名前を考え出しました。
example_sentences.english: Everyone at the company came up with a new name together.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]のみんなで、新[あたら]しい名[な]前[まえ]を考[かんが]え出[だ]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — やり＋直（なお）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Doing (やり) it fixed again (直す): to redo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The moment the work goes wrong, you <kanji form="直">straightaway</kanji> tear it down and carry the pieces back to step one. Building it again from the start like that is <vocabulary form="やり直す">to redo / start over</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 直 is 「なお」 from 直す, the verb it first appeared in, so <vocabulary form="やり直す">to redo / start over</vocabulary> is <reading>やりなおす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 数学の問題を間違えたので、最初からやり直しました。
example_sentences.english: I got the math problem wrong, so I redid it from the start.
example_sentences.furigana: 数[すう]学[がく]の問[もん]題[だい]を間[ま]違[ちが]えたので、最[さい]初[しょ]からやり直[なお]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋がまだ汚いと言われて、少年は掃除をやり直した。
example_sentences.english: Told his room was still dirty, the boy did the cleaning over again.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]がまだ汚[きたな]いと言[い]われて、少[しょう]年[ねん]は掃[そう]除[じ]をやり直[なお]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 大丈夫、何度でもやり直せますよ。
example_sentences.english: It's fine — you can start over as many times as you like.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]、何[なん]度[ど]でもやり直[なお]せますよ。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Doing a favor and giving it: yatte ageru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Out on the <reading>yacht, a giraffe</reading> leans up and knots the top sail no sailor can reach, doing it for the whole crew. Doing the work so that someone else gains is <vocabulary form="やってあげる">to do (for someone)</vocabulary>, the outward giving inside <reading>やってあげる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間がないなら、その仕事は私がやってあげますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't have time, I'll do that job for you.
example_sentences.furigana: 時[じ]間[かん]がないなら、その仕[し]事[ごと]は私[わたし]がやってあげますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の宿題をやってあげたら、母に叱られました。
example_sentences.english: I did my little brother's homework for him and got scolded by Mom.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の宿[しゅく]題[だい]をやってあげたら、母[はは]に叱[しか]られました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が忙しそうだったので、洗濯をやってあげました。
example_sentences.english: My girlfriend looked busy, so I did the laundry for her.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]が忙[いそが]しそうだったので、洗[せん]濯[たく]をやってあげました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 丸（まる）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A machine at Koichi's konbini is set wrong, so every onigiri on the door shelf rolls out a perfect <vocabulary>round</vocabulary> ball instead of a triangle. The い closing the word is its adjective marker, so it can describe any noun.
items.reading_mnemonic: The broken machine at Koichi's konbini rolls out every onigiri like a giant <reading>marble</reading> bouncing along the door shelf. He sighs <reading>まるい</reading>, because each one is perfectly <vocabulary form="丸い">round</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このテーブルは丸いです。
example_sentences.english: This table is round.
example_sentences.furigana: このテーブルは丸[まる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の顔は丸いです。
example_sentences.english: Her face is round.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]の顔[かお]は丸[まる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 丸い箱を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a round box.
example_sentences.furigana: 丸[まる]い箱[はこ]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 元（げん）＋気（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>spirit</kanji> still burning at its <kanji>beginning</kanji> strength is a <vocabulary>healthy / lively</vocabulary> one. It is a な adjective, so な slips in before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんは元気ですか。
example_sentences.english: How is your mother doing?
example_sentences.furigana: お母[かあ]さんは元[げん]気[き]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は朝から元気です。
example_sentences.english: I've been full of energy since this morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は朝[あさ]から元[げん]気[き]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が公園で元気に遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: The dog plays energetically in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]が公[こう]園[えん]で元[げん]気[き]に遊[あそ]ぶ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 広（ひろ）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A caped hero lands on the school field, throws his arms wide for a pose, and still has room to run a full lap. Only a truly <vocabulary>wide / spacious</vocabulary> field leaves that much room to spare.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>hero</reading> paces Grandma Kane's shrine, grumbling that the yard is not <reading>ひろい</reading> enough to land a single jump. He will only strike a pose somewhere properly <vocabulary>wide / spacious</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は広いです。
example_sentences.english: This room is spacious.
example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]は広[ひろ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 広い公園で遊びます。
example_sentences.english: I play in a spacious park.
example_sentences.furigana: 広[ひろ]い公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: あの道は広いですか。
example_sentences.english: Is that road wide?
example_sentences.furigana: あの道[みち]は広[ひろ]いですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 汚（きたな）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You haul your one white shirt out of the river and it comes up streaked brown and reeking of pondweed, somehow worse than before the wash. A shirt in that state is <vocabulary>dirty</vocabulary>, and the trailing い tags it as an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: A stray kitten drags itself out of the riverbank mud with one <reading>kitten eye</reading> gummed shut and its fur matted into grey clumps. You reach to lift it, but it is <reading>きたない</reading> to the bone, far too <vocabulary>dirty</vocabulary> for your lap.

example_sentences.japanese: この服は汚いです。
example_sentences.english: These clothes are dirty.
example_sentences.furigana: この服[ふく]は汚[きたな]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 手が汚い。
example_sentences.english: My hands are dirty.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[て]が汚[きたな]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 汚い水は飲みません。
example_sentences.english: I don't drink dirty water.
example_sentences.furigana: 汚[きたな]い水[みず]は飲[の]みません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 好（す）＋き.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That warm tug toward one exact bench, one exact song, one exact tin of coffee is what being <vocabulary>liked / fond of</vocabulary> feels like from the inside. That な sits in front of the noun it describes.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane leans her one wooden <reading>ski</reading> against that exact bench, cracks open that exact tin of coffee, and hums <reading>すき</reading>, because this is the spot she is most <vocabulary form="好き">fond of</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は猫が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like cats.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は猫[ねこ]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 何が好きですか。
example_sentences.english: What do you like?
example_sentences.furigana: 何[なに]が好[す]きですか。

example_sentences.japanese: お酒は好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I don't like alcohol.
example_sentences.furigana: お酒[さけ]は好[す]きじゃない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 有（ゆう）＋名（めい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A name that exists everywhere: yuumei.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Even with your face hidden, a <kanji>name</kanji> that this many strangers already <kanji>have</kanji> in their heads makes you <vocabulary>famous</vocabulary>. It takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は有名な医者です。
example_sentences.english: She is a famous doctor.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は有[ゆう]名[めい]な医[い]者[しゃ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランは有名です。
example_sentences.english: This restaurant is famous.
example_sentences.furigana: このレストランは有[ゆう]名[めい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は有名な人に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met a famous person.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は有[ゆう]名[めい]な人[ひと]に会[あ]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 同（おな）＋じ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two socks from one dryer load, worn to a matching grey heel, are for every purpose the <vocabulary>same</vocabulary>. Handle it as a な adjective, so な lands before the noun it describes.
items.reading_mnemonic: Pulling two grey-heeled socks from one dryer load, a boy holds them up to his gran and sighs <reading>oh, Nan, gee</reading>, 「<reading>おなじ</reading>」, since the pair really is the <vocabulary form="同じ">same</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これとそれは同じですか。
example_sentences.english: Are this and that the same?
example_sentences.furigana: これとそれは同[おな]じですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は友達と同じ映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I'll watch the same movie as my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は友[とも]達[だち]と同[おな]じ映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は昨日と同じ天気です。
example_sentences.english: Today's weather is the same as yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は昨日[きのう]と同[おな]じ天[てん]気[き]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 曲（ま）＋がる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The straight road suddenly hits a <kanji>bend</kanji> and swings hard to the left. Following that bend around is what it means to <vocabulary>turn</vocabulary> a corner.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your driving <reading>guru</reading> sits silent on the straight road until it swings hard left at the bend, then barks <reading>まがる</reading> and you follow it round to <vocabulary form="曲がる">turn</vocabulary> the corner.

example_sentences.japanese: この角を曲がります。
example_sentences.english: I turn at this corner.
example_sentences.furigana: この角[かど]を曲[ま]がります。

example_sentences.japanese: 角を曲がると駅がある。
example_sentences.english: When you turn the corner, there's a station.
example_sentences.furigana: 角[かど]を曲[ま]がると駅[えき]がある。

example_sentences.japanese: タクシーが角を曲がった。
example_sentences.english: The taxi turned the corner.
example_sentences.furigana: タクシーが角[かど]を曲[ま]がった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 辛（から）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Bite a chilli the colour of a fire hydrant, then chase it with a fistful of rock salt, and your whole mouth is on fire either way. Either burn is <vocabulary>spicy / salty</vocabulary>, and that final い lets you hang it on a noun like any adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hungry pilgrim at Grandma Kane's shrine wolfs a bowl of <reading>curry</reading> left as an offering, gets three steps, and dives into the water trough. A mouth that reacts like that has met something truly <reading>からい</reading>, blazing <vocabulary>spicy / salty</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は辛いです。
example_sentences.english: This dish is spicy.
example_sentences.furigana: この料[りょう]理[り]は辛[から]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 辛い肉を食べました。
example_sentences.english: I ate some spicy meat.
example_sentences.furigana: 辛[から]い肉[にく]を食[た]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: その魚は辛いですか。
example_sentences.english: Is that fish spicy?
example_sentences.furigana: その魚[さかな]は辛[から]いですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 忘（わす）＋れる.
items.mnemonic_text: Let it slip the mind: wasureru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You set your keys down somewhere so ordinary your brain never files it, and an hour later that spot is a blank. Letting a thing fall clean out of your head is to <vocabulary>forget</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: "It <reading>was surely</reading> right here," you mutter, patting the blank shelf where you set your keys an hour ago, <reading>わすれる</reading>, and that empty spot is what it is to <vocabulary form="忘れる">forget</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は財布を忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my wallet.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は財[さい]布[ふ]を忘[わす]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 鍵を忘れないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't forget your keys.
example_sentences.furigana: 鍵[かぎ]を忘[わす]れないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は毎日弁当を忘れる。
example_sentences.english: She forgets her lunch box every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は毎[まい]日[にち]弁[べん]当[とう]を忘[わす]れる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 若（わか）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the shrine, Grandma Kane swears she is still <vocabulary>young</vocabulary> as she chases the cats up the mossy steps two at a time. The い on the end is the marker that makes it an adjective, free to sit before any noun.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane chases the cats up the mossy shrine steps two at a time, a stunt so <reading>wacky</reading> the priest gasps <reading>わかい</reading>. Anyone that spry is still <vocabulary form="若い">young</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は若いです。
example_sentences.english: That teacher is young.
example_sentences.furigana: あの先[せん]生[せい]は若[わか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 若い友達と公園に行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to the park with a young friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 若[わか]い友[とも]達[だち]と公[こう]園[えん]に行[い]く。

example_sentences.japanese: この犬は若いです。
example_sentences.english: This dog is young.
example_sentences.furigana: この犬[いぬ]は若[わか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 狭（せま）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You meet someone in the shrine hallway and you both have to turn sideways to squeeze past, because the walls sit that close together. A passage like that is <vocabulary>narrow / cramped</vocabulary>, and the final い makes it an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>semi</reading> truck noses into the alley behind Koichi's konbini and stops dead, wedged tight between the two walls. The alley is <reading>せまい</reading>, far too <vocabulary>narrow / cramped</vocabulary> for a truck that size.

example_sentences.japanese: この店は狭いです。
example_sentences.english: This shop is cramped.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]は狭[せま]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: うちの台所は狭いです。
example_sentences.english: Our kitchen is cramped.
example_sentences.furigana: うちの台[だい]所[どころ]は狭[せま]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 狭い部屋に入ります。
example_sentences.english: I go into a cramped room.
example_sentences.furigana: 狭[せま]い部屋[へや]に入[はい]ります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 弱（よわ）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You rest one elbow on the wire shelf by the konbini door and the whole rack folds to the floor, onigiri and all. A thing that gives out the moment anything leans on it is <vocabulary>weak</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi rests one elbow on the wire shelf by the konbini door and the whole rack folds to the floor, onigiri and all. He moans <reading>yo, why</reading>, since a shelf that <reading>よわい</reading> is <vocabulary form="弱い">weak</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は体が弱いです。
example_sentences.english: I have a weak body.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は体[からだ]が弱[よわ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: このお茶は弱いです。
example_sentences.english: This tea is weak.
example_sentences.furigana: このお茶[ちゃ]は弱[よわ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は朝に弱いです。
example_sentences.english: She's not a morning person.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は朝[あさ]に弱[よわ]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 起（お）＋きる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The alarm has howled for a full hour. Your eyes crack open, your back peels off the futon, and you <vocabulary>wake up / get up</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: After the alarm howls for a full hour, Roo the kangaroo peels his back off the futon, mumbling <reading>OK, Roo</reading>, 「<reading>おきる</reading>」, and finally has to <vocabulary form="起きる">get up</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝七時に起きます。
example_sentences.english: I wake up at seven every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]七[しち]時[じ]に起[お]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟はまだ起きません。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother isn't up yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]はまだ起[お]きません。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は早く起きた。
example_sentences.english: I got up early today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は早[はや]く起[お]きた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 欲（ほ）＋しい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That itch of <kanji>longing</kanji> when a friend unwraps a present and you realise you want one too is exactly what it means to <vocabulary>want (to have)</vocabulary> something. The い on the end makes it an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: When her friend unwraps a gleaming garden hoe, Mika sighs <reading>oh, she</reading> got one, <reading>ほしい</reading>, and that itch of longing means she <vocabulary form="欲しい">wants</vocabulary> one too.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は新しい本が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a new book.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は新[あたら]しい本[ほん]が欲[ほ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今、冷たい水が欲しい。
example_sentences.english: I want some cold water now.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[いま]、冷[つめ]たい水[みず]が欲[ほ]しい。

example_sentences.japanese: 何が欲しいですか。
example_sentences.english: What do you want?
example_sentences.furigana: 何[なに]が欲[ほ]しいですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 閉（し）＋める.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When the last class leaves, the caretaker at Sei's school walks the hallway pulling every window down and easing every classroom door shut. Bringing something that stood open back to shut is <vocabulary>to close</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hard white <reading>shimmer</reading> bounces off the gym windows and blinds every free throw at Sei's school. So the coach sends a player <vocabulary>to close</vocabulary> <reading>しめる</reading> the blinds before practice.

example_sentences.japanese: ドアを閉めます。
example_sentences.english: I close the door.
example_sentences.furigana: ドアを閉[し]めます。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓を閉めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please close the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]を閉[し]めてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜、店を閉めます。
example_sentences.english: At night, I close the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]、店[みせ]を閉[し]めます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 脱（ぬ）＋ぐ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The only way to <kanji>escape</kanji> a soaked raincoat is to peel it down off your arms and let it drop. Peeling a garment off your body like that is what it means to <vocabulary>take off (clothes)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A walrus flops onto the riverbank and drags its dripping wetsuit off over its head. It grunts 「<reading>ぬぐ</reading>」 as a cold <reading>nugget</reading> of riverweed plops from the sleeve, because it will <vocabulary>take off (clothes)</vocabulary> anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 家で靴を脱ぎます。
example_sentences.english: I take off my shoes at home.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]で靴[くつ]を脱[ぬ]ぎます。

example_sentences.japanese: コートを脱いでください。
example_sentences.english: Please take off your coat.
example_sentences.furigana: コートを脱[ぬ]いでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いからシャツを脱ぐ。
example_sentences.english: I take off my shirt because it's hot.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]いからシャツを脱[ぬ]ぐ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 短（みじか）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A midge is about one pencil-dot wide and lives from breakfast to lunch. That covers <vocabulary>short</vocabulary> in both size and time.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>midge</reading> lands on the beeping till at Koichi's konbini and lifts off again before the beep has finished. A visit that <reading>みじかい</reading> is exactly what <vocabulary>short</vocabulary> describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この道は短いです。
example_sentences.english: This road is short.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は短[みじか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の日は短い。
example_sentences.english: Winter days are short.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]の日[ひ]は短[みじか]い。

example_sentences.japanese: その映画は短かった。
example_sentences.english: That movie was short.
example_sentences.furigana: その映[えい]画[が]は短[みじか]かった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 軽（かる）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You brace hard to heave the box, but it is empty, and it flies up so fast you stumble backwards. Anything that easy to lift is <vocabulary>light (weight)</vocabulary>, and the い ending marks it as an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: You brace to heave the box, but it is empty and flies up so fast you stumble backwards. Now you can <reading>carry</reading> it on one finger, because a box that <reading>かるい</reading> is <vocabulary form="軽い">light</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このかばんは軽いです。
example_sentences.english: This bag is light.
example_sentences.furigana: このかばんは軽[かる]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: その箱は軽い。
example_sentences.english: That box is light.
example_sentences.furigana: その箱[はこ]は軽[かる]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 軽い靴を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought light shoes.
example_sentences.furigana: 軽[かる]い靴[くつ]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 覚（おぼ）＋える.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <vocabulary>memorize</vocabulary> a list is just <kanji>remembering</kanji> forced on purpose. You drill each item into your skull, over and over, until it cannot slip back out.
items.reading_mnemonic: In the echoing school hallway a kid plays the same four bars on her <reading>oboe</reading>, eyes shut, until her fingers move on their own. Drilling something in until it sticks like that is <reading>おぼえる</reading>, which is how you <vocabulary>memorize</vocabulary> anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい料理を覚える。
example_sentences.english: I'm memorizing a new dish.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい料[りょう]理[り]を覚[おぼ]える。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は覚えるのが下手だ。
example_sentences.english: He's bad at memorizing things.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は覚[おぼ]えるのが下手[へた]だ。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日この本を覚える。
example_sentences.english: I'll memorize this book today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]この本[ほん]を覚[おぼ]える。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 開（あ）＋ける.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every morning at Grandma Kane's shrine someone unbars the big wooden doors and folds the shutters right back so the cats can stream through. Doing that to a shut door is <vocabulary>to open</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>A crow</reading> at Grandma Kane's shrine has learned to wedge its beak under the offering-box lid and lever it up. The cats now leave every latched thing on the grounds for the bird <vocabulary>to open</vocabulary> <reading>あける</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝、窓を開けます。
example_sentences.english: In the morning, I open the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]、窓[まど]を開[あ]けます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がドアを開けた。
example_sentences.english: He opened the door.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]がドアを開[あ]けた。

example_sentences.japanese: この箱を開けてください。
example_sentences.english: Please open this box.
example_sentences.furigana: この箱[はこ]を開[あ]けてください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 着（き）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You drag a jumper down over your head and force both arms through the sleeves until your face pops out the top. Winning that wrestling match with a shirt is what it means to <vocabulary>wear (top)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A heron on the mountain trail is so cold it feeds coins to the vending machine and drags on a whole <reading>kilo</reading> of knitted jumpers. It squawks 「<reading>きる</reading>」 and will <vocabulary>wear (top)</vocabulary> anything with sleeves.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はシャツを着ます。
example_sentences.english: I put on a shirt.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はシャツを着[き]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は新しい服を着た。
example_sentences.english: She wore new clothes.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は新[あたら]しい服[ふく]を着[き]た。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬はコートを着ます。
example_sentences.english: In winter I wear a coat.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]はコートを着[き]ます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 遊（あそ）＋ぶ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Turn a knot of kids loose in a park and they run in looping circles for no reason and to no end. That aimless motion, done for its own sake, is what it means to <vocabulary>play</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toss <reading>a soap</reading> bubble into the park and the knot of kids runs looping circles after it, for no reason and to no end, <reading>あそぶ</reading>: that is to <vocabulary form="遊ぶ">play</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で友達と遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: I play with friends at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で友[とも]達[だち]と遊[あそ]ぶ。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日うちで遊んだ。
example_sentences.english: I played at home yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]うちで遊[あそ]んだ。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に海で遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: I play at the sea on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に海[うみ]で遊[あそ]ぶ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 暗（くら）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone unscrews the last working bulb in the basement and now you cannot see your own hand in front of your face. A room like that is <vocabulary>dark</vocabulary>, and the trailing い makes it an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: Someone unscrews the last bulb in the basement and little Kura cannot see her own hand, so she sits on the stairs to <reading>cry</reading>. A basement that <reading>くらい</reading> is truly <vocabulary form="暗い">dark</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は暗いです。
example_sentences.english: This room is dark.
example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]は暗[くら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜の道は暗いです。
example_sentences.english: The road is dark at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]の道[みち]は暗[くら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 暗い部屋で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I read a book in a dark room.
example_sentences.furigana: 暗[くら]い部屋[へや]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 嫌（きら）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The instant curl of your lip at a smell you cannot stand is the whole of being <vocabulary>disliked</vocabulary>. Like every な word, it drops な in front of the noun.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei sniffs the sour old <reading>clay</reading> at the pottery table and her lip curls at once, the way it does at any smell she cannot stand. That curl, <reading>きらい</reading>, means <vocabulary form="嫌い">disliked</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は魚が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: I don't like fish.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は魚[さかな]が嫌[きら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌いな食べ物は肉です。
example_sentences.english: The food I dislike is meat.
example_sentences.furigana: 嫌[きら]いな食[た]べ物[もの]は肉[にく]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は雨の日が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: She doesn't like rainy days.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は雨[あめ]の日[ひ]が嫌[きら]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 寝（ね）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your eyes slam shut and the book drops onto your face. The whole day switches off by itself, and you <vocabulary>sleep</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: With no <reading>nerve</reading> left to keep reading, a student lets the book drop onto his face and drifts off <vocabulary form="寝る">to sleep</vocabulary> with a slow 「<reading>ねる</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎晩早く寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I go to bed early every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]早[はや]く寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟が今寝ています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother is sleeping right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]が今[いま]寝[ね]ています。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫はベッドで寝る。
example_sentences.english: The cat sleeps on the bed.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]はベッドで寝[ね]る。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 働（はたら）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You are on the go from the first bell to the last, with no real break, until your whole body aches. That endless grind is what it means to <vocabulary>work</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: From the first bell to the last, a waiter dashes between the tables and the <reading>hat rack</reading> with no break, groaning 「<reading>はたらく</reading>」 as his body aches. That is what it means <vocabulary form="働く">to work</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は会社で働きます。
example_sentences.english: I work at a company.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は会[かい]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は朝から働きます。
example_sentences.english: She works from the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は朝[あさ]から働[はたら]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は病院で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My father works at a hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は病[びょう]院[いん]で働[はたら]いています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 静（しず）＋か.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Deep in the school library at exam time, forty students hold so still you can hear the wall clock two rooms away. That held breath, not one creaking chair in it, is <vocabulary>quiet</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The students call the library's silence-warden <reading>She's-a-cop</reading> because she books you for breathing too loud. One look from her and the whole room drops <vocabulary>quiet</vocabulary>, and that hush is <reading>しずか</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は静かです。
example_sentences.english: This room is quiet.
example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]は静[しず]かです。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが静かに寝ます。
example_sentences.english: The baby sleeps quietly.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんが静[しず]かに寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 静かな喫茶店が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like quiet coffee shops.
example_sentences.furigana: 静[しず]かな喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]が好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 賑（にぎ）＋やか.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On sports day the school field runs three races at once, a brass band, and parents yelling from every rail. All that noise and motion piled together is <vocabulary>lively / bustling</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On sports day, a dad called <reading>Knee-gear-yakker</reading> yells louder than the brass band across all three races at once. That roar is <reading>にぎやか</reading>, and the whole school field is <vocabulary form="賑やか">lively</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は賑やかです。
example_sentences.english: This town is lively.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]は賑[にぎ]やかです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末の公園は賑やかです。
example_sentences.english: The park is bustling on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]の公[こう]園[えん]は賑[にぎ]やかです。

example_sentences.japanese: 賑やかな店が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like lively shops.
example_sentences.furigana: 賑[にぎ]やかな店[みせ]が好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 踊（おど）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your hips swing, your feet cross and stamp, and your arms cut shapes in the air in time with a beat. All that patterned motion to music is what it means to <vocabulary>dance</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your hips swing and your feet stamp in time with the beat until you crash into the <reading>odd door</reading> in the hall, <reading>おどる</reading>, still moving: that is to <vocabulary form="踊る">dance</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に友達と踊ります。
example_sentences.english: I dance with friends on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に友[とも]達[だち]と踊[おど]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で一緒に踊りましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's dance together in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で一[いっ]緒[しょ]に踊[おど]りましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が庭で踊っています。
example_sentences.english: The kids are dancing in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が庭[にわ]で踊[おど]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Someone doing a favor for me: yatte kureru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Back on the <reading>yacht, a crew</reading> of borrowed hands bails the flooded hull while you only hold the tiller. Someone else doing the work for you, while you sit back, is <vocabulary form="やってくれる">to do (for me)</vocabulary>, the inward favour inside <reading>やってくれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 病気で寝ていたとき、隣の人が買い物をやってくれた。
example_sentences.english: When I was sick in bed, my neighbor did the shopping for me.
example_sentences.furigana: 病[びょう]気[き]で寝[ね]ていたとき、隣[となり]の人[ひと]が買[か]い物[もの]をやってくれた。

example_sentences.japanese: 父はいつも、面倒くさいことを笑ってやってくれる。
example_sentences.english: Dad always does the tedious stuff for me with a smile.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]はいつも、面[めん]倒[どう]くさいことを笑[わら]ってやってくれる。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の準備は、全部田中さんがやってくれました。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san did all the preparation for the meeting for us.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]の準[じゅん]備[び]は、全[ぜん]部[ぶ]田中[たなか]さんがやってくれました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving the favor of an action: yatte morau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Off the <reading>yacht, a moray</reading> eel is the only thing that will chew the fouled anchor rope free, so down it goes to do the job. Getting someone else to do the work in your place is <vocabulary form="やってもらう">to have (someone) do</vocabulary>, the sound sitting inside <reading>やってもらう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい問題は、専門家にやってもらいましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's leave the difficult part to an expert.
example_sentences.furigana: 難[むずか]しい問[もん]題[だい]は、専[せん]門[もん]家[か]にやってもらいましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒くさい仕事は弟にやってもらった。
example_sentences.english: I got my little brother to do the tedious job.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[めん]倒[どう]くさい仕[し]事[ごと]は弟[おとうと]にやってもらった。

example_sentences.japanese: 自分でできないので、店員さんにやってもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't do it myself, so I had the shop clerk do it.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]でできないので、店[てん]員[いん]さんにやってもらいました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 作（つく）＋ってあげる.
items.mnemonic_text: Making something and giving it: tsukutte ageru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="作">make</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="作ってあげる">to make (for someone)</vocabulary> word are the same word, so at heart it just means make. The tail on the end only adds that you make the thing for someone else, not for yourself.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 作 is 「つく」 from 作る, the verb it first appeared in, so <vocabulary form="作ってあげる">to make (for someone)</vocabulary> is <reading>つくってあげる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、彼女に弁当を作ってあげるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm planning to make a boxed lunch for my girlfriend.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、彼[かの]女[じょ]に弁[べん]当[とう]を作[つく]ってあげるつもりです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が風邪なので、私が晩ご飯を作ってあげました。
example_sentences.english: My husband has a cold, so I made dinner for him.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]が風邪[かぜ]なので、私[わたし]が晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を作[つく]ってあげました。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供に紙で小さい箱を作ってあげましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's make a little paper box for the kids.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]に紙[かみ]で小[ちい]さい箱[はこ]を作[つく]ってあげましょう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 見（み）＋せてくれる.
items.mnemonic_text: Someone showing something to me: misete kureru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A friend makes you <kanji form="見">see</kanji> something by holding it up in front of your face. That small favour, done for you, is to <vocabulary form="見せてくれる">show (to me)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 見 is 「み」 from 見る, the verb to look, so <vocabulary form="見せてくれる">to show (to me)</vocabulary> is <reading>みせてくれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父が古い写真を見せてくれました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather showed me some old photos.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]が古[ふる]い写[しゃ]真[しん]を見[み]せてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員さんが地図を見せてくれたので、道が分かりました。
example_sentences.english: The station attendant showed me a map, so I figured out the way.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]さんが地[ち]図[ず]を見[み]せてくれたので、道[みち]が分[わ]かりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日のノート、ちょっと見せてくれる？
example_sentences.english: Could you show me your notes from yesterday for a sec?
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]のノート、ちょっと見[み]せてくれる？

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 教（おし）＋えてもらう.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving the favor of being taught: oshiete morau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="教">teach</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="教えてもらう">to have (someone) teach</vocabulary> word are the same word, so they carry the same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 教 is 「おし」 from 教える, the verb to teach, so <vocabulary form="教えてもらう">to have (someone) teach</vocabulary> is <reading>おしえてもらう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人に駅までの道を教えてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: The person next to me told me the way to the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]に駅[えき]までの道[みち]を教[おし]えてもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎週土曜日、姉に料理を教えてもらっています。
example_sentences.english: Every Saturday, my older sister teaches me how to cook.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]週[しゅう]土[ど]曜[よう]日[び]、姉[あね]に料[りょう]理[り]を教[おし]えてもらっています。

example_sentences.japanese: 分からない漢字は、先生に教えてもらったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You'd better have your teacher explain the kanji you don't know.
example_sentences.furigana: 分[わ]からない漢[かん]字[じ]は、先[せん]生[せい]に教[おし]えてもらったほうがいいですよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 書（か）＋いてあげる.
items.mnemonic_text: Writing something and giving it: kaite ageru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="書">write</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="書いてあげる">to write (for someone)</vocabulary> word are one and the same, so the meaning does not change.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 書 is 「か」 from 書く, the verb to write, so <vocabulary form="書いてあげる">to write (for someone)</vocabulary> is <reading>かいてあげる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は目が悪いので、私が手紙を書いてあげます。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother's eyesight is poor, so I write her letters for her.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は目[め]が悪[わる]いので、私[わたし]が手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]いてあげます。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人のお客さんに、ホテルの住所を紙に書いてあげた。
example_sentences.english: I wrote the hotel's address on a piece of paper for a foreign guest.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]のお客[きゃく]さんに、ホテルの住[じゅう]所[しょ]を紙[かみ]に書[か]いてあげた。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子の名前をカタカナで書いてあげたら、とても喜びました。
example_sentences.english: When I wrote my son's name in katakana for him, he was really happy.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]の名[な]前[まえ]をカタカナで書[か]いてあげたら、とても喜[よろこ]びました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 手（て）＋伝（つだ）＋ってくれる.
items.mnemonic_text: Someone lending a hand for me: tetsudatte kureru.
items.furigana: 手伝[てつだ]ってくれる
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone puts a <kanji form="手">hand</kanji> to your job and lets their own plans <kanji form="伝">go along</kanji> with your work instead. Doing that for you is to <vocabulary form="手伝ってくれる">help (me)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越すとき、仲間がみんな手伝ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: When I moved, all my friends pitched in and helped.
example_sentences.furigana: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]すとき、仲[なか]間[ま]がみんな手伝[てつだ]ってくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 重い荷物を持っていたら、若い男の人が手伝ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: I was carrying heavy bags, and a young man helped me.
example_sentences.furigana: 重[おも]い荷[に]物[もつ]を持[も]っていたら、若[わか]い男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が手伝[てつだ]ってくれた。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の準備は、山田さんが手伝ってくれるそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear Yamada-san is going to help me get ready for the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]の準[じゅん]備[び]は、山田[やまだ]さんが手伝[てつだ]ってくれるそうです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 貸（か）＋してもらう.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving the favor of a loan: kashite morau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You ask, and the owner agrees to <kanji form="貸">lend</kanji> you the thing you need. Walking off with it on that promise is to <vocabulary form="貸してもらう">have (something) lent</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 貸 is 「か」 from 貸す, the verb to lend, so <vocabulary form="貸してもらう">to have (something) lent</vocabulary> is <reading>かしてもらう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降ってきたので、店で傘を貸してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: It started to rain, so the shop lent me an umbrella.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ってきたので、店[みせ]で傘[かさ]を貸[か]してもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 財布を忘れたので、兄にお金を貸してもらった。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my wallet, so I got my older brother to lend me some money.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]を忘[わす]れたので、兄[あに]にお金[かね]を貸[か]してもらった。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館で自転車を貸してもらって、町を回りました。
example_sentences.english: The inn lent us bicycles, and we rode around town.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]館[かん]で自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]を貸[か]してもらって、町[まち]を回[まわ]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 送（おく）＋ってあげる.
items.mnemonic_text: Sending something as a favor: okutte ageru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="送">send</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="送ってあげる">to send (for someone)</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 送 is 「おく」 from 送る, the verb to send, so <vocabulary form="送ってあげる">to send (for someone)</vocabulary> is <reading>おくってあげる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: もう遅いから、家まで送ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: It's late, so I'll take you home.
example_sentences.furigana: もう遅[おそ]いから、家[いえ]まで送[おく]ってあげるよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母に赤ちゃんの写真をたくさん送ってあげました。
example_sentences.english: I sent my aunt lots of photos of the baby.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]に赤[あか]ちゃんの写[しゃ]真[しん]をたくさん送[おく]ってあげました。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国に住んでいる娘に、日本のお菓子を送ってあげたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to send some Japanese snacks to my daughter who lives abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]に住[す]んでいる娘[むすめ]に、日本[にほん]のお菓[か]子[し]を送[おく]ってあげたい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 牛（うし）.
items.mnemonic_text: Horns over a body: a cow.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="牛">cow</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="牛">cow</vocabulary> word are exactly the same character, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Seen from the front, with one slanted horn and those two broad bars of shoulder and back, she makes the farmer sigh <reading>ooh, she</reading> is fine: a <vocabulary form="牛">cow</vocabulary>, <reading>うし</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 農家の牛が道の真ん中で寝ていて、車が止まった。
example_sentences.english: A farmer's cow was lying asleep in the middle of the road, so the cars stopped.
example_sentences.furigana: 農[のう]家[か]の牛[うし]が道[みち]の真[ま]ん中[なか]で寝[ね]ていて、車[くるま]が止[と]まった。

example_sentences.japanese: 牛は水をたくさん飲むそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear cows drink a lot of water.
example_sentences.furigana: 牛[うし]は水[みず]をたくさん飲[の]むそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころ、牛が怖くて近くに行けなかった。
example_sentences.english: As a kid, I was so scared of cows that I couldn't go near them.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]のころ、牛[うし]が怖[こわ]くて近[ちか]くに行[い]けなかった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 自（し）＋然（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One's own (自) natural state (然): nature.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything that is the way it is by its own <kanji form="自">self</kanji>, just that <kanji form="然">sort of thing</kanji> with nobody shaping it, is <vocabulary form="自然">nature</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は自然の多い町に住みたいそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently my grandfather wants to live in a town with lots of nature.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は自[し]然[ぜん]の多[おお]い町[まち]に住[す]みたいそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は自然を見に、川へ出かけることにしました。
example_sentences.english: I decided to head out to the river this weekend to enjoy some nature.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は自[し]然[ぜん]を見[み]に、川[かわ]へ出[で]かけることにしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のうちに、自然の中でたくさん遊んだほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: Kids should play outdoors in nature as much as they can while they are young.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]のうちに、自[し]然[ぜん]の中[なか]でたくさん遊[あそ]んだほうがいい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 星（ほし）＋空（ぞら）. Rendaku: 空 そら → ぞら.
items.mnemonic_text: Stars (星) filling the sky (空): a starry sky.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Wait until a <kanji form="空">sky</kanji> that looked empty all day fills after dark with thousands of small points of light, and you are looking at a <vocabulary form="星空">starry sky</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上に登ると、星空がとてもきれいでした。
example_sentences.english: When we climbed to the top of the mountain, the starry sky was beautiful.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の上[うえ]に登[のぼ]ると、星[ほし]空[ぞら]がとてもきれいでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は星空を見ながら寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: My daughter fell asleep while gazing at the starry sky.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は星[ほし]空[ぞら]を見[み]ながら寝[ね]てしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の夜は、雲がなければ星空が見えるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow night we should see a starry sky, as long as there are no clouds.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の夜[よる]は、雲[くも]がなければ星[ほし]空[ぞら]が見[み]えるだろう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 砂（すな）.
items.mnemonic_text: Stone (石) broken into few (少) grains: sand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <vocabulary form="砂">Sand</vocabulary> is what a cliff turns into after the sea grinds at it for a few thousand years. What is left is a pile of grains so small they run through your fingers and still will not brush off.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fisher drops a <reading>tuna</reading> at the foot of the cliff the sea is grinding down, and it comes up coated in grains that will not brush off. He sighs <reading>すな</reading> and rinses off the <vocabulary form="砂">sand</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が公園で砂の山を作っています。
example_sentences.english: A child is building a mountain of sand in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]で砂[すな]の山[やま]を作[つく]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 靴の中に砂が入って、歩くのが痛いです。
example_sentences.english: Sand got into my shoes, and it hurts to walk.
example_sentences.furigana: 靴[くつ]の中[なか]に砂[すな]が入[はい]って、歩[ある]くのが痛[いた]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 海の砂は白くて、とても熱かったです。
example_sentences.english: The sand at the beach was white and really hot.
example_sentences.furigana: 海[うみ]の砂[すな]は白[しろ]くて、とても熱[あつ]かったです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 台（たい）＋風（ふう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A platform (台) wind (風): a typhoon.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Give one <kanji form="風">wind</kanji> a name, a number, and its own <kanji form="台">pedestal</kanji> on every weather map, and that single most-watched storm is a <vocabulary form="台風">typhoon</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の日は、外に出ないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't go outside on typhoon days.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]の日[ひ]は、外[そと]に出[で]ないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の風で、傘が壊れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The typhoon wind broke my umbrella.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]の風[かぜ]で、傘[かさ]が壊[こわ]れてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 台風が来る場合は、飛行機が遅れることがあります。
example_sentences.english: When a typhoon comes, flights are sometimes delayed.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]が来[く]る場[ば]合[あい]は、飛[ひ]行[こう]機[き]が遅[おく]れることがあります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 和（わ）＋風（ふう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You already know <kanji form="和">harmony</kanji> also stands for Japan itself, and <kanji form="風">wind</kanji> can mean the air or manner of a thing. So the Japanese manner of doing something is <vocabulary form="和風">Japanese-style</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルの部屋は和風で、とても静かです。
example_sentences.english: The rooms at this hotel are Japanese-style and very quiet.
example_sentences.furigana: このホテルの部屋[へや]は和[わ]風[ふう]で、とても静[しず]かです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は和風のお菓子をよく作ります。
example_sentences.english: She often makes Japanese-style sweets.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は和[わ]風[ふう]のお菓[か]子[し]をよく作[つく]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い和風の家に住むのが夢です。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to live in an old Japanese-style house.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い和[わ]風[ふう]の家[いえ]に住[す]むのが夢[ゆめ]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 和（わ）＋食（しょく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take that same <kanji form="和">harmony</kanji> that also stands for Japan, set it in front of <kanji form="食">food</kanji>, and you have the home-side cooking of rice, fish and miso that is <vocabulary form="和食">Japanese food</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母の家に泊まると、毎朝和食が出ます。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I stay at my grandmother's, I get Japanese food every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]の家[いえ]に泊[と]まると、毎[まい]朝[あさ]和[わ]食[しょく]が出[で]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は洋食ではなくて、和食にしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, let's have Japanese food, not Western.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は洋[よう]食[しょく]ではなくて、和[わ]食[しょく]にしましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人の友人を和食の店に連れて行きました。
example_sentences.english: I took a friend from abroad to a Japanese restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]の友[ゆう]人[じん]を和[わ]食[しょく]の店[みせ]に連[つ]れて行[い]きました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A waiter at a packed diner is asked for the list of dishes by <reading>many ewe</reading> at the same moment, a whole coach tour of sheep. He keeps shouting that the <vocabulary form="メニュー">menu</vocabulary> is printed on the back of the placemat, and the sheep just bleat <reading>メニュー</reading> louder.

example_sentences.japanese: このメニューは写真が多いので、外国人にも便利です。
example_sentences.english: This menu has lots of photos, so it's handy for visitors from abroad too.
example_sentences.furigana: このメニューは写[しゃ]真[しん]が多[おお]いので、外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]にも便[べん]利[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員さんに英語のメニューがあるか聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked the clerk if they had an English menu.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]さんに英[えい]語[ご]のメニューがあるか聞[き]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: メニューを見ながら、娘は二十分も悩んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My daughter has been agonizing over the menu for twenty whole minutes.
