example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で辞[じ]書[しょ]を二[に]冊[さつ]借[か]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 机の上に雑誌が何冊もあります。
example_sentences.english: There are quite a few magazines on the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に雑[ざっ]誌[し]が何[なん]冊[さつ]もあります。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 死（し）＋ぬ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Everything that was keeping you going, heartbeat, breath, the warmth in your hands, switches off one part at a time and does not come back. That final shutdown is what it means to <vocabulary>die</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父が去年死にました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather died last year.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]が去[きょ]年[ねん]死[し]にました。

example_sentences.japanese: この木は冬に死ぬ。
example_sentences.english: This tree dies in winter.
example_sentences.furigana: この木[き]は冬[ふゆ]に死[し]ぬ。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が死んで悲しい。
example_sentences.english: I'm sad that the dog died.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]が死[し]んで悲[かな]しい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 西（にし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>west</kanji> kanji is the entire <vocabulary>west</vocabulary> word by itself, so the two mean precisely the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every evening the sinking sun burns a glowing <reading>niche</reading> into the <vocabulary>west</vocabulary> wall of the shrine. The cats curl into that <reading>にし</reading>-shaped alcove for the last of the warmth.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅は西にあります。
example_sentences.english: The station is to the west.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]は西[にし]にあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは西へ歩きました。
example_sentences.english: We walked west.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは西[にし]へ歩[ある]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 山は西のほうにあります。
example_sentences.english: The mountain is in the western direction.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]は西[にし]のほうにあります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 呼（よ）＋ぶ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Shout a name across the room and the person turns; say it warmly with a date attached and they show up to dinner. Both are one verb: to <vocabulary>call or invite</vocabulary> someone.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi leans out the konbini door and shouts <reading>yo, boo</reading> at every regular he spots on the street. To <reading>よぶ</reading> is to <vocabulary>call someone over</vocabulary> until they come in.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は私をケンと呼ぶ。
example_sentences.english: My friend calls me Ken.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]は私[わたし]をケンと呼[よ]ぶ。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日友達を呼びます。
example_sentences.english: I'll invite a friend tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]友[とも]達[だち]を呼[よ]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はタクシーを呼んだ。
example_sentences.english: He called a taxi.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はタクシーを呼[よ]んだ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 泊（と）＋まる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Night drops on the mountain trail before you clear the ridge, and going down blind is how people get hurt. You take the bunk in the trail hut, boots by the door, and <vocabulary>stay overnight</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Boots by the door of the trail hut, you tell the dark ridge you will clear it <reading>tomorrow</reading>, <reading>とまる</reading>, and take the bunk to <vocabulary form="泊まる">stay overnight</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の家に泊まります。
example_sentences.english: I'll stay at a friend's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の家[いえ]に泊[と]まります。

example_sentences.japanese: どこに泊まりますか。
example_sentences.english: Where will you stay?
example_sentences.furigana: どこに泊[と]まりますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は彼の家に泊まる。
example_sentences.english: I'll stay at his place for the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は彼[かれ]の家[いえ]に泊[と]まる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 並（なら）＋べる.
items.mnemonic_text: Set them in a row: naraberu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take a shelf of jumbled cans and turn every label to face front, one behind the next, until they make a clean <kanji>row</kanji>. Setting objects out in a straight rank like that, by hand, is what it means <vocabulary>to line them up</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Night clerk <reading>Nara Bell</reading> turns every jumbled can on the shelf label-out, one behind the next, humming 「<reading>ならべる</reading>」 because her whole job is <vocabulary form="並べる">to line up</vocabulary> the cans.

example_sentences.japanese: 本を机に並べる。
example_sentences.english: I line up the books on the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 本[ほん]を机[つくえ]に並[なら]べる。

example_sentences.japanese: 母が野菜を並べます。
example_sentences.english: Mom lines up the vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]が野[や]菜[さい]を並[なら]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が椅子を並べた。
example_sentences.english: The child lined up the chairs.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が椅[い]子[す]を並[なら]べた。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 英（えい）＋語（ご）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hold one <kanji>language</kanji> under a waterfall of foreign words, let it swallow every one whole, and never let it spit a single word back. What pours out the bottom is <vocabulary>English</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木先生は英語を教えます。
example_sentences.english: Mr Suzuki teaches English.
example_sentences.furigana: 鈴木[すずき]先[せん]生[せい]は英[えい]語[ご]を教[おし]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は毎日英語を勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: She studies English every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は毎[まい]日[にち]英[えい]語[ご]を勉[べん]強[きょう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は英語が分かります。
example_sentences.english: I understand English.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は英[えい]語[ご]が分[わ]かります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 東（ひがし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Written on its own, the <kanji>east</kanji> kanji is already the whole <vocabulary>east</vocabulary> word, and the meaning does not shift at all.
items.reading_mnemonic: At dawn the sun forces a <reading>big gash</reading> of light through the <vocabulary>east</vocabulary> horizon. Hear that tearing sound and you are saying <reading>ひがし</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家は駅の東にあります。
example_sentences.english: My house is east of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の家[いえ]は駅[えき]の東[ひがし]にあります。

example_sentences.japanese: あの山は東にあります。
example_sentences.english: That mountain is to the east.
example_sentences.furigana: あの山[やま]は東[ひがし]にあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 東の空に月が見えます。
example_sentences.english: The moon can be seen in the eastern sky.
example_sentences.furigana: 東[ひがし]の空[そら]に月[つき]が見[み]えます。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 枚（まい）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The thinnest thing you can hold in your mind is one <kanji>sheet</kanji> of paper. Stamps, plates, shirts and pancakes all share that same flatness, so you tally them as <vocabulary>flat objects (counter)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 紙を三枚買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought three sheets of paper.
example_sentences.furigana: 紙[かみ]を三[さん]枚[まい]買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に切符を二枚あげました。
example_sentences.english: I gave two tickets to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]に切[きっ]符[ぷ]を二[に]枚[まい]あげました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は写真を一枚見せました。
example_sentences.english: She showed one photo.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は写[しゃ]真[しん]を一[いち]枚[まい]見[み]せました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 杯（はい）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Fill a cup to the brim, drink it dry, then set it back down, and that is one. Tally every time a bowl or glass gets emptied like that, and the total is your count of <vocabulary>cupfuls</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝コーヒーを二杯飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink two cups of coffee every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]コーヒーを二[に]杯[ばい]飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はお茶を三杯飲みました。
example_sentences.english: She drank three cups of tea.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はお茶[ちゃ]を三[さん]杯[ばい]飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 水を二杯飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I'll drink two glasses of water.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[みず]を二[に]杯[ばい]飲[の]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 南（みなみ）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>south</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>south</vocabulary> word are one and the same, with nothing added and nothing changed.
items.reading_mnemonic: Two horns poke out of the box lashed to the one warm, dry wall, where the goat inside basks as if in <reading>Miami</reading>, 「<reading>みなみ</reading>」, because that wall faces <vocabulary form="南">south</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 鳥は南へ飛びます。
example_sentences.english: The birds fly south.
example_sentences.furigana: 鳥[とり]は南[みなみ]へ飛[と]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 南はあちらです。
example_sentences.english: South is that way.
example_sentences.furigana: 南[みなみ]はあちらです。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬でも南は暖かいです。
example_sentences.english: Even in winter, the south is warm.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]でも南[みなみ]は暖[あたた]かいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 笑（わら）＋う.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your mouth pulls wide, your cheeks bunch up under your eyes, and air comes out of you in short barks you cannot hold back. That whole helpless reaction is what it means to <vocabulary>laugh / smile</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your mouth pulls wide and the air bursts out in short barks, like a <reading>walrus</reading> you cannot hold back, <reading>わらう</reading>, which is what it is to <vocabulary form="笑う">laugh</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が笑う。
example_sentences.english: My friend laughs.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]が笑[わら]う。

example_sentences.japanese: 面白い映画を見て笑う。
example_sentences.english: I laugh watching a funny movie.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[おも]白[しろ]い映[えい]画[が]を見[み]て笑[わら]う。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが今笑っている。
example_sentences.english: The baby is laughing now.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんが今[いま]笑[わら]っている。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 荷（に）kun'yomi ＋ 物（もつ）on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Any <kanji>thing</kanji> you own that isn't nailed down, crammed into two bags for the trip, becomes your <vocabulary>luggage</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は荷物を持って駅に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I carried my luggage to the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は荷[に]物[もつ]を持[も]って駅[えき]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: その荷物はとても重いです。
example_sentences.english: That luggage is very heavy.
example_sentences.furigana: その荷[に]物[もつ]はとても重[おも]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が私の荷物を運んでくれました。
example_sentences.english: He carried my luggage for me.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]が私[わたし]の荷[に]物[もつ]を運[はこ]んでくれました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 探（さが）＋す.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your ring slips off at the riverbank and vanishes into the reeds, so now you are on your knees parting every stalk. Going over a place inch by inch after one lost thing is what it means <vocabulary>to search for</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: On your knees at the riverbank, parting every reed for your lost ring, you mutter that this will take longer than the old Norse <reading>sagas</reading>, <reading>さがす</reading>; that is to <vocabulary form="探す">search for</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋で鍵を探す。
example_sentences.english: I look for my keys in the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]で鍵[かぎ]を探[さが]す。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で友達を探します。
example_sentences.english: I'll look for my friend at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で友[とも]達[だち]を探[さが]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日財布を探した。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday I searched for my wallet.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]財[さい]布[ふ]を探[さが]した。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 授（じゅ）＋業（ぎょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A set hour in which a teacher will <kanji>impart</kanji> the skills of a trade or <kanji>business</kanji> to you is a <vocabulary>class / lesson</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は授業があります。
example_sentences.english: I have class today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 授業は何時に始まりますか。
example_sentences.english: What time does class start?
example_sentences.furigana: 授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]は何[なん]時[じ]に始[はじ]まりますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は授業を休みました。
example_sentences.english: She skipped class.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]を休[やす]みました。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — きっぷ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 切符.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A paper <kanji>token</kanji> gets one clean <kanji>cut</kanji> from the conductor's punch as you board, and that notched stub is your <vocabulary>ticket</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki the tree spirit blocks the platform gate until you trade her a smoked <reading>kipper</reading> for the <reading>きっぷ</reading> she keeps calling your <vocabulary>ticket</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で切符を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a ticket at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で切[きっ]符[ぷ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は切符をかばんに入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put the ticket in my bag.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は切[きっ]符[ぷ]をかばんに入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: その切符を友達にあげました。
example_sentences.english: I gave that ticket to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: その切[きっ]符[ぷ]を友[とも]達[だち]にあげました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 船（ふね）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Something big enough to carry people and cargo can still ride on top of deep water instead of sinking into it. Anything that manages that is a <vocabulary>ship / boat</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Loaded with people and cargo yet riding high on the deep water, the <vocabulary form="船">ship</vocabulary> puffs smoke from its one <reading>funnel</reading>, and dockhands shout 「<reading>ふね</reading>」 as it floats past.

example_sentences.japanese: 船で海を渡ります。
example_sentences.english: We cross the sea by ship.
example_sentences.furigana: 船[ふね]で海[うみ]を渡[わた]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は今船に乗っています。
example_sentences.english: He's on the ship right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は今[いま]船[ふね]に乗[の]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: あの船は大きいです。
example_sentences.english: That ship over there is big.
example_sentences.furigana: あの船[ふね]は大[おお]きいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 登（のぼ）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The only way up to the tree house is the knotted rope, hand over hand, feet slipping on bark. Hauling yourself up something steep like that, using your whole body, is what it means <vocabulary>to climb</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>No bull</reading> could get up the knotted rope to the tree house, but you go hand over hand, feet slipping on bark, <reading>のぼる</reading>, to <vocabulary form="登る">climb</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は山に登ります。
example_sentences.english: I climb mountains.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は山[やま]に登[のぼ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日高い山に登った。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday I climbed a tall mountain.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]高[たか]い山[やま]に登[のぼ]った。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟と一緒に木に登る。
example_sentences.english: I climb a tree with my younger brother.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に木[き]に登[のぼ]る。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 散（さん）＋歩（ぽ）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Handakuon: 歩 ほ → ぽ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your feet stop flat every few steps and the path just <kanji>scatters</kanji> wherever it likes, aiming nowhere. A <kanji>walk</kanji> that loose and unplanned is you choosing to <vocabulary>take a walk</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は毎朝散歩する。
example_sentences.english: My father takes a walk every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]散[さん]歩[ぽ]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は夜散歩するのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like taking walks at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は夜[よる]散[さん]歩[ぽ]するのが好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と一緒に散歩する。
example_sentences.english: I take a walk with her.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に散[さん]歩[ぽ]する。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 言（こと）＋葉（ば）. Rendaku: 葉 は → ば.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Each <kanji>leaf</kanji> on the tree is one thing a person once chose to <kanji>say</kanji>, and the whole crown of them together is <vocabulary>language</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この言葉の意味が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand the meaning of this word.
example_sentences.furigana: この言[こと]葉[ば]の意[い]味[み]が分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は新しい言葉を教えます。
example_sentences.english: The teacher teaches a new word.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は新[あたら]しい言[こと]葉[ば]を教[おし]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい言葉を忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot a difficult word.
example_sentences.furigana: 難[むずか]しい言[こと]葉[ば]を忘[わす]れました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 絵（え）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A kid scribbles crayon over a whole page until the blob is unmistakably the family dog. Any marks made to stand for a real thing are a <vocabulary>drawing</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は絵が好きです。
example_sentences.english: My daughter likes drawing.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は絵[え]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は部屋で絵を見ました。
example_sentences.english: He looked at a picture in the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は部屋[へや]で絵[え]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: この絵は古いです。
example_sentences.english: This picture is old.
example_sentences.furigana: この絵[え]は古[ふる]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（ち）＋下（か）＋鉄（てつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Dig a rail line <kanji>down</kanji> into the <kanji>ground</kanji> and bolt the <kanji>iron</kanji> tracks together where daylight never reaches. A train that runs through that buried tube is a <vocabulary>subway</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は地下鉄に乗ります。
example_sentences.english: I take the subway.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は地[ち]下[か]鉄[てつ]に乗[の]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の近くに地下鉄があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a subway near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くに地[ち]下[か]鉄[てつ]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 地下鉄は便利です。
example_sentences.english: The subway is convenient.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[ち]下[か]鉄[てつ]は便[べん]利[り]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 選（えら）＋ぶ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Ten identical umbrellas stand in the rack, and your hand can take only one. Picking that one and walking past the other nine is what it means to <vocabulary>choose</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: In the school shop Sei picks up and puts back every single <reading>rubber</reading> on the shelf until the bell finally rings. To <reading>えらぶ</reading> is to <vocabulary>choose</vocabulary> one and let the rest go.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこの本を選びます。
example_sentences.english: I'll choose this book.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はこの本[ほん]を選[えら]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: どれを選びますか。
example_sentences.english: Which one will you choose?
example_sentences.furigana: どれを選[えら]びますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は赤い服を選んだ。
example_sentences.english: She chose the red clothes.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は赤[あか]い服[ふく]を選[えら]んだ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 隣（となり）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The house sharing your wall is so close you hear its radio through the plaster and its cat scratches at your door. That wall-to-wall closeness is your <vocabulary>neighbor</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every noon the cat from the house sharing your wall scratches at your door for a bite of your <reading>tuna rye</reading>, 「<reading>となり</reading>」, the lunch that keeps your <vocabulary form="隣">neighbor</vocabulary> close.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣に猫がいます。
example_sentences.english: There's a cat next to me.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]に猫[ねこ]がいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の部屋は静かです。
example_sentences.english: The room next door is quiet.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の部屋[へや]は静[しず]かです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の隣に座ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please sit down next to me.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の隣[となり]に座[すわ]ってください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 洗（せん）＋濯（たく）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>wash</kanji> here is not the dishes and not your hands, but a heaped basket of dirty shirts and socks. That one narrowed-down job is exactly what it means to <vocabulary>do laundry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、服を洗濯する。
example_sentences.english: I'll do laundry for my clothes today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、服[ふく]を洗[せん]濯[たく]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は毎朝洗濯する。
example_sentences.english: My mother does laundry every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]洗[せん]濯[たく]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 汚いシャツを洗濯する。
example_sentences.english: I'll wash the dirty shirt.
example_sentences.furigana: 汚[きたな]いシャツを洗[せん]濯[たく]する。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <reading>Zeus</reading> squeezes a whole storm cloud full of oranges until it rains down into one tall glass. What fills the glass is <vocabulary form="ジュース">juice</vocabulary>, <reading>ジュース</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 喫茶店でジュースを注文しました。
example_sentences.english: I ordered a juice at the coffee shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]でジュースを注[ちゅう]文[もん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんがジュースのコップを落とした。
example_sentences.english: The baby dropped the glass of juice.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんがジュースのコップを落[お]とした。

example_sentences.japanese: 車で来たので、私はジュースにします。
example_sentences.english: I came by car, so I'll have juice.
example_sentences.furigana: 車[くるま]で来[き]たので、私[わたし]はジュースにします。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A small child at the table starts to <reading>whine</reading> the moment the adults uncork the dark red bottle and fill their glasses. That guarded grown-up drink is <reading>ワイン</reading>, the <vocabulary form="ワイン">wine</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は毎晩ワインを少しだけ飲みます。
example_sentences.english: My father drinks just a little wine every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]ワインを少[すこ]しだけ飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉が結婚したので、みんなでワインを開けました。
example_sentences.english: My sister got married, so we all opened some wine.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]が結[けっ]婚[こん]したので、みんなでワインを開[あ]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの部屋にワインが置いてありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a bottle of wine waiting in the hotel room.
example_sentences.furigana: ホテルの部屋[へや]にワインが置[お]いてありました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every morning you loop a silk strip around your neck and tie it in a snug knot. That plain <reading>neck tie</reading> is a <reading>ネクタイ</reading>, a <vocabulary form="ネクタイ">necktie</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫のネクタイはどれも青い。
example_sentences.english: Every one of my husband's ties is blue.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]のネクタイはどれも青[あお]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いので、ネクタイを取ってもいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: It's hot, so feel free to take off your tie.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]いので、ネクタイを取[と]ってもいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子のネクタイが曲がっていたので、直してあげた。
example_sentences.english: My son's tie was crooked, so I straightened it for him.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]のネクタイが曲[ま]がっていたので、直[なお]してあげた。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <reading>skirt</reading> a puddle you swing wide around its edge. Swing your hips that way as you walk and the loose cloth that flares out from your waist is a <reading>スカート</reading>, a <vocabulary form="スカート">skirt</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 風が強いので、今日はスカートじゃなくてズボンにします。
example_sentences.english: It's windy, so today I'll wear trousers instead of a skirt.
example_sentences.furigana: 風[かぜ]が強[つよ]いので、今日[きょう]はスカートじゃなくてズボンにします。

example_sentences.japanese: このスカートは少しきついので、取り替えたいです。
example_sentences.english: This skirt is a little tight, so I'd like to exchange it.
example_sentences.furigana: このスカートは少[すこ]しきついので、取[と]り替[か]えたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘のスカートを洗濯したら、小さくなった。
example_sentences.english: I washed my daughter's skirt and it shrank.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]のスカートを洗[せん]濯[たく]したら、小[ちい]さくなった。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sit down, feed one leg in and then the other, and <reading>zip on</reading> the two cloth tubes. Fastened at your waist, that pair of tubes is <reading>ズボン</reading>, your <vocabulary form="ズボン">trousers</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と遊んだら、ズボンが泥で汚くなった。
example_sentences.english: I played with the dog, and my trousers got all muddy.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]と遊[あそ]んだら、ズボンが泥[どろ]で汚[きたな]くなった。

example_sentences.japanese: このズボンは長すぎるので、短くしてもらった。
example_sentences.english: These trousers were too long, so I had them shortened.
example_sentences.furigana: このズボンは長[なが]すぎるので、短[みじか]くしてもらった。

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車に乗るときは、ズボンのほうが便利です。
example_sentences.english: Trousers are more practical when you ride a bike.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]るときは、ズボンのほうが便[べん]利[り]です。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull the thick wool top down over your head and within a minute you start to <reading>sweat</reading>. The heavy knitted layer that does that to you is a <reading>セーター</reading>, a <vocabulary form="セーター">sweater</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は冬になると、同じ茶色のセーターを毎日着ている。
example_sentences.english: Every winter, my grandfather wears the same brown sweater every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は冬[ふゆ]になると、同[おな]じ茶[ちゃ]色[いろ]のセーターを毎[まい]日[にち]着[き]ている。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜は寒いかもしれないから、セーターを持って行って。
example_sentences.english: It might get cold at night, so take a sweater.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]は寒[さむ]いかもしれないから、セーターを持[も]って行[い]って。

example_sentences.japanese: このセーターを着ると、首が痒くなる。
example_sentences.english: When I wear this sweater, my neck gets itchy.
example_sentences.furigana: このセーターを着[き]ると、首[くび]が痒[かゆ]くなる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 靴（くつ）＋下（した）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hidden <kanji form="下">below</kanji> your <kanji form="靴">shoes</kanji> all day where nobody sees them, wrapped straight onto the foot, are your <vocabulary form="靴下">socks</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨で靴下が濡れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My socks got soaked in the rain.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]で靴[くつ]下[した]が濡[ぬ]れてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯した後で、白い靴下が見つかりません。
example_sentences.english: After doing the laundry, I can't find my white socks.
example_sentences.furigana: 洗[せん]濯[たく]した後[あと]で、白[しろ]い靴[くつ]下[した]が見[み]つかりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は赤い靴下が一番好きです。
example_sentences.english: My little brother likes red socks best.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は赤[あか]い靴[くつ]下[した]が一[いち]番[ばん]好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Slip the jewelled chain off your collarbones and the bare skin leaves your <reading>neck less</reading> dressed than before. Put the chain back to fix that and you are wearing a <reading>ネックレス</reading>, a <vocabulary form="ネックレス">necklace</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉のネックレスを借りてもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Can I borrow my sister's necklace?
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]のネックレスを借[か]りてもいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がネックレスで遊んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The cat is playing with my necklace.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]がネックレスで遊[あそ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: このネックレスは高すぎて、買うことができません。
example_sentences.english: This necklace is too expensive for me to buy.
example_sentences.furigana: このネックレスは高[たか]すぎて、買[か]うことができません。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Load a leather shoulder <reading>bag</reading> with your purse, phone and keys until its sides go round and firm. Carried as part of an outfit, that piece is a <reading>バッグ</reading>, a <vocabulary form="バッグ">bag</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の席にバッグを置かないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't put your bag on the train seats.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]車[しゃ]の席[せき]にバッグを置[お]かないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 財布と携帯と鍵を、小さいバッグに入れて出かけました。
example_sentences.english: I put my wallet, phone and keys in a small bag and headed out.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]と携[けい]帯[たい]と鍵[かぎ]を、小[ちい]さいバッグに入[い]れて出[で]かけました。

example_sentences.japanese: その素敵なバッグは、どこで買いましたか。
example_sentences.english: Where did you buy that lovely bag?
example_sentences.furigana: その素[す]敵[てき]なバッグは、どこで買[か]いましたか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The tailor runs the tape around your chest, reads the number, and <reading>sighs</reading>. That number, how big your clothes have to be, is your <reading>サイズ</reading>, your <vocabulary form="サイズ">size</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このシャツは、もう少し大きいサイズがありますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have this shirt in a slightly bigger size?
example_sentences.furigana: このシャツは、もう少[すこ]し大[おお]きいサイズがありますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の足はすぐ大きくなるので、靴のサイズがよく変わります。
example_sentences.english: Kids' feet grow fast, so their shoe size changes often.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]の足[あし]はすぐ大[おお]きくなるので、靴[くつ]のサイズがよく変[か]わります。

example_sentences.japanese: 箱のサイズを間違えて、荷物が入りませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I got the box size wrong, and the things wouldn't fit.
example_sentences.furigana: 箱[はこ]のサイズを間[ま]違[ちが]えて、荷[に]物[もつ]が入[はい]りませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 売（う）＋り＋場（ば）.
items.mnemonic_text: A place (場) to sell (売る): a sales counter.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The lit patch of <kanji form="場">place</kanji> on a shop floor where the staff do nothing but <kanji form="売">sell</kanji> one kind of goods is that department's <vocabulary form="売り場">sales floor</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 野菜売り場の店員は、とても親切です。
example_sentences.english: The clerk in the produce section is really kind.
example_sentences.furigana: 野[や]菜[さい]売[う]り場[ば]の店[てん]員[いん]は、とても親[しん]切[せつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートの地下の食べ物売り場は、いつも賑やかです。
example_sentences.english: The food floor in the department store basement is always busy.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートの地[ち]下[か]の食[た]べ物[もの]売[う]り場[ば]は、いつも賑[にぎ]やかです。

example_sentences.japanese: エスカレーターを降りると、すぐ右にかばん売り場があります。
example_sentences.english: Step off the escalator and the bag counter is right there on your right.
example_sentences.furigana: エスカレーターを降[お]りると、すぐ右[みぎ]にかばん売[う]り場[ば]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 注（ちゅう）＋文（もん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Pouring (注) a written request (文): an order.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="注">pour</kanji> one clear <kanji form="文">sentence</kanji> across the counter, telling the shop exactly what you want. That sentence is your <vocabulary form="注文">order</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員が注文を間違えて、カレーが来ました。
example_sentences.english: The clerk got the order wrong, and I was brought curry.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]が注[ちゅう]文[もん]を間[ま]違[ちが]えて、カレーが来[き]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄の注文はいつも同じラーメンなんです。
example_sentences.english: My older brother orders the same ramen every time.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]の注[ちゅう]文[もん]はいつも同[おな]じラーメンなんです。

example_sentences.japanese: 電話で弁当の注文をしました。
example_sentences.english: I placed an order for boxed lunches over the phone.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]で弁[べん]当[とう]の注[ちゅう]文[もん]をしました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 体（たい）＋重（じゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The body's (体) heaviness (重): body weight.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Step on a scale and it tells you one thing: how <kanji form="重">heavy</kanji> the <kanji form="体">body</kanji> you carry around all day has become. That one number is your <vocabulary form="体重">body weight</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の間に体重が増えてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I put on weight over the winter.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]の間[あいだ]に体[たい]重[じゅう]が増[ふ]えてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 医者によると、うちの猫は体重が重すぎるそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to the vet, our cat weighs too much.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]によると、うちの猫[ねこ]は体[たい]重[じゅう]が重[おも]すぎるそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 甘い物を食べなくなったら、体重が減りました。
example_sentences.english: Once I stopped eating sweets, my weight went down.
example_sentences.furigana: 甘[あま]い物[もの]を食[た]べなくなったら、体[たい]重[じゅう]が減[へ]りました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 熱（ねつ）.
items.mnemonic_text: A hot (熱) burning inside: a fever.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lay the back of your hand on a sick child's forehead and it comes away warm, like a pebble left out in full sun. That trapped warmth pouring off the skin is a <vocabulary form="熱">fever / heat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があるので、今日は早く寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I have a fever, so I'm going to bed early tonight.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねつ]があるので、今日[きょう]は早[はや]く寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの熱が夜になっても下がらない。
example_sentences.english: The baby's fever still hasn't come down, even now that it's night.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんの熱[ねつ]が夜[よる]になっても下[さ]がらない。

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが熱を持って、動かなくなった。
example_sentences.english: The computer got hot and stopped working.
example_sentences.furigana: パソコンが熱[ねつ]を持[も]って、動[うご]かなくなった。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — かぜをひく cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 風邪をひく.
items.mnemonic_text: Pulling (引く) the cold wind (風邪) in: to catch a cold.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull a <kanji form="邪">wicked</kanji> <kanji form="風">wind</kanji> deep into your chest and let it settle in as a three-day fever. Drawing bad air right inside you like that is what it means <vocabulary form="風邪をひく">to catch a cold</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cold gust off the river hooks Kaz like a fish on a line and reels him straight into bed. When chilled air <reading>hooks</reading> into you and holds on, that is <reading>かぜをひく</reading>, <vocabulary form="風邪をひく">to catch a cold</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨に濡れて、風邪をひいてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I got caught in the rain and ended up catching a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]に濡[ぬ]れて、風邪[かぜ]をひいてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪をひかないように、コートを着て出かけましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's put our coats on before we go out so we don't catch a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]をひかないように、コートを着[き]て出[で]かけましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が風邪をひいたので、会社を休みました。
example_sentences.english: My daughter caught a cold, so I took the day off work.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]が風邪[かぜ]をひいたので、会[かい]社[しゃ]を休[やす]みました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 手（しゅ）＋術（じゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="手術">surgery</vocabulary> is a trained <kanji form="手">hand</kanji> putting every bit of its learned <kanji form="術">technique</kanji> to work inside a body that has been opened up.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は来週、目の手術をすることになった。
example_sentences.english: It's been decided that my grandfather will have eye surgery next week.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は来[らい]週[しゅう]、目[め]の手[しゅ]術[じゅつ]をすることになった。

example_sentences.japanese: 手術の前の日は、何も食べてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You can't eat anything the day before surgery.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[しゅ]術[じゅつ]の前[まえ]の日[ひ]は、何[なに]も食[た]べてはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 手術が終わるまで、母は静かに待っていました。
example_sentences.english: My mother waited quietly until the surgery was over.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[しゅ]術[じゅつ]が終[お]わるまで、母[はは]は静[しず]かに待[ま]っていました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 入（にゅう）＋院（いん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Entering (入) the hospital (院): to be admitted.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="入">enter</kanji> the medical <kanji form="院">institution</kanji> as a patient, the doors fall shut, and you are not sleeping at home tonight. Ending up kept inside like that is what it means <vocabulary form="入院する">to be hospitalized</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は自転車から落ちて、一週間入院した。
example_sentences.english: My little brother fell off his bike and spent a week in the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]から落[お]ちて、一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]入[にゅう]院[いん]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 入院している間、毎日、本を読んでいました。
example_sentences.english: While I was in the hospital, I read books every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 入[にゅう]院[いん]している間[あいだ]、毎[まい]日[にち]、本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 入院するなら、何を持って行けばいいですか。
example_sentences.english: If I'm going into the hospital, what should I bring?
example_sentences.furigana: 入[にゅう]院[いん]するなら、何[なに]を持[も]って行[い]けばいいですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 退（たい）＋院（いん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Retreating (退) from the hospital (院): to be discharged.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The morning you can finally stand on your own, you <kanji form="退">withdraw</kanji> from the <kanji form="院">institution</kanji> and walk back out to the street. Getting yourself out the doors like that is <vocabulary form="退院する">to leave hospital</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人は明日退院するそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently the person in the next bed is leaving the hospital tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]は明日[あした]退[たい]院[いん]するそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 退院した日に、ラーメンを食べに行った。
example_sentences.english: The day I got out of the hospital, I went out for ramen.
example_sentences.furigana: 退[たい]院[いん]した日[ひ]に、ラーメンを食[た]べに行[い]った。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が退院する前に、部屋を掃除しておきます。
example_sentences.english: I'll clean the room before my husband comes home from the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]が退[たい]院[いん]する前[まえ]に、部屋[へや]を掃[そう]除[じ]しておきます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 薬（くすり）＋を＋飲（の）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: Drinking (飲む) the medicine (薬): to take medicine.
items.meaning_mnemonic: English says you take a pill; Japanese says you <kanji form="飲">drink</kanji> it. So even a dry tablet of <kanji form="薬">medicine</kanji> goes down the same way water does, and that is what it means <vocabulary form="薬を飲む">to take medicine</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 水と一緒に、この薬を飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please take this medicine with water.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[みず]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に、この薬[くすり]を飲[の]んでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は咳が止まらないので、毎晩薬を飲んでいる。
example_sentences.english: My older sister can't stop coughing, so she takes medicine every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は咳[せき]が止[と]まらないので、毎[まい]晩[ばん]薬[くすり]を飲[の]んでいる。

example_sentences.japanese: 苦い薬を飲んだ後で、チョコレートを食べた。
example_sentences.english: After taking the bitter medicine, I ate some chocolate.
example_sentences.furigana: 苦[にが]い薬[くすり]を飲[の]んだ後[あと]で、チョコレートを食[た]べた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 痛（いた）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: A sickness (疒) piercing through steadily: to ache.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A back tooth starts to throb late at night with nobody near it and nothing pressing on it. When a part of you sends up that steady, unasked-for pain on its own, it has begun <vocabulary form="痛む">to hurt / ache</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 痛 is 「いた」 from 痛い, so for a sore knee <vocabulary form="痛む">to hurt / ache</vocabulary> on its own is <reading>いたむ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、古い怪我が痛むんです。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, my old injury aches.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、古[ふる]い怪[け]我[が]が痛[いた]むんです。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は朝起きると、首が少し痛むそうです。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather says his neck aches a little when he gets up in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は朝[あさ]起[お]きると、首[くび]が少[すこ]し痛[いた]むそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たいジュースを飲みすぎて、お腹が痛みます。
example_sentences.english: I drank too much cold juice, and now my stomach hurts.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たいジュースを飲[の]みすぎて、お腹[なか]が痛[いた]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 目（め）＋が＋悪（わる）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: The eyes (目) being bad (悪い): poor vision.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When the <kanji form="目">eye</kanji> itself has gone <kanji form="悪">bad</kanji> and anything past your own arm is a blur, that is <vocabulary form="目が悪い">to have poor eyesight</vocabulary>. The final い is the ending that makes it an adjective.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は目が悪いので、夜は運転しません。
example_sentences.english: My father has poor eyesight, so he doesn't drive at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は目[め]が悪[わる]いので、夜[よる]は運[うん]転[てん]しません。

example_sentences.japanese: 暗い所で本を読むと、目が悪くなりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you read in the dark, your eyesight will get worse.
example_sentences.furigana: 暗[くら]い所[ところ]で本[ほん]を読[よ]むと、目[め]が悪[わる]くなりますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 目が悪いのに、眼鏡を家に忘れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My eyes are bad, and I still went and left my glasses at home.
example_sentences.furigana: 目[め]が悪[わる]いのに、眼鏡[めがね]を家[いえ]に忘[わす]れてしまいました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 耳（みみ）＋が＋遠（とお）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: The ears (耳) being far (遠い): hard of hearing.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="耳">ear</kanji> still works, but every sound now has to cross a long <kanji form="遠">distant</kanji> road to reach it and arrives faint. Sound landing that far off is <vocabulary form="耳が遠い">to be hard of hearing</vocabulary>, and the closing い marks it as an adjective.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は耳が遠いので、電話より手紙のほうが好きです。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is hard of hearing, so he prefers letters to phone calls.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は耳[みみ]が遠[とお]いので、電[でん]話[わ]より手[て]紙[がみ]のほうが好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は耳が遠くなってから、声が大きくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my mother started losing her hearing, her voice has gotten louder.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は耳[みみ]が遠[とお]くなってから、声[こえ]が大[おお]きくなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 耳が遠いはずの彼が、私たちの話を全部聞いていました。
example_sentences.english: He's supposed to be hard of hearing, but he heard every word we said.
example_sentences.furigana: 耳[みみ]が遠[とお]いはずの彼[かれ]が、私[わたし]たちの話[はなし]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]聞[き]いていました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <reading>スポーツマン</reading> is just the English words <reading>sports man</reading> pushed together, and a man whose whole week is training and games is an <vocabulary form="スポーツマン">athlete</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツマンになりたくて、毎朝公園を走っています。
example_sentences.english: I want to be an athlete, so I run in the park every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: スポーツマンになりたくて、毎[まい]朝[あさ]公[こう]園[えん]を走[はし]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は自分をスポーツマンだと言いますが、エレベーターしか使いません。
example_sentences.english: My older brother calls himself an athlete, but he only ever takes the elevator.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は自[じ]分[ぶん]をスポーツマンだと言[い]いますが、エレベーターしか使[つか]いません。

example_sentences.japanese: 有名なスポーツマンに会えて、息子はとても喜んでいました。
example_sentences.english: My son was thrilled to get to meet a famous athlete.
example_sentences.furigana: 有[ゆう]名[めい]なスポーツマンに会[あ]えて、息子[むすこ]はとても喜[よろこ]んでいました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 運（うん）＋動（どう）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: What it means <vocabulary form="運動する">to exercise</vocabulary> is to <kanji form="運">carry</kanji> your own body through enough hard <kanji form="動">motion</kanji> to leave you breathless.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は八十歳ですが、毎朝庭で運動しています。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather is eighty, but he exercises in the garden every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は八[はち]十[じゅう]歳[さい]ですが、毎[まい]朝[あさ]庭[にわ]で運[うん]動[どう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 運動しすぎて、次の日は階段を上がるのが大変でした。
example_sentences.english: I overdid the exercise, and the next day even climbing the stairs was a struggle.
example_sentences.furigana: 運[うん]動[どう]しすぎて、次[つぎ]の日[ひ]は階[かい]段[だん]を上[あ]がるのが大[たい]変[へん]でした。

example_sentences.japanese: 体重を減らすために、夕方は一時間運動することにしました。
example_sentences.english: To lose weight, I've decided to exercise for an hour every evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 体[たい]重[じゅう]を減[へ]らすために、夕[ゆう]方[がた]は一[いち]時[じ]間[かん]運[うん]動[どう]することにしました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A striker drops one shoulder and the goalkeeper lunges the wrong way like a <reading>sucker</reading>. Ninety minutes of fooling the last defender like that is <vocabulary form="サッカー">soccer</vocabulary>, <reading>サッカー</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日にサッカーをすると、服が泥で汚くなります。
example_sentences.english: If you play soccer on a rainy day, your clothes get filthy with mud.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]にサッカーをすると、服[ふく]が泥[どろ]で汚[きたな]くなります。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の友達は、野球よりサッカーのほうが好きだと言っていました。
example_sentences.english: My friend from abroad said they like soccer more than baseball.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の友[とも]達[だち]は、野[や]球[きゅう]よりサッカーのほうが好[す]きだと言[い]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: サッカーを見ているとき、祖母はいつも一番大きい声を出します。
example_sentences.english: When we watch soccer, my grandmother is always the loudest one.
example_sentences.furigana: サッカーを見[み]ているとき、祖[そ]母[ぼ]はいつも一[いち]番[ばん]大[おお]きい声[こえ]を出[だ]します。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A street <reading>busker</reading> gives up on coins. He nails his hat to a lamppost, lobs a rubber ball through it again and again, and that hooped, hand-thrown game is <vocabulary form="バスケットボール">basketball</vocabulary>, <reading>バスケットボール</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 身長が低くても、バスケットボールは上手になれますよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you're short, you can still get good at basketball.
example_sentences.furigana: 身[しん]長[ちょう]が低[ひく]くても、バスケットボールは上手[じょうず]になれますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 体育の授業でバスケットボールをしたので、足が痛いです。
example_sentences.english: We played basketball in PE class, so my legs hurt.
example_sentences.furigana: 体[たい]育[いく]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]でバスケットボールをしたので、足[あし]が痛[いた]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、会社の仲間とバスケットボールをすることになりました。
example_sentences.english: It's been arranged that I'll play basketball with some coworkers this weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、会[かい]社[しゃ]の仲[なか]間[ま]とバスケットボールをすることになりました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two <reading>tenants</reading> on either side of a net argue over every bounce by whacking a ball back across it. That racket-swung quarrel is <vocabulary form="テニス">tennis</vocabulary>, <reading>テニス</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: テニスって、思ったより難しいですね。
example_sentences.english: Tennis is harder than I thought, isn't it?
example_sentences.furigana: テニスって、思[おも]ったより難[むずか]しいですね。

example_sentences.japanese: 暑すぎて、テニスをしている間に水を三本も飲みました。
example_sentences.english: It was so hot that I drank three whole bottles of water while playing tennis.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]すぎて、テニスをしている間[あいだ]に水[みず]を三[さん]本[ぼん]も飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は六十歳からテニスを習い始めました。
example_sentences.english: My aunt started taking tennis lessons at sixty.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]は六[ろく]十[じゅう]歳[さい]からテニスを習[なら]い始[はじ]めました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A ball sails off the tee, clears a wide sandy <reading>gulf</reading> of a bunker, and drops beside a little flag. Walking eighteen of those crossings in an afternoon is <vocabulary form="ゴルフ">golf</vocabulary>, <reading>ゴルフ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日になると、夫はいつもゴルフに出かけます。
example_sentences.english: When Sunday comes around, my husband always heads out to play golf.
example_sentences.furigana: 日[にち]曜[よう]日[び]になると、夫[おっと]はいつもゴルフに出[で]かけます。

example_sentences.japanese: ゴルフをするために、朝四時に起きる人もいます。
example_sentences.english: Some people get up at four in the morning just to play golf.
example_sentences.furigana: ゴルフをするために、朝[あさ]四[し]時[じ]に起[お]きる人[ひと]もいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はお客さんとゴルフをするのも仕事だと言っています。
example_sentences.english: He says playing golf with clients is part of his job too.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はお客[きゃく]さんとゴルフをするのも仕[し]事[ごと]だと言[い]っています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 水（すい）＋泳（えい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A lane of nothing but <kanji form="水">water</kanji>, and you crossing it end to end under your own power with just arms and legs, is what <vocabulary form="水泳">swimming</vocabulary> is.

example_sentences.japanese: 水泳は体にとてもいいと、医者に言われました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor told me swimming is really good for my body.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[すい]泳[えい]は体[からだ]にとてもいいと、医[い]者[しゃ]に言[い]われました。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は顔を水に入れるのが怖くて、水泳の授業が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: My son is scared to put his face in the water, so he hates swimming class.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は顔[かお]を水[みず]に入[い]れるのが怖[こわ]くて、水[すい]泳[えい]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]が嫌[きら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 水泳を始めてから、だんだん体が強くなってきました。
example_sentences.english: Since I took up swimming, my body has been getting stronger little by little.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[すい]泳[えい]を始[はじ]めてから、だんだん体[からだ]が強[つよ]くなってきました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Strap two long boards to your boots, point the tips downhill, and let them run over the snow with a <reading>squeaky</reading> hiss all the way to the bottom. That boarded slide is <vocabulary form="スキー">skiing</vocabulary>, <reading>スキー</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: スキーに行くなら、暖かい手袋を持って行ったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: If you're going skiing, you'd better take warm gloves.
example_sentences.furigana: スキーに行[い]くなら、暖[あたた]かい手[て]袋[ぶくろ]を持[も]って行[い]ったほうがいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: スキーの最初の日は、立っているより座っている時間が長かったです。
example_sentences.english: On my first day of skiing, I spent more time sitting than standing.
example_sentences.furigana: スキーの最[さい]初[しょ]の日[ひ]は、立[た]っているより座[すわ]っている時[じ]間[かん]が長[なが]かったです。

example_sentences.japanese: この山は雪が多いので、冬はスキーをする人で賑やかになります。
example_sentences.english: This mountain gets lots of snow, so in winter it's busy with skiers.
example_sentences.furigana: この山[やま]は雪[ゆき]が多[おお]いので、冬[ふゆ]はスキーをする人[ひと]で賑[にぎ]やかになります。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <reading>dunce</reading> sent to stand in the corner gets bored and starts swaying, then spinning, then throwing shapes to music only he can hear. Moving your body in time like that is <vocabulary form="ダンス">dance</vocabulary>, <reading>ダンス</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は毎週、部屋で新しいダンスを練習しています。
example_sentences.english: Every week my older sister practices a new dance in her room.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は毎[まい]週[しゅう]、部屋[へや]で新[あたら]しいダンスを練[れん]習[しゅう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のダンスを見て、妹は笑いすぎて泣いていました。
example_sentences.english: My little sister watched me dance and laughed so hard she cried.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]のダンスを見[み]て、妹[いもうと]は笑[わら]いすぎて泣[な]いていました。

example_sentences.japanese: このダンスは簡単なので、子供でもすぐ覚えられます。
example_sentences.english: This dance is simple, so even kids can pick it up right away.
example_sentences.furigana: このダンスは簡[かん]単[たん]なので、子[こ]供[ども]でもすぐ覚[おぼ]えられます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A concert announcer rolls the name of the big lacquered keyboard out slow and grand, <reading>pee-AH-no</reading>, and the lid lifts back off eighty-eight keys. That strung box of felt hammers is a <vocabulary form="ピアノ">piano</vocabulary>, <reading>ピアノ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は五歳のときから、先生にピアノを習っています。
example_sentences.english: My daughter has been taking piano lessons from a teacher since she was five.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は五[ご]歳[さい]のときから、先[せん]生[せい]にピアノを習[なら]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノは重いので、三階まで運ぶのに四人かかりました。
example_sentences.english: The piano was so heavy it took four people to carry it up to the third floor.
example_sentences.furigana: ピアノは重[おも]いので、三[さん]階[かい]まで運[はこ]ぶのに四[よ]人[にん]かかりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の家から、毎晩下手なピアノが聞こえてきます。
example_sentences.english: Every night I hear clumsy piano playing from the house next door.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の家[いえ]から、毎[まい]晩[ばん]下手[へた]なピアノが聞[き]こえてきます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The six strings stretched over the flat wooden box are so sticky they might as well be strung with <reading>gee, tar</reading>, yet you still strum them for a tune. That sticky-stringed box is a <vocabulary form="ギター">guitar</vocabulary>, <reading>ギター</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: ギターを持って、公園で歌っている青年がいました。
example_sentences.english: There was a young man in the park, singing with a guitar.
example_sentences.furigana: ギターを持[も]って、公[こう]園[えん]で歌[うた]っている青[せい]年[ねん]がいました。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 将（しょう）on'yomi ＋ 来（らい）on'yomi ＋ の ＋ 夢（ゆめ）kun'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A future's (将来) dream (夢): one's aspiration.
items.furigana: 将[しょう]来[らい]の夢[ゆめ]

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 読（どく）＋書（しょ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Reading (読) books (書): reading as a hobby.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sitting down with pages someone else took the trouble to <kanji form="書">write</kanji>, and working through them line by line to <kanji form="読">read</kanji> them, is <vocabulary form="読書">reading (books)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.english: My reading time is while I'm riding the train.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 小（しょう）＋説（せつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A small (小) telling (説): a novel.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take one writer's <kanji form="小">small</kanji>, made-up <kanji form="説">explanation</kanji> of how some invented life might go, then stretch it across three hundred pages. That padded little theory is a <vocabulary form="小説">novel</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: この小[しょう]説[せつ]は長[なが]すぎて、まだ半[はん]分[ぶん]しか読[よ]んでいません。

example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]が若[わか]いときに書[か]いた小[しょう]説[せつ]を、引[ひ]き出[だ]しの中[なか]で見[み]つけました。

example_sentences.japanese: 小説の最後が悲しくて、喫茶店で泣いてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The ending of the novel was so sad that I cried in a coffee shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 小[しょう]説[せつ]の最[さい]後[ご]が悲[かな]しくて、喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]で泣[な]いてしまいました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Kids too broke for a real board split one stick of <reading>gum</reading> as the prize and make up rules for winning it on the spot. Any contest run like that is a <vocabulary form="ゲーム">game</vocabulary>, <reading>ゲーム</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 釣（つ）＋り.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sit on the riverbank, bait a hook, and drop it on a long line into the water. Waiting like that for something below to pull is <vocabulary form="釣り">fishing</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A grey desk machine that grinds through a million sums a second is a thing that <reading>computes</reading>, and the flat everyday name for it is <vocabulary form="コンピューター">computer</vocabulary>, <reading>コンピューター</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <reading>enter a net</reading> stretched over the whole planet, and every fact anyone ever wrote hangs caught in its mesh, in reach from wherever you stand. items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 皿（さら）.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 困（こま）＋る.
