example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前に看板があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a sign in front of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]に看[かん]板[ばん]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 美（び）＋術（じゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take raw <kanji>beauty</kanji>, the kind that just happens in a sunset, and make a person sit down and build it on purpose; that deliberate version is <vocabulary>art</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は美術が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like art.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は美[び]術[じゅつ]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は学校で美術を勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: She is studying art at school.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は学[がっ]校[こう]で美[び]術[じゅつ]を勉[べん]強[きょう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: この美術は有名です。
example_sentences.english: This art is famous.
example_sentences.furigana: この美[び]術[じゅつ]は有[ゆう]名[めい]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 世（せ）＋界（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Generations (世) bounded (界): the whole world.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The people of one <kanji>generation</kanji>, sealed together inside a single <kanji>boundary</kanji> of years, all live in one <vocabulary>world</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界で一番高い山はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the tallest mountain in the world?
example_sentences.furigana: 世[せ]界[かい]で一[いち]番[ばん]高[たか]い山[やま]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は船で世界を旅行しました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather traveled around the world by ship.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は船[ふね]で世[せ]界[かい]を旅[りょ]行[こう]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は地図を見ながら、世界の海の名前を覚えています。
example_sentences.english: My daughter is memorizing the names of the world's oceans while looking at a map.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は地[ち]図[ず]を見[み]ながら、世[せ]界[かい]の海[うみ]の名[な]前[まえ]を覚[おぼ]えています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 法（ほう）＋律（りつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A rule (法) set in rhythm (律): the law.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every rule the whole country has agreed to write down and back with courts, police and prisons, instead of leaving it to a friendly handshake, is <vocabulary>law</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律で、ここに車を止めてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: By law, you can't park your car here.
example_sentences.furigana: 法[ほう]律[りつ]で、ここに車[くるま]を止[と]めてはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 法律の本は、言葉がとても難しいです。
example_sentences.english: The words in law books are really difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 法[ほう]律[りつ]の本[ほん]は、言[こと]葉[ば]がとても難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から法律が変わるので、会社は準備しています。
example_sentences.english: The law changes next month, so the company is getting ready.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]から法[ほう]律[りつ]が変[か]わるので、会[かい]社[しゃ]は準[じゅん]備[び]しています。

items.word_type: な adjective, する verb, transitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 心（しん）＋配（ぱい）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Handakuon: 配 はい → ぱい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji>heart</kanji> gets <kanji>parcelled out</kanji>, a scrap of it pinned to every bad thing that might happen. Carry it stretched that thin and you <vocabulary>worry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は私の仕事を心配すると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think my mother worries about my job.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は私[わたし]の仕[し]事[ごと]を心[しん]配[ぱい]すると思[おも]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は試験のことを心配するでしょう。
example_sentences.english: He'll probably worry about the exam.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は試[し]験[けん]のことを心[しん]配[ぱい]するでしょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は私の体を心配すると言いました。
example_sentences.english: My father said he worries about my health.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は私[わたし]の体[からだ]を心[しん]配[ぱい]すると言[い]いました。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 値（ね）kun'yomi ＋ 段（だん）on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every item on the shelf is standing on one <kanji>step</kanji> of a tall staircase, and how far up its step sits is the thing's <vocabulary>price</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この店の値段は安いです。
example_sentences.english: The prices at this shop are cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]の値[ね]段[だん]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 卵の値段が高くなりました。
example_sentences.english: The price of eggs has gone up.
example_sentences.furigana: 卵[たまご]の値[ね]段[だん]が高[たか]くなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 値段を聞きましたか。
example_sentences.english: Did you ask the price?
example_sentences.furigana: 値[ね]段[だん]を聞[き]きましたか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 結（けっ）＋婚（こん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 結 けつ → けっ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two people <kanji>knot</kanji> their lives together into one <kanji>marriage</kanji> that is built never to come undone. Tie that knot and you <vocabulary>marry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は来月結婚する。
example_sentences.english: She's getting married next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は来[らい]月[げつ]結[けっ]婚[こん]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は彼女と結婚するだろう。
example_sentences.english: He'll probably marry her.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は彼[かの]女[じょ]と結[けっ]婚[こん]するだろう。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は来年結婚するだろう。
example_sentences.english: My older brother will probably get married next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は来[らい]年[ねん]結[けっ]婚[こん]するだろう。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（ち）＋図（ず）＋帳（ちょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Bind one <kanji>map</kanji> of every stretch of <kanji>ground</kanji> into a single fat <kanji>notebook</kanji>, and that book is an <vocabulary>atlas</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこの地図帳が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like this atlas.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はこの地[ち]図[ず]帳[ちょう]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 地図帳は机の上にあります。
example_sentences.english: The atlas is on the desk.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[ち]図[ず]帳[ちょう]は机[つくえ]の上[うえ]にあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は新しい地図帳を買いました。
example_sentences.english: My older brother bought a new atlas.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は新[あたら]しい地[ち]図[ず]帳[ちょう]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 貼（は）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You press a stamp onto the envelope's corner and smooth it until it will not lift. Fixing one flat thing onto another by hand is to <vocabulary>stick</vocabulary> it there.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi slaps a name sticker reading <reading>Harold</reading> onto every onigiri on the shelf and rubs each one down, 「<reading>はる</reading>」, and pressing a label flat onto a surface is to <vocabulary>paste</vocabulary> it on.

example_sentences.japanese: 箱に紙を貼ります。
example_sentences.english: I stick paper on the box.
example_sentences.furigana: 箱[はこ]に紙[かみ]を貼[は]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓に紙を貼りました。
example_sentences.english: I stuck paper on the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]に紙[かみ]を貼[は]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙に切手を貼ります。
example_sentences.english: I stick a stamp on the letter.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[て]紙[がみ]に切[きっ]手[て]を貼[は]ります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 伝（でん）＋統（とう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Passed down (伝) and unified (統): tradition.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When one <kanji>overall</kanji> way of doing things is <kanji>transmit</kanji>ted from each parent to each child for ten generations without a gap, that unbroken handoff is <vocabulary>tradition</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年、祖母と伝統の料理を作ります。
example_sentences.english: Every year I make traditional dishes with my grandmother.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]年[ねん]、祖[そ]母[ぼ]と伝[でん]統[とう]の料[りょう]理[り]を作[つく]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: この店には百年の伝統があります。
example_sentences.english: This shop has a hundred years of tradition.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]には百[ひゃく]年[ねん]の伝[でん]統[とう]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 若い人は、あまり伝統の服を着なくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Young people don't wear traditional clothes much anymore.
example_sentences.furigana: 若[わか]い人[ひと]は、あまり伝[でん]統[とう]の服[ふく]を着[き]なくなりました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 歳（さい）.
items.mnemonic_text: Count of years of age: sai.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every birthday you get through stacks one more ring of <kanji>age</kanji> onto the pile inside you. Count the rings in that stack and the number is how many <vocabulary>years old</vocabulary> you are.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は何歳ですか。
example_sentences.english: How old are you?
example_sentences.furigana: 君[きみ]は何[なん]歳[さい]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は来年二十歳になります。
example_sentences.english: She'll turn twenty next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は来[らい]年[ねん]二十歳[はたち]になります。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は八十歳ですが、元気です。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother is eighty, but she's healthy.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は八[はち]十[じゅう]歳[さい]ですが、元[げん]気[き]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 置（お）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You set the heavy box down on the floor exactly where you want it, then lift your hands away. Leaving a thing to rest in a chosen spot is to <vocabulary>put</vocabulary> it there.
items.reading_mnemonic: You set the heavy <reading>oak</reading> box down on the floor exactly where you want it, 「<reading>おく</reading>」, and lift your hands away, which is to <vocabulary form="置く">put</vocabulary> it there.

example_sentences.japanese: かばんをここに置いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put your bag here.
example_sentences.furigana: かばんをここに置[お]いてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 本をテーブルの上に置きました。
example_sentences.english: I put the book on the table.
example_sentences.furigana: 本[ほん]をテーブルの上[うえ]に置[お]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 鍵をどこに置いたか忘れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot where I put my keys.
example_sentences.furigana: 鍵[かぎ]をどこに置[お]いたか忘[わす]れました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 茶（ちゃ）＋碗（わん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take that steaming <kanji>tea</kanji> cup and make it deep and wide enough to pack with a scoop of rice, and it turns into a <vocabulary>rice bowl</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは茶碗です。
example_sentences.english: This is a rice bowl.
example_sentences.furigana: これは茶[ちゃ]碗[わん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 茶碗にご飯を入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put rice in the rice bowl.
example_sentences.furigana: 茶[ちゃ]碗[わん]にご飯[はん]を入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: テーブルの上に茶碗があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a rice bowl on the table.
example_sentences.furigana: テーブルの上[うえ]に茶[ちゃ]碗[わん]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 数（すう）＋学（がく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take the <kanji>study</kanji> a child does under that cover and point it only at <kanji>number</kanji>s, and the pages fill with nothing but <vocabulary>mathematics</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、数学の宿題をしました。
example_sentences.english: I did my math homework today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、数[すう]学[がく]の宿[しゅく]題[だい]をしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は数学が好きです。
example_sentences.english: She likes mathematics.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は数[すう]学[がく]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 数学のテストは難しかったです。
example_sentences.english: The math test was difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 数[すう]学[がく]のテストは難[むずか]しかったです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 鳴（な）＋る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A phone left face-down on the konbini counter lets out its full-volume <kanji>cry</kanji> with nobody near it. A thing sounding off by itself is what it means to <vocabulary>ring</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A shop cat creeping along the <reading>narrow</reading> konbini counter freezes when the face-down phone goes 「<reading>なる</reading>」 at full volume, a thing left alone to <vocabulary form="鳴る">ring</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話が鳴りました。
example_sentences.english: The phone rang.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]が鳴[な]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 時計が鳴ると、起きます。
example_sentences.english: When the clock rings, I get up.
example_sentences.furigana: 時計[とけい]が鳴[な]ると、起[お]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯が鳴っています。
example_sentences.english: My phone is ringing.
example_sentences.furigana: 携[けい]帯[たい]が鳴[な]っています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 練（れん）＋習（しゅう）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Running the same scale, the same kick, the same brush stroke over and over until your hands do it without you watching is what it means <vocabulary>to practice</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日日本語を練習する。
example_sentences.english: I practice Japanese every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]日本[にほん]語[ご]を練[れん]習[しゅう]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は毎朝歌を練習する。
example_sentences.english: My older sister practices singing every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]歌[うた]を練[れん]習[しゅう]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は公園でスポーツを練習することが好きだ。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother likes practicing sports at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は公[こう]園[えん]でスポーツを練[れん]習[しゅう]することが好[す]きだ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 一（いっ）＋緒（しょ）＋に, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 一 いち → いっ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lash the whole load onto a single leather <kanji>thong</kanji> and cinch it into <kanji>one</kanji> tight bundle. Everything that now rides that one strap travels <vocabulary>together</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と一緒に映画を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I watched a movie together with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に晩ご飯を食べませんか。
example_sentences.english: Won't you eat dinner with me?
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いっ]緒[しょ]に晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べませんか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と一緒に公園を歩きました。
example_sentences.english: I walked through the park together with her.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に公[こう]園[えん]を歩[ある]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 国（こく）＋際（さい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Countries (国) meeting at the border (際): international.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything that happens right on the <kanji>edge</kanji> where one <kanji>country</kanji>'s wall butts against the next one's is, by definition, <vocabulary>international</vocabulary>.
items.description: Almost always used stuck in front of another noun, the way a label is, rather than standing on its own as a full noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は国際会議で英語を話しました。
example_sentences.english: She spoke English at an international conference.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は国[こく]際[さい]会[かい]議[ぎ]で英[えい]語[ご]を話[はな]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は国際問題の本をたくさん読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My older brother reads lots of books on international issues.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は国[こく]際[さい]問[もん]題[だい]の本[ほん]をたくさん読[よ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 国際社会の中で、日本は何ができるでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: What can Japan do within the international community?
example_sentences.furigana: 国[こく]際[さい]社[しゃ]会[かい]の中[なか]で、日本[にほん]は何[なに]ができるでしょうか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 趣（しゅ）＋味（み）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The one thing you keep doing purely for its <kanji>flavour</kanji>, chasing the <kanji>gist</kanji> of it while nobody pays you a cent, is your <vocabulary>hobby</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の趣味は料理です。
example_sentences.english: My hobby is cooking.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の趣[しゅ]味[み]は料[りょう]理[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの趣味は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What is your hobby?
example_sentences.furigana: あなたの趣[しゅ]味[み]は何[なに]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の趣味は写真です。
example_sentences.english: His hobby is photography.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の趣[しゅ]味[み]は写[しゃ]真[しん]です。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 箸（はし）.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two slim tapered sticks you pinch in one hand to carry food up to your mouth are <vocabulary>chopsticks</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi pinches two slim tapered sticks in one hand and lifts <reading>hash</reading> browns up to his mouth, 「<reading>はし</reading>」, bite by bite with his <vocabulary form="箸">chopsticks</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は箸で肉を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat meat with chopsticks.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は箸[はし]で肉[にく]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は箸を使いました。
example_sentences.english: She used chopsticks.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は箸[はし]を使[つか]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この箸は新しいです。
example_sentences.english: These chopsticks are new.
example_sentences.furigana: この箸[はし]は新[あたら]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 権（けん）＋利（り）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Authority (権) that benefits (利): a right.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>benefit</kanji> the law guarantees you from birth, one that no ruler or vote is allowed to strip away, is a <vocabulary>right (entitlement)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供にも遊ぶ権利があります。
example_sentences.english: Children have the right to play, too.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]にも遊[あそ]ぶ権[けん]利[り]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 働く人には休む権利があります。
example_sentences.english: Working people have the right to rest.
example_sentences.furigana: 働[はたら]く人[ひと]には休[やす]む権[けん]利[り]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: お金を払ったので、私たちにはこの席に座る権利があります。
example_sentences.english: We paid, so we have every right to sit in these seats.
example_sentences.furigana: お金[かね]を払[はら]ったので、私[わたし]たちにはこの席[せき]に座[すわ]る権[けん]利[り]があります。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You post a paper letter through a slot and it thumps onto a desk across the planet before the flap has swung back. <reading>Mail</reading> that fast is <vocabulary form="メール">email</vocabulary>, and the slot clacks out <reading>メール</reading> every time one lands.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の時間が変わったので、みんなにメールで知らせました。
example_sentences.english: The meeting time changed, so I let everyone know by email.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]の時[じ]間[かん]が変[か]わったので、みんなにメールで知[し]らせました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女からのメールを待っていて、昨日はあまり寝られませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I was waiting for an email from my girlfriend, so I barely slept last night.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]からのメールを待[ま]っていて、昨日[きのう]はあまり寝[ね]られませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 間違えて、姉に送るメールを先生に送ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I accidentally sent my teacher an email that was meant for my older sister.
example_sentences.furigana: 間[ま]違[ちが]えて、姉[あね]に送[おく]るメールを先[せん]生[せい]に送[おく]ってしまいました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You tap in an address and a whole shop unfolds where your blank screen was, shelves and counter and a visitor book by the door. A <reading>sight</reading> you can step into like that is a <vocabulary form="サイト">website</vocabulary>, and it goes by <reading>サイト</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: このサイトは色が暗くて、読みにくいです。
example_sentences.english: This website uses dark colors, so it's hard to read.
example_sentences.furigana: このサイトは色[いろ]が暗[くら]くて、読[よ]みにくいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館のサイトで、土曜日の席を予約しました。
example_sentences.english: I reserved seats for Saturday on the cinema's website.
example_sentences.furigana: 映[えい]画[が]館[かん]のサイトで、土[ど]曜[よう]日[び]の席[せき]を予[よ]約[やく]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は猫の写真のサイトを作っています。
example_sentences.english: My aunt runs a website full of cat photos.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]は猫[ねこ]の写[しゃ]真[しん]のサイトを作[つく]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You press one bright square on the glass and it does exactly one job — counts your steps, nothing else. A small program you <reading>apply</reading> to a single task is an <vocabulary form="アプリ">app</vocabulary>, and every square on that screen is one <reading>アプリ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリがあれば、電車の時間がすぐ分かります。
example_sentences.english: With this app, you can check train times right away.
example_sentences.furigana: このアプリがあれば、電[でん]車[しゃ]の時[じ]間[かん]がすぐ分[わ]かります。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいアプリを入れたら、携帯が遅くなりました。
example_sentences.english: After I installed a new app, my phone got slow.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しいアプリを入[い]れたら、携[けい]帯[たい]が遅[おそ]くなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語のアプリで、毎晩寝る前に漢字を十個練習しています。
example_sentences.english: Every night before bed, I practice ten kanji with a Japanese app.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]のアプリで、毎[まい]晩[ばん]寝[ね]る前[まえ]に漢[かん]字[じ]を十[じゅう]個[こ]練[れん]習[しゅう]しています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 伝（でん）＋言（ごん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="伝言">message (spoken)</vocabulary> is a run of <kanji form="言">words</kanji> you hand to one person so they can <kanji form="伝">carry it along</kanji> to the next, mouth to mouth, with nothing written down.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんから「少し遅れる」という伝言がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a message from Tanaka-san saying he'd be a little late.
example_sentences.furigana: 田中[たなか]さんから「少[すこ]し遅[おく]れる」という伝[でん]言[ごん]がありました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がいなかったので、他の先生に伝言を頼みました。
example_sentences.english: My teacher wasn't there, so I asked another teacher to pass on a message.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]がいなかったので、他[ほか]の先[せん]生[せい]に伝[でん]言[ごん]を頼[たの]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 奥さんからの伝言を、ご主人に伝えるのを忘れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to pass his wife's message on to him.
example_sentences.furigana: 奥[おく]さんからの伝[でん]言[ごん]を、ご主[しゅ]人[じん]に伝[つた]えるのを忘[わす]れてしまいました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 画（が）＋面（めん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A drawn (画) face (面): a screen.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="画面">screen (display)</vocabulary> is the flat <kanji form="面">face</kanji> of the device, and every <kanji form="画">picture</kanji> it shows is painted straight onto that face.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯を落として、画面が壊れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped my phone and broke the screen.
example_sentences.furigana: 携[けい]帯[たい]を落[お]として、画[が]面[めん]が壊[こわ]れてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 画面が明るすぎて、夜は目が痛くなります。
example_sentences.english: The screen is too bright, so my eyes hurt at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 画[が]面[めん]が明[あか]るすぎて、夜[よる]は目[め]が痛[いた]くなります。

example_sentences.japanese: 教室の後ろの席からは、画面がよく見えません。
example_sentences.english: From the seats at the back of the classroom, you can't see the screen well.
example_sentences.furigana: 教[きょう]室[しつ]の後[うし]ろの席[せき]からは、画[が]面[めん]がよく見[み]えません。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The metal box on your desk is the hard part of the machine; the <reading>soft</reading> part is the lists of instructions inside, which you can rewrite without turning a single screw. That rewritable half is <vocabulary form="ソフト">software</vocabulary>, and you call it <reading>ソフト</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: このソフトを使えば、写真の色を簡単に変えられます。
example_sentences.english: With this software, you can easily change the colors in a photo.
example_sentences.furigana: このソフトを使[つか]えば、写[しゃ]真[しん]の色[いろ]を簡[かん]単[たん]に変[か]えられます。

example_sentences.japanese: 古いパソコンには、新しいソフトが入りません。
example_sentences.english: New software won't install on the old computer.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]いパソコンには、新[あたら]しいソフトが入[はい]りません。

example_sentences.japanese: ソフトの使い方が複雑すぎて、店員に三回も質問しました。
example_sentences.english: The software was so complicated to use that I asked the store clerk about it three times.
example_sentences.furigana: ソフトの使[つか]い方[かた]が複[ふく]雑[ざつ]すぎて、店[てん]員[いん]に三[さん]回[かい]も質[しつ]問[もん]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You point it, press once, and the shot is already a grid of numbers on a card — no film, no developing tray. A <reading>digi-cam</reading> that keeps every picture as bare digits is a <vocabulary form="デジカメ">digital camera</vocabulary>, and its name is <reading>デジカメ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年買ったデジカメを、電車の中に忘れてきました。
example_sentences.english: I left the digital camera I bought last year on the train.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]買[か]ったデジカメを、電[でん]車[しゃ]の中[なか]に忘[わす]れてきました。

example_sentences.japanese: このデジカメは軽いので、山に登るときに便利です。
example_sentences.english: This digital camera is light, so it's handy when you climb mountains.
example_sentences.furigana: このデジカメは軽[かる]いので、山[やま]に登[のぼ]るときに便[べん]利[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: デジカメの写真をパソコンに入れて、家族に見せました。
example_sentences.english: I put the photos from my digital camera on the computer and showed them to my family.
example_sentences.furigana: デジカメの写[しゃ]真[しん]をパソコンに入[い]れて、家[か]族[ぞく]に見[み]せました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The bundle on the counter holds nothing but <reading>new</reading> things — a fire last night, a price that jumped this morning, none of it old yet. A stack of only-just-happened facts is the <vocabulary form="ニュース">news</vocabulary>, and you ask for it as <reading>ニュース</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝のニュースによると、今日は午後から雪が降るそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to the morning news, it's going to snow this afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]のニュースによると、今日[きょう]は午[ご]後[ご]から雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]るそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 地震のニュースを見て、日本にいる友人に電話しました。
example_sentences.english: I saw the news about the earthquake and called a friend in Japan.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[じ]震[しん]のニュースを見[み]て、日本[にほん]にいる友[ゆう]人[じん]に電[でん]話[わ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: いいニュースと悪いニュース、どちらから聞きたいですか。
example_sentences.english: Good news and bad news — which do you want to hear first?
example_sentences.furigana: いいニュースと悪[わる]いニュース、どちらから聞[き]きたいですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 記（き）＋事（じ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A recorded (記) matter (事): an article.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <vocabulary form="記事">article</vocabulary> is a <kanji form="記">written account</kanji> of exactly one <kanji form="事">matter</kanji>, pinned down so hard it cannot wriggle off the page before you finish reading.

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞の記事で、近くに新しい病院ができることを知りました。
example_sentences.english: I learned from a newspaper article that a new hospital is going up nearby.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[しん]聞[ぶん]の記[き]事[じ]で、近[ちか]くに新[あたら]しい病[びょう]院[いん]ができることを知[し]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 雑誌の記事を書くために、毎日ラーメンを食べ続けました。
example_sentences.english: To write a magazine article, I ate ramen every single day.
example_sentences.furigana: 雑[ざっ]誌[し]の記[き]事[じ]を書[か]くために、毎[まい]日[にち]ラーメンを食[た]べ続[つづ]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: その記事は、名前が一つ間違っていました。
example_sentences.english: That article got one of the names wrong.
example_sentences.furigana: その記[き]事[じ]は、名[な]前[まえ]が一[ひと]つ間違[まちが]っていました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（だい）＋学（がく）＋院（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: University's (大学) inner court (院): grad school.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="大学院">graduate school</vocabulary> is the <kanji form="院">institution</kanji> you climb to only after a full degree, where the <kanji form="学">studying</kanji> is a <kanji form="大">big</kanji>ger version of everything you did downstairs.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は来年から大学院で歴史を勉強します。
example_sentences.english: My older sister starts studying history at graduate school next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は来[らい]年[ねん]から大[だい]学[がく]院[いん]で歴[れき]史[し]を勉[べん]強[きょう]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院の授業は難しいけど、とても面白い。
example_sentences.english: Grad school classes are hard, but really interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]院[いん]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]は難[むずか]しいけど、とても面[おも]白[しろ]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院に行くつもりなら、今から準備したほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: If you plan to go to grad school, you'd better start preparing now.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]院[いん]に行[い]くつもりなら、今[いま]から準[じゅん]備[び]したほうがいい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 入（にゅう）＋学（がく）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <vocabulary form="入学する">enter school</vocabulary> is simply to <kanji form="入">enter</kanji> through the gate on your first morning and join the <kanji form="学">learning</kanji> already going on inside.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は春にこの学校に入学する。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister starts at this school in spring.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は春[はる]にこの学[がっ]校[こう]に入[にゅう]学[がく]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 入学したばかりの学生は、まだ教室の場所が分からない。
example_sentences.english: Students who just started don't know where the classrooms are yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 入[にゅう]学[がく]したばかりの学[がく]生[せい]は、まだ教[きょう]室[しつ]の場[ば]所[しょ]が分[わ]からない。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に入学するために、週末も図書館で勉強した。
example_sentences.english: I studied at the library even on weekends to get into university.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]に入[にゅう]学[がく]するために、週[しゅう]末[まつ]も図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で勉[べん]強[きょう]した。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 合（ごう）＋格（かく）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Matching (合) the standard (格): to pass.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Either your score <kanji form="合">fits</kanji> the <kanji form="格">rank</kanji> the examiners drew or it falls short. The moment it fits, you have <vocabulary form="合格する">passed (an exam)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験に合格して、父がケーキを買ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: I passed the exam, and Dad bought me a cake.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]に合[ごう]格[かく]して、父[ちち]がケーキを買[か]ってくれた。

example_sentences.japanese: 合格したら、すぐ祖母に電話するね。
example_sentences.english: If I pass, I'll call Grandma right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 合[ごう]格[かく]したら、すぐ祖[そ]母[ぼ]に電[でん]話[わ]するね。

example_sentences.japanese: 合格するまで、何度でも頑張るつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I'll keep at it as many times as it takes until I pass.
example_sentences.furigana: 合[ごう]格[かく]するまで、何[なん]度[ど]でも頑[がん]張[ば]るつもりだ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋合（ごう）＋格（かく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stick a <kanji form="不">negative</kanji> mark in front, and the score that would have <kanji form="合">fit</kanji> the <kanji form="格">rank</kanji> now sits just below the line. That gap is a <vocabulary form="不合格">failing (an exam)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 不合格だったけど、次はもっと頑張る。
example_sentences.english: I failed, but next time I'll try harder.
example_sentences.furigana: 不[ふ]合[ごう]格[かく]だったけど、次[つぎ]はもっと頑[がん]張[ば]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 不合格と聞いて、弟は部屋から出てこなかった。
example_sentences.english: When he heard he'd failed, my little brother wouldn't come out of his room.
example_sentences.furigana: 不[ふ]合[ごう]格[かく]と聞[き]いて、弟[おとうと]は部屋[へや]から出[で]てこなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 不合格の理由は、名前を書き忘れたことだった。
example_sentences.english: The reason I failed was that I forgot to write my name.
example_sentences.furigana: 不[ふ]合[ごう]格[かく]の理[り]由[ゆう]は、名[な]前[まえ]を書[か]き忘[わす]れたことだった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 休（きゅう）＋暇（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A rest (休) period (暇): time off.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Line up a run of <kanji form="休">rest</kanji> days with enough <kanji form="暇">spare time</kanji> stacked behind them to do nothing at all, and the stretch you get away from work is a <vocabulary form="休暇">vacation / leave</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の休暇に、海の近くの旅館に泊まる予定です。
example_sentences.english: For the summer vacation, I'm planning to stay at an inn near the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]の休[きゅう]暇[か]に、海[うみ]の近[ちか]くの旅[りょ]館[かん]に泊[と]まる予[よ]定[てい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 会社から一週間の休暇をもらった。
example_sentences.english: I got a week of leave from work.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]から一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]の休[きゅう]暇[か]をもらった。

example_sentences.japanese: 休暇の間、猫は隣の人に頼んだ。
example_sentences.english: While I'm on vacation, I've asked the neighbor to look after the cat.
example_sentences.furigana: 休[きゅう]暇[か]の間[あいだ]、猫[ねこ]は隣[となり]の人[ひと]に頼[たの]んだ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 出（しゅっ）＋勤（きん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 出 しゅつ → しゅっ.
items.mnemonic_text: Exiting (出) to duty (勤): to commute to work.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Each morning you <kanji form="出">exit</kanji> the front door and carry your day's <kanji form="勤">diligence</kanji> to the office, and making that trip is what it means to <vocabulary form="出勤する">go to work</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪が降っても、彼女は自転車で出勤する。
example_sentences.english: Even when it snows, she cycles to work.
example_sentences.furigana: 雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]っても、彼[かの]女[じょ]は自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]で出[しゅっ]勤[きん]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は八時までに出勤してください。
example_sentences.english: Please come in to work by eight tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は八[はち]時[じ]までに出[しゅっ]勤[きん]してください。

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日なのに出勤しなければならない。
example_sentences.english: I have to go in to work even though it's Sunday.
example_sentences.furigana: 日[にち]曜[よう]日[び]なのに出[しゅっ]勤[きん]しなければならない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 退（たい）＋勤（きん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Retreating (退) from duty (勤): to clock out.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once the day's <kanji form="勤">diligence</kanji> is all spent, you <kanji form="退">withdraw</kanji> from the office and head home, and that quiet exit is what it means to <vocabulary form="退勤する">leave work</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫はいつも六時に退勤します。
example_sentences.english: My husband always leaves work at six.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]はいつも六[ろく]時[じ]に退[たい]勤[きん]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 退勤する前に、パソコンを消してください。
example_sentences.english: Please shut down your computer before you leave work.
example_sentences.furigana: 退[たい]勤[きん]する前[まえ]に、パソコンを消[け]してください。

example_sentences.japanese: 退勤してから、駅の近くでラーメンを食べた。
example_sentences.english: After leaving work, I had ramen near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 退[たい]勤[きん]してから、駅[えき]の近[ちか]くでラーメンを食[た]べた。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 残（ざん）＋業（ぎょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The office lights go off but part of the day's <kanji form="業">business</kanji> still <kanji form="残">remains</kanji> on your desk. The extra hour you stay to clear it is <vocabulary form="残業">overtime work</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週は毎晩残業で、晩ご飯がいつも遅い。
example_sentences.english: I've had overtime every night this week, so dinner is always late.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[こん]週[しゅう]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]残[ざん]業[ぎょう]で、晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]がいつも遅[おそ]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は残業しないで、早く帰りたい。
example_sentences.english: Today I want to skip overtime and go home early.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は残[ざん]業[ぎょう]しないで、早[はや]く帰[かえ]りたい。

example_sentences.japanese: 残業が多い会社は、あまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I'm not a fan of companies with lots of overtime.
example_sentences.furigana: 残[ざん]業[ぎょう]が多[おお]い会[かい]社[しゃ]は、あまり好[す]きじゃない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 社（しゃ）＋員（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A company's (社) staff member (員): an employee.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Put one more <kanji form="員">member</kanji> on a <kanji form="社">company</kanji>'s payroll, paid from its own account, and that person is now a <vocabulary form="社員">company employee</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社の社員は、金曜日はネクタイをしない。
example_sentences.english: Employees at this company skip the tie on Fridays.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]の社[しゃ]員[いん]は、金[きん]曜[よう]日[び]はネクタイをしない。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい社員に、エレベーターの場所を教えた。
example_sentences.english: I showed the new employee where the elevator is.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい社[しゃ]員[いん]に、エレベーターの場[ば]所[しょ]を教[おし]えた。

example_sentences.japanese: 社員が五人しかいない小さい会社です。
example_sentences.english: It's a small company with only five employees.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]員[いん]が五[ご]人[にん]しかいない小[ちい]さい会[かい]社[しゃ]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 部（ぶ）＋長（ちょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A department's (部) chief (長): a manager.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="長">leader</kanji> whose reach stops at the edge of one <kanji form="部">section</kanji>, with someone above them running everything else, is a <vocabulary form="部長">department head</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長は厳しいけど、優しいところもある。
example_sentences.english: The department head is strict, but has a gentle side too.
example_sentences.furigana: 部[ぶ]長[ちょう]は厳[きび]しいけど、優[やさ]しいところもある。

example_sentences.japanese: 部長に書類を出すのを忘れていた。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to hand the documents in to the department head.
example_sentences.furigana: 部[ぶ]長[ちょう]に書[しょ]類[るい]を出[だ]すのを忘[わす]れていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の間、部長は一回も話さなかった。
example_sentences.english: The department head didn't say a single word during the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]の間[あいだ]、部[ぶ]長[ちょう]は一[いっ]回[かい]も話[はな]さなかった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 社（しゃ）＋長（ちょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A company's (社) chief (長): the president.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Follow the chain of command in a <kanji form="社">company</kanji> all the way up to the one <kanji form="長">leader</kanji> with nobody above them, and that person is the <vocabulary form="社長">company president</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の車は、驚くほど古い。
example_sentences.english: The company president's car is surprisingly old.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]長[ちょう]の車[くるま]は、驚[おどろ]くほど古[ふる]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 来月、社長が工場に来るそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear the president is coming to the factory next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]、社[しゃ]長[ちょう]が工[こう]場[じょう]に来[く]るそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は三十歳で小さい会社の社長になった。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather became president of a small company at thirty.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は三[さん]十[じゅう]歳[さい]で小[ちい]さい会[かい]社[しゃ]の社[しゃ]長[ちょう]になった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 計（けい）＋画（かく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Counting (計) a drawn picture (画): a plan.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="計">plot</kanji> you have only worked out in your head turns into a <vocabulary form="計画">plan</vocabulary> the moment you lay it out in clear <kanji form="画">brush-strokes</kanji> on paper.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末の計画を、恋人と話し合った。
example_sentences.english: I talked over our weekend plans with my partner.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]の計[けい]画[かく]を、恋[こい]人[びと]と話[はな]し合[あ]った。

example_sentences.japanese: 台風で、旅行の計画を変えなければならなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because of the typhoon, we had to change our travel plans.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]で、旅[りょ]行[こう]の計[けい]画[かく]を変[か]えなければならなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父の計画は、いつも複雑すぎる。
example_sentences.english: My uncle's plans are always far too complicated.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]の計[けい]画[かく]は、いつも複[ふく]雑[ざつ]すぎる。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 説（せつ）＋明（めい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Speech (説) making things bright (明): an explanation.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take a rough <kanji form="説">theory</kanji> and make every step of it <kanji form="明">bright</kanji> enough for anyone to follow, and what you have handed them is an <vocabulary form="説明">explanation</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の説明は、とても分かりやすい。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's explanations are really easy to follow.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]の説[せつ]明[めい]は、とても分[わ]かりやすい。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員の説明を聞いて、このカメラに決めた。
example_sentences.english: After hearing the clerk's explanation, I decided on this camera.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]の説[せつ]明[めい]を聞[き]いて、このカメラに決[き]めた。

example_sentences.japanese: 説明が長すぎて、みんな寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: The explanation went on so long that everyone fell asleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 説[せつ]明[めい]が長[なが]すぎて、みんな寝[ね]てしまった。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — とりひきさき cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 取引先.
items.mnemonic_text: A dealing's (取引) destination (先): a client.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The outside firm you <kanji form="取">take</kanji> orders from and <kanji form="引">pull</kanji> deals back and forth with, always one step <kanji form="先">ahead</kanji> of you along the trade line, is your <vocabulary form="取引先">business partner/client</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto the door-to-door turtle trails the firm one step ahead along the trade line, takes its orders and hauls deals back until he <reading>tore a hockey sack</reading>: <reading>とりひきさき</reading>, his biggest <vocabulary form="取引先">client</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先に新しい値段を説明しなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: I have to explain the new prices to our client.
example_sentences.furigana: 取[とり]引[ひき]先[さき]に新[あたら]しい値[ね]段[だん]を説[せつ]明[めい]しなければなりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先の人とゴルフに行くのも仕事です。
example_sentences.english: Going golfing with clients is part of the job too.
example_sentences.furigana: 取[とり]引[ひき]先[さき]の人[ひと]とゴルフに行[い]くのも仕[し]事[ごと]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先から電話があったら、すぐ私に知らせてください。
example_sentences.english: If a client calls, let me know right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 取[とり]引[ひき]先[さき]から電[でん]話[わ]があったら、すぐ私[わたし]に知[し]らせてください。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — うりあげ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 売上.
items.mnemonic_text: What's sold (売) and raised (上げ): sales figures.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Each time you <kanji form="売">sell</kanji> something the price adds <kanji form="上">up</kanji> onto the day's running total, and that whole pile of takings is the <vocabulary form="売上">sales (revenue)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Uri's fruit stall makes all its money through one till, so she reads that machine like <reading>a gauge</reading> of the whole month. The total it rings up is the stall's <vocabulary form="売上">sales (revenue)</vocabulary>, the figure she means when she says 「<reading>うりあげ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏はアイスクリームの売上が一番多いです。
example_sentences.english: Ice cream sales are highest in summer.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]はアイスクリームの売[うり]上[あげ]が一[いち]番[ばん]多[おお]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今月の売上は先月の半分しかありません。
example_sentences.english: This month's sales are only half of last month's.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[こん]月[げつ]の売[うり]上[あげ]は先[せん]月[げつ]の半[はん]分[ぶん]しかありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいメニューを始めてから、売上が増えました。
example_sentences.english: Sales have gone up since we started the new menu.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しいメニューを始[はじ]めてから、売[うり]上[あげ]が増[ふ]えました。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — とりひき cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 取引.
items.mnemonic_text: Taking (取) and pulling (引): a deal.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every time a shopkeeper lets you <kanji form="引">pull</kanji> goods across the counter and <kanji form="取">take</kanji> them while your cash slides the other way, that swap is a <vocabulary form="取引">transaction</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto the turtle pulls goods across the counter and slides his cash the other way like a puck in <reading>Tori hockey</reading>, calling <reading>とりひき</reading> as the <vocabulary form="取引">transaction</vocabulary> closes.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社とは、もう十年も取引をしています。
example_sentences.english: We've been doing business with that company for ten years now.
example_sentences.furigana: あの会[かい]社[しゃ]とは、もう十[じゅう]年[ねん]も取[とり]引[ひき]をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 現金だけの取引は、ちょっと怖いな。
example_sentences.english: Deals in cash only scare me a little.
example_sentences.furigana: 現[げん]金[きん]だけの取[とり]引[ひき]は、ちょっと怖[こわ]いな。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の企業との取引が決まって、社員はみんな喜んだ。
example_sentences.english: When the deal with a foreign firm was settled, the whole staff was delighted.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の企[き]業[ぎょう]との取[とり]引[ひき]が決[き]まって、社[しゃ]員[いん]はみんな喜[よろこ]んだ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 書（しょ）＋類（るい）＋提（てい）＋出（しゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Submitting (提出) papers (書類): filing documents.
items.furigana: 書[しょ]類[るい]提[てい]出[しゅつ]
items.meaning_mnemonic: Gather the <kanji form="書">write</kanji>ten sheets of every <kanji form="類">kind</kanji> into one folder. <kanji form="提">Carry</kanji> that folder in hand and <kanji form="出">exit</kanji> to drop it at the front desk, and you have done the <vocabulary form="書類提出">document submission</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類提出は来週の金曜日までです。
example_sentences.english: The documents are due next Friday.
example_sentences.furigana: 書[しょ]類[るい]提[てい]出[しゅつ]は来[らい]週[しゅう]の金[きん]曜[よう]日[び]までです。

example_sentences.japanese: 書類提出の前に、部長に一度見てもらいましょう。
example_sentences.english: Before we hand in the documents, let's have the department head look them over.
example_sentences.furigana: 書[しょ]類[るい]提[てい]出[しゅつ]の前[まえ]に、部[ぶ]長[ちょう]に一[いち]度[ど]見[み]てもらいましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 書類提出の窓口は二階にあります。
example_sentences.english: The counter for submitting documents is on the second floor.
example_sentences.furigana: 書[しょ]類[るい]提[てい]出[しゅつ]の窓[まど]口[ぐち]は二[に]階[かい]にあります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 会（かい）＋合（ごう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Meeting (会) and matching (合): a gathering.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When enough people <kanji form="会">meet</kanji> in one room that the chairs and the heads finally <kanji form="合">fit</kanji> the same count, that filled room is a <vocabulary form="会合">gathering</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 町の会合で、公園の掃除について話し合いました。
example_sentences.english: At the neighborhood meeting, we talked about cleaning the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 町[まち]の会[かい]合[ごう]で、公[こう]園[えん]の掃[そう]除[じ]について話[はな]し合[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 会合は七時に始まるから、急ぎましょう。
example_sentences.english: The meeting starts at seven, so let's hurry.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]合[ごう]は七[しち]時[じ]に始[はじ]まるから、急[いそ]ぎましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 月に一回、大学の仲間との会合があります。
example_sentences.english: Once a month I have a get-together with my university friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 月[つき]に一[いっ]回[かい]、大[だい]学[がく]の仲[なか]間[ま]との会[かい]合[ごう]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 出（しゅっ）＋席（せき）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 出 しゅつ → しゅっ.
items.mnemonic_text: Exiting (出) to a seat (席): to attend.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When you <kanji form="出">leave</kanji> home and go fill your own <kanji form="席">seat</kanji> in the lecture hall, you <vocabulary form="出席する">attend</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議には、外国のお客さんも出席します。
example_sentences.english: Some clients from overseas will also attend tomorrow's meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の会[かい]議[ぎ]には、外[がい]国[こく]のお客[きゃく]さんも出[しゅっ]席[せき]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があったけど、授業には出席した。
example_sentences.english: I had a fever, but I still went to class.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねつ]があったけど、授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]には出[しゅっ]席[せき]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 出席する人の名前を、ここに書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write the names of everyone attending here.
example_sentences.furigana: 出[しゅっ]席[せき]する人[ひと]の名[な]前[まえ]を、ここに書[か]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 提（てい）＋供（きょう）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Presenting (提) and offering (供): to provide.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="提">carry</kanji> a tray of samples to a customer in your hands and <kanji form="供">offer</kanji> each one across to them; passing goods to someone like that is to <vocabulary form="提供する">provide</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルは、和食の朝ご飯を提供しています。
example_sentences.english: This hotel serves a Japanese-style breakfast.
example_sentences.furigana: このホテルは、和[わ]食[しょく]の朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を提[てい]供[きょう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 地震のとき、市が水と食べ物を提供します。
example_sentences.english: When there's an earthquake, the city provides water and food.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[じ]震[しん]のとき、市[し]が水[みず]と食[た]べ物[もの]を提[てい]供[きょう]します。

example_sentences.japanese: この喫茶店は、一人で仕事をする人に静かな席を提供している。
example_sentences.english: This café offers quiet seats to people working on their own.
example_sentences.furigana: この喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]は、一人[ひとり]で仕[し]事[ごと]をする人[ひと]に静[しず]かな席[せき]を提[てい]供[きょう]している。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 参（さん）＋加（か）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Joining (参) and adding (加): to take part.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Just <kanji form="参">coming</kanji> along to the event is only half of it; once your name is <kanji form="加">add</kanji>ed to the sign-in sheet, you <vocabulary form="参加する">participate</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、ダンスの練習に参加しませんか。
example_sentences.english: Would you like to join the dance practice this weekend?
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、ダンスの練[れん]習[しゅう]に参[さん]加[か]しませんか。

example_sentences.japanese: その料理の教室には、男の人も参加しています。
example_sentences.english: Men take part in that cooking class too.
example_sentences.furigana: その料[りょう]理[り]の教[きょう]室[しつ]には、男[おとこ]の人[ひと]も参[さん]加[か]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 去年は忙しかったので、会社の旅行に参加しなかった。
example_sentences.english: Last year I was busy, so I sat out the company trip.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]は忙[いそが]しかったので、会[かい]社[しゃ]の旅[りょ]行[こう]に参[さん]加[か]しなかった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 最（さい）＋近（きん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The very (最) nearest (近) time: recently.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Out of all past time, the stretch sitting <kanji form="近">near</kanji>est to right now is the <kanji form="最">most</kanji> current one. Whatever happened inside it happened <vocabulary form="最近">recently</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、野菜の値段がかなり上がった。
example_sentences.english: Vegetable prices have gone up quite a bit lately.
example_sentences.furigana: 最[さい]近[きん]、野[や]菜[さい]の値[ね]段[だん]がかなり上[あ]がった。

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、元気がないね。何かあった？
example_sentences.english: You've seemed down lately. Did something happen?
example_sentences.furigana: 最[さい]近[きん]、元[げん]気[き]がないね。何[なに]かあった？

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の子供は、外であまり遊ばないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently kids these days don't play outside much.
example_sentences.furigana: 最[さい]近[きん]の子[こ]供[ども]は、外[そと]であまり遊[あそ]ばないらしい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 将（しょう）＋来（らい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: About to (将) come (来): the future.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A parade <kanji form="将">commander</kanji> keeps shouting which unit will <kanji form="来">come</kanji> up the road next. Every unit that has not yet marched past you is still <vocabulary form="将来">the future</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は将来、医者になりたいと言っている。
example_sentences.english: My daughter says she wants to be a doctor when she grows up.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は将[しょう]来[らい]、医[い]者[しゃ]になりたいと言[い]っている。

example_sentences.japanese: 将来のことを考えると、少し不安になる。
example_sentences.english: Thinking about the future makes me a little anxious.
example_sentences.furigana: 将[しょう]来[らい]のことを考[かんが]えると、少[すこ]し不[ふ]安[あん]になる。

example_sentences.japanese: 将来は、海が見える家に住みたいです。
example_sentences.english: Someday I want to live in a house with a view of the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 将[しょう]来[らい]は、海[うみ]が見[み]える家[いえ]に住[す]みたいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 当（とう）＋時（じ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: That very (当) time (時): back then.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Point back at a past event and name the exact <kanji form="時">hour</kanji> it happened. The moment your finger <kanji form="当">hit</kanji>s is what people call <vocabulary form="当時">at that time</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 当時、祖父は駅員として働いていた。
example_sentences.english: Back then, my grandfather worked as a station attendant.
example_sentences.furigana: 当[とう]時[じ]、祖[そ]父[ふ]は駅[えき]員[いん]として働[はたら]いていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 当時はまだ携帯がなかったので、よく手紙を書いた。

example_sentences.japanese: 電話の相手は誰でしたか。
example_sentences.english: Who was that on the phone?
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]の相[あい]手[て]は誰[だれ]でしたか。

example_sentences.japanese: 相手の名前をすぐ忘れるので、ノートに書きます。
example_sentences.english: I forget people's names right away, so I write them in a notebook.
example_sentences.furigana: 相[あい]手[て]の名[な]前[まえ]をすぐ忘[わす]れるので、ノートに書[か]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 次の相手は強そうですね。
example_sentences.english: Our next opponent looks strong, doesn't he?
example_sentences.furigana: 次[つぎ]の相[あい]手[て]は強[つよ]そうですね。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 浅（あさ）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You wade into the lake ready to swim, and fifty steps out the water still only reaches your knees. Water that never gets deep enough to swim in is <vocabulary form="浅い">shallow</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Fifty steps out into the lake the water still only reaches your knees, so you let out <reading>a sigh</reading>, <reading>あさい</reading>, because nobody can swim in water this <vocabulary form="浅い">shallow</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この川は浅いので、歩いて渡れます。
example_sentences.english: This river is shallow, so you can walk across it.
example_sentences.furigana: この川[かわ]は浅[あさ]いので、歩[ある]いて渡[わた]れます。

example_sentences.japanese: 浅い皿に魚を並べました。
example_sentences.english: I laid the fish out on a shallow plate.
example_sentences.furigana: 浅[あさ]い皿[さら]に魚[さかな]を並[なら]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は海の浅い所で遊んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My son is playing in the shallow part of the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は海[うみ]の浅[あさ]い所[ところ]で遊[あそ]んでいます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 立（りっ）＋派（ぱ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 立 りつ → りっ. Handakuon: 派 は → ぱ.
items.mnemonic_text: Standing (立) in a fine faction (派): splendid.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="派">faction</kanji> that can <kanji form="立">stand</kanji> tall on its own, propped up by nothing, is an impressive thing, and impressive is exactly <vocabulary form="立派">splendid / fine</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な slots in ahead of the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父の家には立派な庭があります。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather's house has a magnificent garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]の家[いえ]には立[りっ]派[ぱ]な庭[にわ]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で荷物を全部運んで、立派だったね。
example_sentences.english: You carried all the luggage by yourself. Well done.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で荷[に]物[もつ]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]運[はこ]んで、立[りっ]派[ぱ]だったね。

example_sentences.japanese: この魚は大きくて立派ですね。
example_sentences.english: What a big, fine fish this is.
example_sentences.furigana: この魚[さかな]は大[おお]きくて立[りっ]派[ぱ]ですね。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 恋（こい）＋人（びと）. Rendaku: 人 ひと → びと.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (人) of love (恋): a lover.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single <kanji>person</kanji> your heart keeps circling back to, the one you actually picked, is your <vocabulary>lover / partner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人に手紙を書いたのに、まだ送っていません。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a letter to my partner, but I still haven't sent it.
example_sentences.furigana: 恋[こい]人[びと]に手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]いたのに、まだ送[おく]っていません。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉の恋人は料理がとても上手です。
example_sentences.english: My older sister's partner is a really good cook.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]の恋[こい]人[びと]は料[りょう]理[り]がとても上手[じょうず]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人と湖の近くを散歩したいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to take a walk by the lake with my partner.
example_sentences.furigana: 恋[こい]人[びと]と湖[みずうみ]の近[ちか]くを散[さん]歩[ぽ]したいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 恥（は）＋ずかしい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That single kanji carries the plain sense of <kanji>shame</kanji>, and adding the い ending turns it into the adjective <vocabulary>embarrassing</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A customer burns with shame at the till: the man <reading>has a cashier</reading> staring at him, and his whisper of 「<reading>はずかしい</reading>」 trails off into a long ee, because this is so <vocabulary form="恥ずかしい">embarrassing</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 質問に答えられなくて恥ずかしかったです。
example_sentences.english: I was embarrassed that I couldn't answer the question.
example_sentences.furigana: 質[しつ]問[もん]に答[こた]えられなくて恥[は]ずかしかったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 恥ずかしいから、あまり話しません。
example_sentences.english: It's embarrassing, so I don't talk much.
example_sentences.furigana: 恥[は]ずかしいから、あまり話[はな]しません。

example_sentences.japanese: 写真を見せるのは恥ずかしいです。
example_sentences.english: Showing photos is embarrassing.
example_sentences.furigana: 写[しゃ]真[しん]を見[み]せるのは恥[は]ずかしいです。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — めんどくさい cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 面倒くさい.
items.mnemonic_text: A face (面) that's too much bother: annoying.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You put on a stiff <kanji form="面">mask</kanji> just to answer the door, and the whole prop shelf <kanji form="倒">collapses</kanji> on you as you reach for it. A small job that turns into that much bother is <vocabulary form="面倒くさい">troublesome</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Mendo pulls on a stiff mask to answer the door, the whole prop shelf collapses on him, and <reading>Mendo cusses</reading> 「<reading>めんどくさい</reading>」 from under the pile, a job grown <vocabulary form="面倒くさい">troublesome</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎晩皿を洗うのが面倒くさい。
example_sentences.english: Washing the dishes every night is such a pain.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]晩[ばん]皿[さら]を洗[あら]うのが面[めん]倒[どう]くさい。

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒くさいから、今日は駅までタクシーで行きます。
example_sentences.english: I can't be bothered, so I'm taking a taxi to the station today.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[めん]倒[どう]くさいから、今日[きょう]は駅[えき]までタクシーで行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒くさい書類は、明日書きます。
example_sentences.english: I'll fill out the annoying paperwork tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[めん]倒[どう]くさい書[しょ]類[るい]は、明日[あした]書[か]きます。

items.word_type: な adjective, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 偶（ぐう）＋然（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A paired (偶) natural (然) event: a coincidence.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two things line up by pure <kanji>accident</kanji>, with nothing behind it but being <kanji>that sort of thing</kanji>, and you call it a <vocabulary>coincidence</vocabulary>. It takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で偶然先生に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I happened to run into my teacher at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で偶[ぐう]然[ぜん]先[せん]生[せい]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: それは偶然です。
example_sentences.english: That's a coincidence.
example_sentences.furigana: それは偶[ぐう]然[ぜん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 偶然、財布を見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I happened to find a wallet.
example_sentences.furigana: 偶[ぐう]然[ぜん]、財[さい]布[ふ]を見[み]つけました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 寂（さび）＋しい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The kanji here already means <kanji>loneliness</kanji> all by itself, and the い on the end makes it the adjective <vocabulary>lonely</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: All her loneliness comes out in one <reading>sob, she</reading> sound with a thin trailing ee, 「<reading>さびしい</reading>」, and that small cry is how feeling <vocabulary form="寂しい">lonely</vocabulary> sounds.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: I feel lonely being by myself.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で寂[さび]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい学校で友達がいなくて寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm lonely at my new school without any friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい学[がっ]校[こう]で友[とも]達[だち]がいなくて寂[さび]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母に会えなくて寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm lonely because I can't see my grandmother.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]に会[あ]えなくて寂[さび]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 深（ふか）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You drop a stone into the well and count five full seconds before you hear it hit water. A gap that long between the top and the bottom is what <vocabulary form="深い">deep</vocabulary> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your stone takes five full seconds to splash down the well, and you mutter that <reading>few can</reading> climb out of a hole that <vocabulary form="深い">deep</vocabulary>. The word for it is <reading>ふかい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: この湖は深いので、子供は入ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: This lake is deep, so children must not go in.
example_sentences.furigana: この湖[みずうみ]は深[ふか]いので、子[こ]供[ども]は入[はい]ってはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 山の中に深い川がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a deep river up in the mountains.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の中[なか]に深[ふか]い川[かわ]がありました。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は深い箱に古い写真を入れた。
example_sentences.english: My father put the old photos in a deep box.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は深[ふか]い箱[はこ]に古[ふる]い写[しゃ]真[しん]を入[い]れた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 細（ほそ）＋い.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="細">thin</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="細い">thin / slender</vocabulary> word are the same character and carry the same sense. The い on the end is what lets it stand in front of a noun like any adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: The farmer lays a <reading>hose</reading> along the mud path between the rice fields, and it only fits because each path is no wider than a thread. Anything that narrow is <reading>ほそい</reading>, <vocabulary form="細い">thin</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の後ろに細い道があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a narrow lane behind the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の後[うし]ろに細[ほそ]い道[みち]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母の髪は細くて長いです。
example_sentences.english: My aunt's hair is fine and long.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]の髪[かみ]は細[ほそ]くて長[なが]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 細いペンで名前を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write your name with a thin pen.
example_sentences.furigana: 細[ほそ]いペンで名[な]前[まえ]を書[か]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 痒（かゆ）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A sickness (疒) that wants (羊) scratching: itchy.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One mosquito gets into the tent at the riverbank and finds the strip of skin behind your knee. By dawn that spot is so <vocabulary form="痒い">itchy</vocabulary> you have scratched it raw in your sleep.
items.reading_mnemonic: In the tent by the river you wake with that bite behind your knee burning, and you beg your friend <reading>can you</reading> scratch it. You groan <reading>かゆい</reading>, it is so <vocabulary form="痒い">itchy</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で遊んだら、足が痒くなった。
example_sentences.english: After I played in the park, my legs got itchy.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]んだら、足[あし]が痒[かゆ]くなった。

example_sentences.japanese: このコートは首が痒いので、もう着ません。
example_sentences.english: This coat makes my neck itch, so I don't wear it anymore.
example_sentences.furigana: このコートは首[くび]が痒[かゆ]いので、もう着[き]ません。

example_sentences.japanese: 目が痒いときは、この薬を使ってください。
example_sentences.english: When your eyes are itchy, please use this medicine.
example_sentences.furigana: 目[め]が痒[かゆ]いときは、この薬[くすり]を使[つか]ってください。

items.word_type: な adjective, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 得（とく）＋意（い）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji form="得">Getting</kanji> the exact result your <kanji form="意">heart</kanji> aimed at, time after time, is what being <vocabulary form="得意">good at</vocabulary> something feels like. It is a な adjective, so it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫は高い所に登るのが得意だ。
example_sentences.english: Cats are good at climbing up to high places.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]は高[たか]い所[ところ]に登[のぼ]るのが得[とく]意[い]だ。

example_sentences.japanese: 数学が得意な兄に宿題を教えてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: My older brother, who is good at math, helped me with my homework.
example_sentences.furigana: 数[すう]学[がく]が得[とく]意[い]な兄[あに]に宿[しゅく]題[だい]を教[おし]えてもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は絵が得意なので、店の看板を作りました。
example_sentences.english: She is good at drawing, so she made the sign for the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は絵[え]が得[とく]意[い]なので、店[みせ]の看[かん]板[ばん]を作[つく]りました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 貿（ぼう）＋易（えき）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Goods traded (貿) for a change (易): commerce.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once two countries make it <kanji>easy</kanji> to swap whatever each of them has stacked up in surplus, that steady back-and-forth swapping is <vocabulary>trade (commerce)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は外国と貿易をしています。
example_sentences.english: Japan trades with foreign countries.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]は外[がい]国[こく]と貿[ぼう]易[えき]をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 貿易の仕事はおもしろいです。
example_sentences.english: Trade work is interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 貿[ぼう]易[えき]の仕[し]事[ごと]はおもしろいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は貿易の会社で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My father works at a trading company.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は貿[ぼう]易[えき]の会[かい]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]いています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 税（ぜい）＋金（きん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Money (金) taken as tax (税): a tax.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The slice of everyone's <kanji>money</kanji> that the government quietly rakes off every year to pay for roads, schools and soldiers is <vocabulary>tax</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を払うのは私たちの義務です。
example_sentences.english: Paying taxes is our duty.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]を払[はら]うのは私[わたし]たちの義[ぎ]務[む]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を忘れると大変です。
example_sentences.english: If you forget about taxes, it becomes a big problem.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]を忘[わす]れると大[たい]変[へん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 税金が高すぎて困っています。
example_sentences.english: The taxes are too high, and it's a problem for me.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]が高[たか]すぎて困[こま]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 偉（えら）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) of great deeds: admirable.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At ninety, Grandma Kane still climbs the shrine's mossy steps twice a day to sweep each one clean. The whole town agrees that is <vocabulary form="偉い">great / admirable</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane is up <reading>early</reading> at ninety, sweeping every mossy shrine step before sunrise, and the whole town nods <reading>えらい</reading>, calling her <vocabulary form="偉い">admirable</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日宿題をして、偉いね。
example_sentences.english: You do your homework every day. Good for you.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]宿[しゅく]題[だい]をして、偉[えら]いね。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は会社で一番偉い人です。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is the most senior person at his company.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は会[かい]社[しゃ]で一[いち]番[ばん]偉[えら]い人[ひと]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が偉いと思っている人は、あまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I don't much like people who think they're important.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]が偉[えら]いと思[おも]っている人[ひと]は、あまり好[す]きじゃない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 農（のう）＋家（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Farming's (農) household (家): a farmer's home.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>house</kanji> standing alone out in the crop fields, pig still under its roof, worked from dawn to dusk by whoever lives there, is a <vocabulary>farmhouse / farmer</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は農家で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather works on a farm.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は農[のう]家[か]で働[はたら]いています。

example_sentences.japanese: あの農家は野菜をたくさん売っています。
example_sentences.english: That farmhouse sells a lot of vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: あの農[のう]家[か]は野[や]菜[さい]をたくさん売[う]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 農家の子供たちは毎朝早く起きます。
example_sentences.english: The farmer's children wake up early every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 農[のう]家[か]の子[こ]供[ども]たちは毎[まい]朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 羨（うらや）＋ましい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your friend shows you her new apartment with the huge balcony and the view of the park, and yours looks at a wall. That hot, sour wish to have her place instead of yours is being <vocabulary form="羨ましい">envious</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: From your friend's huge new balcony you spot her red sports car by the park and groan 「<reading>うらやましい</reading>」, as in <reading>you're a Maserati</reading> owner too. Your window faces a wall, so you are <vocabulary form="羨ましい">envious</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は毎年外国へ旅行できるので、羨ましいです。
example_sentences.english: My older sister gets to travel abroad every year, so I envy her.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は毎[まい]年[ねん]外[がい]国[こく]へ旅[りょ]行[こう]できるので、羨[うらや]ましいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 君の新しい自転車、本当に羨ましいよ。
example_sentences.english: I really envy you that new bike.
example_sentences.furigana: 君[きみ]の新[あたら]しい自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]、本[ほん]当[とう]に羨[うらや]ましいよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手な隣の人が羨ましかった。
example_sentences.english: I was jealous of the person next to me, whose Japanese was so good.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]が上手[じょうず]な隣[となり]の人[ひと]が羨[うらや]ましかった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 漁（ぎょ）＋業（ぎょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Scale that odd little tree-stump <kanji>business</kanji> up until a whole coast of boats is hauling nets of fish to market, and you have the <vocabulary>fishing industry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は漁業で有名です。
example_sentences.english: This town is famous for its fishing industry.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]は漁[ぎょ]業[ぎょう]で有[ゆう]名[めい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の家族は漁業をしています。
example_sentences.english: His family works in the fishing industry.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の家[か]族[ぞく]は漁[ぎょ]業[ぎょう]をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 漁業の仕事はとても大変です。
example_sentences.english: Fishing industry work is very hard.
example_sentences.furigana: 漁[ぎょ]業[ぎょう]の仕[し]事[ごと]はとても大[たい]変[へん]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 適（てき）＋当（とう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Fitting (適) the situation (当): suitable, or careless.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="適">suitable</kanji> pick is the one that <kanji form="当">hit</kanji>s the target dead center, and a pick that lands there is <vocabulary form="適当">appropriate</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な sits before the noun it describes.
items.description: In careful use 適当 means fitting or suitable. In casual speech it often means the opposite: something done at random, with little thought.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議に適当な部屋を探しています。
example_sentences.english: We're looking for a suitable room for the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]に適[てき]当[とう]な部屋[へや]を探[さが]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は料理のとき、塩を適当に入れる。
example_sentences.english: When my older brother cooks, he just throws in salt without measuring.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は料[りょう]理[り]のとき、塩[しお]を適[てき]当[とう]に入[い]れる。

example_sentences.japanese: 質問に適当に答えないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't answer the questions carelessly.
example_sentences.furigana: 質[しつ]問[もん]に適[てき]当[とう]に答[こた]えないでください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 無（む）＋駄（だ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A mule hauls a <kanji form="駄">burdensome</kanji> load all day and brings back <kanji form="無">nothing</kanji> for it, so every step of that trip was <vocabulary form="無駄">wasteful / useless</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な belongs before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は食べ物を無駄にするのが嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother hates wasting food.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は食[た]べ物[もの]を無[む]駄[だ]にするのが嫌[きら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 使わない物を買うのは、お金の無駄です。
example_sentences.english: Buying things you won't use is a waste of money.
example_sentences.furigana: 使[つか]わない物[もの]を買[か]うのは、お金[かね]の無[む]駄[だ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 無駄な話が多くて、授業が終わらない。
example_sentences.english: There's so much pointless chatter that class never ends.
example_sentences.furigana: 無[む]駄[だ]な話[はなし]が多[おお]くて、授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]が終[お]わらない。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 緩（ゆる）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: Thread with slack in it: loose.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The elastic in Sei's gym shorts has lost all its stretch. One jog down the field and the waistband slides past his hips, flapping <vocabulary form="緩い">loose / lax</vocabulary> with every step.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei's gym shorts are hand-me-downs from <reading>Yuri</reading>, and one jog down the field sends the worn waistband sliding past his hips. Yuri just shrugs <reading>ゆるい</reading>, they were always <vocabulary form="緩い">loose</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子が緩くて、風で飛びました。
example_sentences.english: My hat was loose, and the wind blew it off.
example_sentences.furigana: 帽[ぼう]子[し]が緩[ゆる]くて、風[かぜ]で飛[と]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 眼鏡が緩いので、店で直してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: My glasses were loose, so I had them fixed at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 眼鏡[めがね]が緩[ゆる]いので、店[みせ]で直[なお]してもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: この学校は緩いので、生徒は好きな服を着られます。
example_sentences.english: This school is relaxed, so pupils can wear whatever clothes they like.
example_sentences.furigana: この学[がっ]校[こう]は緩[ゆる]いので、生[せい]徒[と]は好[す]きな服[ふく]を着[き]られます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 厳（きび）＋しい.
items.mnemonic_text: A stern cliff of rules: strict.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your piano teacher stops you at the first wrong note, every time, and will not let you move on until the bar is perfect. Being held to a standard that hard, with nothing let slide, is <vocabulary form="厳しい">strict</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your piano teacher, a bee named <reading>Kibi</reading>, buzzes <reading>きびしい</reading> and stops you at the first wrong note, never letting a single bar slide, because she is that <vocabulary form="厳しい">strict</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの数学の先生は宿題にとても厳しい。
example_sentences.english: That math teacher is really strict about homework.
example_sentences.furigana: あの数[すう]学[がく]の先[せん]生[せい]は宿[しゅく]題[だい]にとても厳[きび]しい。

example_sentences.japanese: この会社は時間に厳しいので、遅れないでください。
example_sentences.english: This company is strict about time, so please don't be late.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]は時[じ]間[かん]に厳[きび]しいので、遅[おく]れないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は食事のとき厳しかったです。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother was strict at mealtimes.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は食[しょく]事[じ]のとき厳[きび]しかったです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 優（やさ）＋しい.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A person who meets everyone with <kanji form="優">tenderness</kanji>, quick to go easy on you and slow to judge, is what Japanese calls <vocabulary form="優しい">kind / gentle</vocabulary>. The final い is the ending that makes it an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: You mumble a wrong order and brace for a scolding, but the person who goes easy on everyone only smiles <reading>yeah, sushi</reading>, no judging. That soft <reading>やさしい</reading> reply is <vocabulary form="優しい">kind</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の奥さんはいつも猫に優しいです。
example_sentences.english: The lady next door is always gentle with cats.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の奥[おく]さんはいつも猫[ねこ]に優[やさ]しいです。

example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]さんが優[やさ]しく道[みち]を教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は優しい声で赤ちゃんに歌を歌った。

example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は優[やさ]しい声[こえ]で赤[あか]ちゃんに歌[うた]を歌[うた]った。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 早（さっ）＋速（そく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Fast (早) and speedy (速): right away.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set <kanji form="早">early</kanji> next to <kanji form="速">quick</kanji> and you get fast piled on fast, the sun barely over the hills and you are already moving. Doing a thing that far ahead of the clock is doing it <vocabulary form="早速">immediately / promptly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいゲームを買って、早速友達と遊びました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new game and played it with friends right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しいゲームを買[か]って、早[さっ]速[そく]友[とも]達[だち]と遊[あそ]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙が届いて、早速お母さんに電話しました。
example_sentences.english: The letter arrived, and I called my mother right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[て]紙[がみ]が届[とど]いて、早[さっ]速[そく]お母[かあ]さんに電[でん]話[わ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: では、早速始めましょう。
example_sentences.english: Well then, let's get started right away.
example_sentences.furigana: では、早[さっ]速[そく]始[はじ]めましょう。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 特（とく）＋に.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pick one thing out of the herd and treat it as <kanji form="特">special</kanji>, the way the temple keeps a single cow that is never for eating. Marking that one out from all the rest is <vocabulary form="特に">especially</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本料理の中で、特に寿司が好きです。
example_sentences.english: Of all Japanese food, I especially like sushi.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]料[りょう]理[り]の中[なか]で、特[とく]に寿[す]司[し]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は特に寒いですね。
example_sentences.english: It's especially cold today, isn't it?
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は特[とく]に寒[さむ]いですね。

example_sentences.japanese: この道は、夜は特に危ないです。
example_sentences.english: This road is especially dangerous at night.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は、夜[よる]は特[とく]に危[あぶ]ないです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull the bun from the steamer basket and it is <reading>hot on dough</reading> right around the outside, but the middle is still raw. Cooked that near to done is <reading>ほとんど</reading>, <vocabulary form="ほとんど">almost / mostly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]にお金[かね]がほとんど残[のこ]っていません。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Going out of your way: wazawaza.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sei steps off the fairground <reading>waltzer, waltzer</reading> and walks straight back to the end of the queue for another turn. Riding the very same thing twice on purpose is <reading>わざわざ</reading>, <vocabulary form="わざわざ">specially / deliberately</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 近[ちか]くにコンビニがあるのに、わざわざ遠[とお]いスーパーへ行[い]きました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The offering bowl at Grandma Kane's shrine is tipped over again, and <reading>yeah, Harry</reading> the fat tom cat is sitting right beside it. It went the way everyone knew it would, and that is <reading>やはり</reading>, <vocabulary form="やはり">as expected / after all</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 色[いろ]々[いろ]考[かんが]えましたが、やはり行[い]かないことにしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 安い時計は、やはりすぐ壊れますね。

example_sentences.furigana: 安[やす]い時計[とけい]は、やはりすぐ壊[こわ]れますね。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The dog tied outside Koichi's konbini barks the second the door chime sounds, a flat <reading>yap already</reading>, right on cue like every other day. Calling that no-surprise-there in a casual voice is <reading>やっぱり</reading>, <vocabulary form="やっぱり">as expected (casual)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Right or wrong, just do it: zehi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hesitate on the step, and the innkeeper throws the door wide with a bright <reading>Zee, hi</reading> and waves you straight in. That whole-hearted come-right-in is <reading>ぜひ</reading>, <vocabulary form="ぜひ">by all means</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: ぜひ一[いち]度[ど]、富[ふ]士[じ]山[やま]に登[のぼ]りたいです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Rain has turned the riverbank path to <reading>mushy</reading> mud. The guide says that <reading>もし</reading> your boots sink in you should turn back, the word that sets up a plain <vocabulary form="もし">if (hypothetical)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Packed down to the point: tsumari.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the end of class the teacher wipes the board and writes one short line under everything that was there. Boiling the whole hour down to that single <reading>summary</reading> is <reading>つまり</reading>, <vocabulary form="つまり">in other words</vocabulary>.
