example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は日[にち]曜[よう]日[び]、つまり仕[し]事[ごと]はありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は母の妹、つまり私の叔母です。
example_sentences.english: She's my mother's younger sister — in other words, my aunt.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は母[はは]の妹[いもうと]、つまり私[わたし]の叔母[おば]です。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Adding yet another layer: sara ni.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On your first morning the manager lists the small perks, then adds one more item on top, the <reading>salary</reading>. Stacking that extra point onto what was already said is <reading>さらに</reading>, <vocabulary form="さらに">furthermore</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱が下がらない。さらに咳も出てきた。

example_sentences.english: My older brother is a good cook. What's more, he's good at cleaning too.

example_sentences.japanese: 野菜の値段がさらに上がりました。

example_sentences.furigana: 野[や]菜[さい]の値[ね]段[だん]がさらに上[あ]がりました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — その＋上（うえ）.
items.mnemonic_text: On top (上) of that (その): moreover.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Put the new point <kanji form="上">above</kanji> the one you just made, one slab laid on top of another. That stacking of a second thing over the first is <vocabulary form="その上">moreover</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On its own 上 is read 「うえ」, the sound you already know, so <vocabulary form="その上">moreover</vocabulary> simply ends that way and is <reading>そのうえ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は広くて明るい。その上、駅から近い。

example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]は広[ひろ]くて明[あか]るい。その上[うえ]、駅[えき]から近[ちか]い。

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が遅れた。その上、席がなかった。
example_sentences.english: The train was late. And on top of that, there were no seats.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]車[しゃ]が遅[おく]れた。その上[うえ]、席[せき]がなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は優しくて、その上とても面白い人だ。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather is kind, and on top of that he's a really funny person.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は優[やさ]しくて、その上[うえ]とても面[おも]白[しろ]い人[ひと]だ。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Shifting the place of topic: tokorode.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Mid-conversation on the highway, the driver <reading>took a road</reading> off to the right with no warning and opened a whole new subject. Swerving the talk onto another route is <reading>ところで</reading>, <vocabulary form="ところで">by the way</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: ところで、明日[あした]の会[かい]議[ぎ]は何[なん]時[じ]からですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しかったね。ところで、来週は暇？

example_sentences.furigana: 楽[たの]しかったね。ところで、来[らい]週[しゅう]は暇[ひま]？

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、あの映画はもう見ましたか。

example_sentences.furigana: ところで、あの映[えい]画[が]はもう見[み]ましたか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The locksmith lifts one blank off the ring, holds it to the light, and says it is <reading>key to</reading> this lock with no doubt at all. That flat certainty before he has even tried it is <reading>きっと</reading>, <vocabulary form="きっと">surely / certainly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日練習したから、きっと合格するよ。
example_sentences.english: You practiced every day, so you'll definitely pass.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]練[れん]習[しゅう]したから、きっと合[ごう]格[かく]するよ。

example_sentences.furigana: 雲[くも]が多[おお]い。午[ご]後[ご]はきっと雨[あめ]だ。

example_sentences.japanese: なるほど、だから猫が冷蔵庫の上にいるんですね。
example_sentences.english: I see, so that's why the cat is on top of the fridge.
example_sentences.furigana: なるほど、だから猫[ねこ]が冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の上[うえ]にいるんですね。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — お＋世（せ）＋話（わ）＋になる, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving generational (世) care: osewa ni naru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The people of your <kanji form="世">world</kanji> will not stop <kanji form="話">talking</kanji> about whether you have eaten and slept enough. When a whole family keeps you fed and rested like that, you have come <vocabulary form="お世話になる">to be in someone's care</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月からお世話になる旅館の人に手紙を書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a letter to the people at the inn who will be looking after me from next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]からお世[せ]話[わ]になる旅[りょ]館[かん]の人[ひと]に手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 入院する前に、お世話になる医者に会いました。
example_sentences.english: Before going into the hospital, I met the doctor who would be taking care of me.
example_sentences.furigana: 入[にゅう]院[いん]する前[まえ]に、お世[せ]話[わ]になる医[い]者[しゃ]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の間、叔母の家でお世話になることになりました。
example_sentences.english: It's been settled that I'll stay with my aunt for the summer.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]の間[あいだ]、叔母[おば]の家[いえ]でお世[せ]話[わ]になることになりました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A baker flips a flawless omelette off a lump of fresh <reading>omelette dough</reading>. The whole cafe stands up and shouts <reading>おめでとう</reading>, which is how you say <vocabulary form="おめでとう">congratulations</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟に赤ちゃんが生まれたので、電話でおめでとうと言いました。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother's baby was born, so I called him to say congratulations.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]に赤[あか]ちゃんが生[う]まれたので、電[でん]話[わ]でおめでとうと言[い]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 家族みんなで祖父に「おめでとう」と言って、ケーキを出しました。
example_sentences.english: The whole family said "Congratulations!" to Grandpa and brought out the cake.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]みんなで祖[そ]父[ふ]に「おめでとう」と言[い]って、ケーキを出[だ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 給料が上がったって？おめでとう！
example_sentences.english: Your salary went up? Congratulations!
example_sentences.furigana: 給[きゅう]料[りょう]が上[あ]がったって？おめでとう！

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — お＋大（だい）＋事（じ）＋に, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Wishing importance to their health: odaiji ni.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A sick friend should treat getting better as a <kanji form="大">big</kanji> <kanji form="事">matter</kanji>, barbed to them so they cannot set it down. Telling them so is how you say <vocabulary form="お大事に">take care (get well)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があるなら、今日は早く帰ってください。お大事に。
example_sentences.english: If you have a fever, please go home early today. Take care.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねつ]があるなら、今日[きょう]は早[はや]く帰[かえ]ってください。お大[だい]事[じ]に。

example_sentences.japanese: 薬局の人は薬を渡して、「お大事に」と言いました。
example_sentences.english: The pharmacist handed me the medicine and said, "Get well soon."
example_sentences.furigana: 薬[やっ]局[きょく]の人[ひと]は薬[くすり]を渡[わた]して、「お大[だい]事[じ]に」と言[い]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 足の怪我、お大事にしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please take good care of that injured leg.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]の怪[け]我[が]、お大[だい]事[じ]にしてください。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A request for good favor: yoroshiku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the two-person boat the deal is simple: <reading>you row, she cooks</reading>. You shake on it and say <reading>よろしく</reading>, asking her to <vocabulary form="よろしく">please treat me well</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日からこの会社で働く田中です。よろしくお願いします。
example_sentences.english: I'm Tanaka, and I start working at this company today. I look forward to working with you.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]からこの会[かい]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]く田中[たなか]です。よろしくお願[ねが]いします。

example_sentences.japanese: 今年はありがとう。来年もよろしくね。
example_sentences.english: Thanks for this year. Let's keep it up next year too.
example_sentences.furigana: 今年[ことし]はありがとう。来[らい]年[ねん]もよろしくね。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣に引っ越してきた人が、「よろしく」とお菓子をくれました。
example_sentences.english: The person who moved in next door gave me some sweets and said, "Nice to meet you."
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]に引[ひ]っ越[こ]してきた人[ひと]が、「よろしく」とお菓[か]子[し]をくれました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hold the lift doors and wave the next person in, telling them to <reading>do so</reading> before you. You say <reading>どうぞ</reading>, which is <vocabulary form="どうぞ">please (go ahead)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このペン、借りてもいいですか」「はい、どうぞ」
example_sentences.english: "May I borrow this pen?" "Sure, go ahead."
example_sentences.furigana: 「このペン、借[か]りてもいいですか」「はい、どうぞ」

example_sentences.japanese: エレベーターの前で、おばあさんに「どうぞ」と言いました。
example_sentences.english: At the elevator, I said "After you" to an elderly woman.
example_sentences.furigana: エレベーターの前[まえ]で、おばあさんに「どうぞ」と言[い]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: どうぞ、ゆっくり召し上がってください。
example_sentences.english: Please, take your time and enjoy your meal.
example_sentences.furigana: どうぞ、ゆっくり召[め]し上[あ]がってください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（だい）＋丈（じょう）＋夫（ぶ）＋です, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Reassuring that all is well: daijoubu desu.
items.furigana: 大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]です
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="大">big</kanji> man built to full <kanji form="丈">measure</kanji> is a <kanji form="夫">man</kanji> nothing knocks over. Point at that sturdy figure and you are saying <vocabulary form="大丈夫です">it's fine / no problem</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 「荷物、持ちましょうか」「大丈夫です。軽いですから」
example_sentences.english: "Shall I carry your bag?" "I'm fine, it's light."
example_sentences.furigana: 「荷[に]物[もつ]、持[も]ちましょうか」「大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]です。軽[かる]いですから」

example_sentences.japanese: 傘がなくても、駅まで近いので大丈夫です。
example_sentences.english: I don't need an umbrella; the station is close, so it's no problem.
example_sentences.furigana: 傘[かさ]がなくても、駅[えき]まで近[ちか]いので大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 熱は下がりました。月曜日から会社に行っても大丈夫ですか。
example_sentences.english: My fever has gone down. Is it okay for me to go back to work from Monday?
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねつ]は下[さ]がりました。月[げつ]曜[よう]日[び]から会[かい]社[しゃ]に行[い]っても大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]ですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 早（さっ）＋速（そく）＋ですが, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A polite way to start business: sassoku desu ga.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The sun is barely <kanji form="早">early</kanji>-morning high and you are already moving <kanji form="速">quick</kanji> on the job. Starting with no small talk like that is <vocabulary form="早速ですが">getting right to it</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 早速ですが、今日の予定を説明します。
example_sentences.english: Getting right to it, I'll explain today's schedule.
example_sentences.furigana: 早[さっ]速[そく]ですが、今日[きょう]の予[よ]定[てい]を説[せつ]明[めい]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 早速ですが、この書類に名前を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Let's get straight to it: please write your name on this form.
example_sentences.furigana: 早[さっ]速[そく]ですが、この書[しょ]類[るい]に名[な]前[まえ]を書[か]いてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 早速ですが、値段について質問があります。
example_sentences.english: To get right to the point, I have a question about the price.
example_sentences.furigana: 早[さっ]速[そく]ですが、値[ね]段[だん]について質[しつ]問[もん]があります。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — お ＋ 気（き）on'yomi ＋ に ＋ 召（め）kun'yomi ＋ す.
items.mnemonic_text: Something entering their favored spirit: oki ni mesu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A fine object <kanji form="召">calls</kanji> out to a person's <kanji form="気">spirit</kanji> and lifts it like steam off a mown field. Something that can do that has managed <vocabulary form="お気に召す">to be pleasing (honorific)</vocabulary>.
items.description: Honorific, and used only about what pleases someone you are raising up, such as a guest, customer, or superior. Never use it for your own likes.

example_sentences.japanese: お気に召すサイズがなかったら、言ってください。
example_sentences.english: If we don't have a size you like, please let us know.
example_sentences.furigana: お気[き]に召[め]すサイズがなかったら、言[い]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: どうぞ、お気に召す物を一つ選んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please, choose any one item you like.
example_sentences.furigana: どうぞ、お気[き]に召[め]す物[もの]を一[ひと]つ選[えら]んでください。

example_sentences.japanese: この和食は、お客さんのお気に召すと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think our guest will be pleased with this Japanese meal.
example_sentences.furigana: この和[わ]食[しょく]は、お客[きゃく]さんのお気[き]に召[め]すと思[おも]います。

items.word_type: な adjective, adverb, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The pet shop <reading>canary</reading> is louder than a normal bird by a wide margin. Naming that wide margin above ordinary is <reading>かなり</reading>, meaning <vocabulary form="かなり">quite / considerably</vocabulary>.
items.description: Usually an adverb placed right before an adjective, close to fairly or pretty in English. It can also act as a na-adjective before a noun, but that use is much rarer.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅から旅館まで、歩くとかなり遠いです。
example_sentences.english: It's quite a long way from the station to the inn on foot.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]から旅[りょ]館[かん]まで、歩[ある]くとかなり遠[とお]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 一年でかなり日本語が上手になりましたね。
example_sentences.english: Your Japanese has gotten a lot better in a year.
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いち]年[ねん]でかなり日本[にほん]語[ご]が上手[じょうず]になりましたね。

example_sentences.japanese: このカレーはかなり辛いので、牛乳を飲みながら食べました。
example_sentences.english: This curry was pretty spicy, so I ate it while drinking milk.
example_sentences.furigana: このカレーはかなり辛[から]いので、牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]を飲[の]みながら食[た]べました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 十（じゅう）＋分（ぶん）＋な, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The na-form of juubun: sufficiently enough.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Cut something into <kanji form="十">ten</kanji> <kanji form="分">part</kanji>s and hand someone all ten. Getting the whole set with none missing is what <vocabulary form="十分な">sufficient (attributive)</vocabulary> describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 十分な時間がなかったので、最後の問題はできませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn't have enough time, so I couldn't do the last question.
example_sentences.furigana: 十[じゅう]分[ぶん]な時[じ]間[かん]がなかったので、最[さい]後[ご]の問[もん]題[だい]はできませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中には、四人に十分な食べ物があります。
example_sentences.english: There's enough food in the fridge for four people.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の中[なか]には、四[よ]人[にん]に十[じゅう]分[ぶん]な食[た]べ物[もの]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫に十分な水をあげてから、出かけました。
example_sentences.english: I gave the cat plenty of water before heading out.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]に十[じゅう]分[ぶん]な水[みず]をあげてから、出[で]かけました。

items.word_type: な adjective, adverb, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 特（とく）＋別（べつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One cow, held <kanji form="別">separate</kanji> from the market herd for the temple alone, is <kanji form="特">special</kanji>. That set-apart quality is what <vocabulary form="特別">special</vocabulary> means, and as a な adjective the word takes な before its noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は特別な日なので、レストランで食事します。
example_sentences.english: Today is a special day, so we're eating at a restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は特[とく]別[べつ]な日[ひ]なので、レストランで食[しょく]事[じ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: このお茶は、特別なお客さんにだけ出します。
example_sentences.english: We only serve this tea to special guests.
example_sentences.furigana: このお茶[ちゃ]は、特[とく]別[べつ]なお客[きゃく]さんにだけ出[だ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員さんが特別に安くしてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The shop clerk gave me a special discount.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]さんが特[とく]別[べつ]に安[やす]くしてくれました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 重（じゅう）＋要（よう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pile a thousand rice sacks onto something you already <kanji form="要">need</kanji>, and the <kanji form="重">heavy</kanji> load makes it impossible to set aside. A need that weighs that much is <vocabulary form="重要">important</vocabulary>, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

example_sentences.japanese: この書類はとても重要なので、無くさないでください。
example_sentences.english: This document is very important, so please don't lose it.
example_sentences.furigana: この書[しょ]類[るい]はとても重[じゅう]要[よう]なので、無[な]くさないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 部長は重要な会議の前に、いつも水を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: The department head always drinks water before an important meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 部[ぶ]長[ちょう]は重[じゅう]要[よう]な会[かい]議[ぎ]の前[まえ]に、いつも水[みず]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験に合格するために、何が一番重要ですか。
example_sentences.english: What matters most for passing the exam?
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]に合[ごう]格[かく]するために、何[なに]が一[いち]番[ばん]重[じゅう]要[よう]ですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（たい）＋切（せつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Big (大) and cutting (切) close: precious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture one sharp stroke about to <kanji form="切">cut</kanji> away a <kanji form="大">big</kanji> piece of your life. What you would throw yourself in front of to save is <vocabulary form="大切">important / precious</vocabulary>, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

example_sentences.japanese: これは叔母にもらった大切な指輪です。
example_sentences.english: This is a precious ring my aunt gave me.
example_sentences.furigana: これは叔母[おば]にもらった大[たい]切[せつ]な指[ゆび]輪[わ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館の本は大切に使ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please take good care of library books.
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]の本[ほん]は大[たい]切[せつ]に使[つか]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 健康は、お金より大切だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think health is more important than money.
example_sentences.furigana: 健[けん]康[こう]は、お金[かね]より大[たい]切[せつ]だと思[おも]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 幸（こう）＋福（ふく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Good fortune (幸) and blessing (福): happiness.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set the homegrown <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji> of a stalk in your own soil next to an outright <kanji form="福">blessing</kanji> dropped in your lap, and stacked together they are <vocabulary form="幸福">formal happiness</vocabulary>. This is a な adjective, so な goes in front of the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族の幸福を祈っています。
example_sentences.english: I'm praying for my family's happiness.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]の幸[こう]福[ふく]を祈[いの]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: お金がたくさんある人も、いつも幸福ではありません。
example_sentences.english: People with lots of money aren't always happy either.
example_sentences.furigana: お金[かね]がたくさんある人[ひと]も、いつも幸[こう]福[ふく]ではありません。

example_sentences.japanese: その夫婦は、海の近くの家で幸福に過ごしました。
example_sentences.english: The couple lived happily in a house near the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: その夫[ふう]婦[ふ]は、海[うみ]の近[ちか]くの家[いえ]で幸[こう]福[ふく]に過[す]ごしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 幸（しあわ）＋せ.
items.mnemonic_text: A blessed state of being: shiawase.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk you raised yourself, coming up green through your own patch of earth, is the small sure <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji> of being <vocabulary form="幸せ">happy / fortunate</vocabulary>. It works as a な adjective, so な sits before the noun.
items.reading_mnemonic: When the stalk she raised herself pokes green through her own patch of earth, the gardener crouches and <reading>she waves</reading> at it, <reading>しあわせ</reading>, as <vocabulary form="幸せ">happy</vocabulary> as anyone can be.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い日に熱いラーメンを食べると、幸せな気分になります。
example_sentences.english: Eating hot ramen on a cold day puts me in a happy mood.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い日[ひ]に熱[あつ]いラーメンを食[た]べると、幸[しあわ]せな気[き]分[ぶん]になります。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と公園を散歩する時間が一番幸せです。
example_sentences.english: Walking the dog in the park is when I'm happiest.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]と公[こう]園[えん]を散[さん]歩[ぽ]する時[じ]間[かん]が一[いち]番[ばん]幸[しあわ]せです。

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚おめでとう。幸せになってください。
example_sentences.english: Congratulations on your wedding. I hope you'll be happy.
example_sentences.furigana: 結[けっ]婚[こん]おめでとう。幸[しあわ]せになってください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋幸（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Draw one hard <kanji form="不">negative</kanji> stroke through that stalk of <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji> standing in your own soil, and what is left is <vocabulary form="不幸">unfortunate / misfortune</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な comes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年は病気や怪我で、不幸な一年でした。
example_sentences.english: Last year was an unlucky year, with illness and injuries.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]は病[びょう]気[き]や怪[け]我[が]で、不[ふ]幸[こう]な一[いち]年[ねん]でした。

example_sentences.japanese: 不幸にも、旅行の日に台風が来ました。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, a typhoon hit on the day of our trip.
example_sentences.furigana: 不[ふ]幸[こう]にも、旅[りょ]行[こう]の日[ひ]に台[たい]風[ふう]が来[き]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の不幸を聞いて、とても悲しくなった。
example_sentences.english: I felt very sad when I heard about my friend's misfortune.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の不[ふ]幸[こう]を聞[き]いて、とても悲[かな]しくなった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 気（き）＋楽（らく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Let your <kanji form="気">spirit</kanji> rise off you light as steam and everything within reach feel like plain <kanji form="楽">ease</kanji>, and that is what being <vocabulary form="気楽">carefree / relaxed</vocabulary> is. As a な adjective, な comes before the noun it modifies.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で旅行するのは気楽です。
example_sentences.english: Traveling alone is easygoing.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で旅[りょ]行[こう]するのは気[き]楽[らく]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験が終わって、気楽な週末を過ごしています。
example_sentences.english: Exams are over, and I'm having a relaxed weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]が終[お]わって、気[き]楽[らく]な週[しゅう]末[まつ]を過[す]ごしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は最初の授業ですから、気楽に質問してください。
example_sentences.english: It's only the first class today, so feel free to ask questions.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は最[さい]初[しょ]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]ですから、気[き]楽[らく]に質[しつ]問[もん]してください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 申（もう）＋し＋込（こ）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: Speaking your request into the pile: moushikomu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You fill in your name and push the sheet into the <kanji form="込">crowded</kanji> stack of everyone else's forms on the counter. Adding yourself to that packed pile is how you <vocabulary form="申し込む">apply</vocabulary> for a place.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月の日本語の試験に申し込みました。
example_sentences.english: I signed up for next month's Japanese exam.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]の日本[にほん]語[ご]の試[し]験[けん]に申[もう]し込[こ]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 電話でも申し込むことができますよ。
example_sentences.english: You can apply by phone, too.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]でも申[もう]し込[こ]むことができますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 早く申し込まなければ、席が無くなるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: If you don't sign up soon, the seats might run out.
example_sentences.furigana: 早[はや]く申[もう]し込[こ]まなければ、席[せき]が無[な]くなるかもしれません。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — ご＋存（ぞん）＋じ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A fact your honored guest is already <kanji form="存">aware of</kanji> was sitting in their head before you spoke. Something that already <kanji form="存">exists</kanji> in a superior's mind before it is said is the honored form of <vocabulary form="ご存じ">knowing</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: この近くに郵便局があるか、ご存じですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you know if there's a post office near here?
example_sentences.furigana: この近[ちか]くに郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]があるか、ご存[ぞん]じですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員なら、バスの時間をご存じだと思います。
example_sentences.english: The station staff should know the bus times.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]なら、バスの時[じ]間[かん]をご存[ぞん]じだと思[おも]います。

example_sentences.japanese: あの方は日本の歴史をよくご存じです。
example_sentences.english: That gentleman knows Japanese history very well.
example_sentences.furigana: あの方[ほう]は日本[にほん]の歴[れき]史[し]をよくご存[ぞん]じです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 迎（むか）＋える.
items.mnemonic_text: Going out on the road to meet someone: mukaeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You throw the front door open, step out onto the path, and draw your visitor inside by both hands: doing that to a guest is how you <vocabulary form="迎える">welcome / greet</vocabulary> them.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cow pulls up in a taxi with one long <reading>moo-car</reading> honk. You throw the front door open, step onto the path and draw her in by both hooves, <reading>むかえる</reading>, to <vocabulary form="迎える">welcome</vocabulary> her.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が駅まで弟を迎えに行きました。
example_sentences.english: Dad went to the station to pick up my little brother.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]が駅[えき]まで弟[おとうと]を迎[むか]えに行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館の人たちが笑って客を迎えました。
example_sentences.english: The staff at the inn greeted the guests with a smile.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]館[かん]の人[ひと]たちが笑[わら]って客[きゃく]を迎[むか]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の春、うちは新しい猫を家族に迎えました。
example_sentences.english: This spring, we welcomed a new cat into the family.
example_sentences.furigana: 今年[ことし]の春[はる]、うちは新[あたら]しい猫[ねこ]を家[か]族[ぞく]に迎[むか]えました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 沈（しず）＋む.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A slow leak fills the rowboat until it tips its nose down and slides under the lake, and the water closes flat over the top. A heavy thing dropping below the surface and staying there is what it is to <vocabulary form="沈む">sink</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The free diver breathes out, whispers 「<reading>she zooms</reading>」, and drops straight down to the dark lake bed. Going under the water and staying down there is what it means to <vocabulary form="沈む">sink</vocabulary>, 「<reading>しずむ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏は夜の八時ごろに日が沈みます。
example_sentences.english: In summer, the sun sets around eight at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]は夜[よる]の八[はち]時[じ]ごろに日[ひ]が沈[しず]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が作った紙の船は、すぐ湖に沈んだ。
example_sentences.english: The paper boat the kid made sank into the lake right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が作[つく]った紙[かみ]の船[ふね]は、すぐ湖[みずうみ]に沈[しず]んだ。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、いつも気分が沈むんです。
example_sentences.english: Rainy days always get me down.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、いつも気[き]分[ぶん]が沈[しず]むんです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 伺（うかが）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) watching (司) respectfully: ukagau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You knock softly and wait outside the doorway until someone waves you in, then lean your head through to put your question. Approaching a person's home and their attention that carefully is to <vocabulary form="伺う">visit and ask humbly</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A polite <reading>kangaroo</reading> props its paws on the garden fence and waits to be waved through before hopping in to ask after your health. Peeking in and raising a question that gently is <vocabulary form="伺う">to visit and ask humbly</vocabulary>, which comes out as <reading>うかがう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週の火曜日に、そちらへ伺ってもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: May I come and visit you next Tuesday?
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]週[しゅう]の火[か]曜[よう]日[び]に、そちらへ伺[うかが]ってもいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: そのお話は、会議の後でゆっくり伺います。
example_sentences.english: I'll hear about that properly after the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: そのお話[はなし]は、会[かい]議[ぎ]の後[あと]でゆっくり伺[うかが]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員に道を伺ったら、親切に教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: When I asked the station staff for directions, they explained kindly.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]に道[みち]を伺[うかが]ったら、親[しん]切[せつ]に教[おし]えてくれました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 残（ざん）＋念（ねん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A remaining (残) thought (念): a shame.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The one <kanji form="念">wish</kanji> you never acted on is the part that <kanji form="残">remains</kanji> unburied after the chance is gone. That is what <vocabulary form="残念">regrettable</vocabulary> names, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 残念ですが、その日は会議があって行けません。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, I have a meeting that day, so I can't go.
example_sentences.furigana: 残[ざん]念[ねん]ですが、その日[ひ]は会[かい]議[ぎ]があって行[い]けません。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前のあの喫茶店が無くなって、本当に残念です。
example_sentences.english: It's a real shame that café in front of the station is gone.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]のあの喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]が無[な]くなって、本[ほん]当[とう]に残[ざん]念[ねん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 残念な結果でしたが、次の試験のためにまた勉強します。
example_sentences.english: The result was disappointing, but I'll study again for the next exam.
example_sentences.furigana: 残[ざん]念[ねん]な結[けっ]果[か]でしたが、次[つぎ]の試[し]験[けん]のためにまた勉[べん]強[きょう]します。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 祈（いの）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: An altar (示) plus an axe-shaped vow: inoru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Bow your head, close your eyes, and quietly ask a power you cannot see to keep someone safe. That asking, with nothing but words, is to <vocabulary form="祈る">pray</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At dawn a line of pilgrims kneels in one long <reading>row</reading> on the shrine steps, foreheads to the stone, each asking an unseen power for rain. Kneeling in a <reading>row</reading> and begging like that is to <vocabulary form="祈る">pray</vocabulary>, which is <reading>いのる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は毎晩、寝る前に静かに祈ります。
example_sentences.english: Every night before bed, my grandmother prays quietly.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]、寝[ね]る前[まえ]に静[しず]かに祈[いの]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の試験の前に、家族みんなで祈りました。
example_sentences.english: Before my little brother's exam, the whole family prayed together.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の試[し]験[けん]の前[まえ]に、家[か]族[ぞく]みんなで祈[いの]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は雨が降らないように祈っています。
example_sentences.english: I'm praying it doesn't rain this weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]らないように祈[いの]っています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 拝（はい）＋見（けん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Bowing (拝) to view (見): to humbly look.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You bow so low over the offered document that your <kanji form="見">seeing</kanji> eye has to peer up at it from just above the floor. Looking at what someone shows you from that far down is how you <vocabulary form="拝見する">see it, humbly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、お手紙を拝見しました。
example_sentences.english: I read your letter yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、お手[て]紙[がみ]を拝[はい]見[けん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、切符を拝見します。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, may I see your ticket?
example_sentences.furigana: すみません、切[きっ]符[ぷ]を拝[はい]見[けん]します。

example_sentences.japanese: おじいさんの古い写真を拝見して、とても驚きました。
example_sentences.english: I was really surprised when I saw your grandfather's old photos.
example_sentences.furigana: おじいさんの古[ふる]い写[しゃ]真[しん]を拝[はい]見[けん]して、とても驚[おどろ]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 承（しょう）＋知（ち）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving (承) knowledge (知) humbly: shouchi suru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An order comes in and lands dead center, the way the arrow thumps into the target: now you <kanji form="知">know</kanji> it. Bowing to show it struck home and you will carry it out is how you <vocabulary form="承知する">acknowledge an instruction, humbly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: はい、承知しました。書類は明日の朝までに送ります。
example_sentences.english: Yes, understood. I'll send the documents by tomorrow morning.
example_sentences.furigana: はい、承[しょう]知[ち]しました。書[しょ]類[るい]は明日[あした]の朝[あさ]までに送[おく]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員は「承知しました」と言って、すぐ席を準備した。
example_sentences.english: The clerk said "Certainly" and got a seat ready right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]は「承[しょう]知[ち]しました」と言[い]って、すぐ席[せき]を準[じゅん]備[び]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 値段が高いことは承知していますが、これを買います。
example_sentences.english: I'm well aware it's expensive, but I'll take this one.
example_sentences.furigana: 値[ね]段[だん]が高[たか]いことは承[しょう]知[ち]していますが、これを買[か]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 逃（に）＋げる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The side door is propped open a crack, and by the time the guard turns back the cell is empty. Getting clear through a gap before anyone can stop you is what it means <vocabulary form="逃げる">to escape / run away</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Nigel</reading> the gerbil works a bar of his cage loose every night and is halfway down the hall before the lights come on. A small thing bolting for the gap the moment it opens is 「<reading>にげる</reading>」, <vocabulary form="逃げる">to escape / run away</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: ドアを開けたら、犬が外へ逃げてしまった。
example_sentences.english: When I opened the door, the dog ran off outside.
example_sentences.furigana: ドアを開[あ]けたら、犬[いぬ]が外[そと]へ逃[に]げてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が強かったので、みんな駅の中に逃げました。
example_sentences.english: The rain was so heavy that everyone fled into the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が強[つよ]かったので、みんな駅[えき]の中[なか]に逃[に]げました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟はいつも宿題から逃げて、テレビを見ています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother always runs away from his homework and watches TV.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]はいつも宿[しゅく]題[だい]から逃[に]げて、テレビを見[み]ています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 追（お）＋いかける.
items.mnemonic_text: Following closely on the road: oikakeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A bun rolls off the bakery shelf and a boy runs after it down three aisles, hands out, never quite closing the gap. Staying right behind a thing that will not stop, trying to catch it, is what it means <vocabulary form="追いかける">to chase</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The baker bellows <reading>oi, cack-a-roo</reading> at the boy hopping down three aisles after the runaway bun, never quite closing the gap: <reading>おいかける</reading>, to <vocabulary form="追いかける">chase</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 庭で、うちの猫が鳥を追いかけていました。
example_sentences.english: Our cat was chasing a bird in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 庭[にわ]で、うちの猫[ねこ]が鳥[とり]を追[お]いかけていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 風で飛んだ帽子を、走って追いかけました。
example_sentences.english: I ran after my hat when the wind blew it away.
example_sentences.furigana: 風[かぜ]で飛[と]んだ帽[ぼう]子[し]を、走[はし]って追[お]いかけました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は今も自分の夢を追いかけています。
example_sentences.english: He is still chasing his dream.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は今[いま]も自[じ]分[ぶん]の夢[ゆめ]を追[お]いかけています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 怒（おこ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (心) enslaved (奴) by rage: okoru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone slides into the parking spot you waited ten minutes for and smirks at you through the glass. Your face goes hot, your voice climbs, and that sudden flare of temper is what it means <vocabulary form="怒る">to get angry</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The driver who slid into your parking spot smirks at you over a tub of <reading>okra</reading>, and your face goes hot as your voice climbs: <reading>おこる</reading>, to <vocabulary form="怒る">get angry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟はよく怒る。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother gets angry a lot.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]はよく怒[おこ]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 私が遅れたので、先生が怒りました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher got angry because I was late.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]が遅[おく]れたので、先[せん]生[せい]が怒[おこ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はなぜ怒っているのですか。
example_sentences.english: Why is she angry?
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はなぜ怒[おこ]っているのですか。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 信（しん）＋じる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To take another person's word as plain <kanji form="信">truth</kanji>, with no proof in your hand, is to <vocabulary form="信じる">believe</vocabulary> them.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の言葉を信じる人は、弟だけでした。
example_sentences.english: The only one who believed what I said was my little brother.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の言[こと]葉[ば]を信[しん]じる人[ひと]は、弟[おとうと]だけでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 母はいつも「自分の力を信じる」と言っています。
example_sentences.english: My mom always says, "Believe in your own strength."
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]はいつも「自[じ]分[ぶん]の力[ちから]を信[しん]じる」と言[い]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫が冷蔵庫を開けた話は、誰も信じるはずがない。
example_sentences.english: There's no way anyone will believe the story about the cat opening the fridge.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]が冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]を開[あ]けた話[はなし]は、誰[だれ]も信[しん]じるはずがない。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 浮（う）＋かぶ.
items.mnemonic_text: Bobbing lightly on the water: ukabu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You let go of the beach ball under the pool water and it shoots straight back up to sit on the surface. A thing riding on top of the water instead of going under is what it is to <vocabulary form="浮かぶ">float</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You <reading>hook a boot</reading> out of the canal, and it will not stay under no matter how you shove it. It keeps riding back up to the top, and sitting on the surface like that is what it means to <vocabulary form="浮かぶ">float</vocabulary>, 「<reading>うかぶ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 見て、川に大きい魚が浮かんでいるよ。
example_sentences.english: Look, there's a big fish floating in the river.
example_sentences.furigana: 見[み]て、川[かわ]に大[おお]きい魚[さかな]が浮[う]かんでいるよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 海では体が軽いから、簡単に浮かぶことができます。
example_sentences.english: Your body is light in the sea, so you can float easily.
example_sentences.furigana: 海[うみ]では体[からだ]が軽[かる]いから、簡[かん]単[たん]に浮[う]かぶことができます。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験のとき、答えが全然浮かびませんでした。
example_sentences.english: During the exam, the answers just wouldn't come to me.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]のとき、答[こた]えが全[ぜん]然[ぜん]浮[う]かびませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 凍（こお）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Ice locking the water still: kooru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Leave water still in the cold long enough and it turns hard and <kanji form="凍">frozen</kanji> all by itself. Water going solid like that, with nobody freezing it, is <vocabulary form="凍る">to freeze</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Cora</reading> leaves a bucket of water sitting still in the cold overnight, and by dawn it has turned hard all by itself. She taps the ice and says <reading>こおる</reading>, having watched water <vocabulary form="凍る">freeze</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 外に置いておいた水が、朝には凍っていました。
example_sentences.english: The water I'd left outside was frozen by morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[そと]に置[お]いておいた水[みず]が、朝[あさ]には凍[こお]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中で牛乳が凍っていたので、飲めませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The milk had frozen in the fridge, so I couldn't drink it.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の中[なか]で牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]が凍[こお]っていたので、飲[の]めませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬は道が凍るので、ゆっくり歩いてください。
example_sentences.english: The roads freeze in winter, so please walk slowly.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]は道[みち]が凍[こお]るので、ゆっくり歩[ある]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 悩（なや）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (忄) tangled in brains (脳): nayamu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You have two job offers and one week to pick, and every night you lie awake running the same lists. Turning a hard choice over and over until it wears a groove in you is <vocabulary form="悩む">to worry / agonize</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Lying awake over the two job offers, you <reading>gnaw a yam</reading> at midnight and run the same lists again until they wear a groove: <reading>なやむ</reading>, to <vocabulary form="悩む">agonize</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: どれを買うか悩んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I can't decide which one to buy.
example_sentences.furigana: どれを買[か]うか悩[なや]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は仕事のことでいつも悩んでいる。
example_sentences.english: She's always worried about work.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は仕[し]事[ごと]のことでいつも悩[なや]んでいる。

example_sentences.japanese: 悩んでも答えが見つからなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even after agonizing over it, I couldn't find an answer.
example_sentences.furigana: 悩[なや]んでも答[こた]えが見[み]つからなかった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 修（しゅう）＋理（り）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Cultivating (修) the logic (理) back: to repair.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="修">discipline</kanji> a broken machine part by part until every piece lines up with its own <kanji form="理">logic</kanji> again, and that is to <vocabulary form="修理する">repair</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は壊れたラジオを修理するのが得意です。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is good at repairing broken radios.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は壊[こわ]れたラジオを修[しゅう]理[り]するのが得[とく]意[い]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫が動かないので、明日修理する人が来ます。
example_sentences.english: The fridge isn't working, so someone is coming tomorrow to repair it.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]が動[うご]かないので、明日[あした]修[しゅう]理[り]する人[ひと]が来[き]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い靴を修理する店が、駅の近くにあります。
example_sentences.english: There's a shop near the station that repairs old shoes.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い靴[くつ]を修[しゅう]理[り]する店[みせ]が、駅[えき]の近[ちか]くにあります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 致（いた）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: A humble hand reaching to serve: itasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A servant finishes every task before anyone notices it needed doing, then sweeps away their own footprints so no one sees the work. Getting the whole job done while keeping yourself invisible is to <vocabulary form="致す">do it, humbly</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Two overalled helpers answer every call at the back door with a soft <reading>it's us</reading>, then quietly fix whatever broke and slip out again. Doing the work for someone while staying that far in the background is <vocabulary form="致す">to do, humbly</vocabulary>, spoken as <reading>いたす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夕方、もう一度電話致します。
example_sentences.english: I'll call you once more this evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 夕[ゆう]方[がた]、もう一[いち]度[ど]電[でん]話[わ]致[いた]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 料理は私が致しますので、テレビでも見ていてください。
example_sentences.english: I'll take care of the cooking, so why not watch some TV?
example_sentences.furigana: 料[りょう]理[り]は私[わたし]が致[いた]しますので、テレビでも見[み]ていてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み物はコーヒーに致します。
example_sentences.english: For my drink, I'll have coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: 飲[の]み物[もの]はコーヒーに致[いた]します。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 差（さ）on'yomi ＋ し ＋ 上（あ）kun'yomi ＋ げ ＋ る.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Noticing the <kanji form="差">difference</kanji> in rank between you and the higher-ranked person, you raise the gift <kanji form="上">up</kanji> with both arms so it travels toward them. Handing something upward across that gap is to <vocabulary form="差し上げる">give, humbly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんにお茶を差し上げてください。
example_sentences.english: Please serve our guest some tea.
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さんにお茶[ちゃ]を差[さ]し上[あ]げてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館の方に、外国のお菓子を差し上げました。
example_sentences.english: I gave the staff at the inn some sweets from abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]館[かん]の方[ほう]に、外[がい]国[こく]のお菓[か]子[し]を差[さ]し上[あ]げました。

example_sentences.japanese: この本、よかったら差し上げます。
example_sentences.english: If you'd like this book, it's yours.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]、よかったら差[さ]し上[あ]げます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 頂（いただ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving something atop your head: itadaku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You take the gift in both hands and lift it up past your forehead, putting yourself lower than the thing you were just given. Receiving or eating anything from that bowed-under position is to <vocabulary form="頂く">receive it, humbly</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the shrine a tame duck waddles up and drops a rice cracker into your cupped hands, and you bow lower than the bird to take it. That <reading>eat a duck</reading> moment, receiving with your head down, is <vocabulary form="頂く">to receive and eat, humbly</vocabulary>, said as <reading>いただく</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の方から野菜をたくさん頂きました。
example_sentences.english: Our neighbor gave us a whole lot of vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の方[ほう]から野[や]菜[さい]をたくさん頂[いただ]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: お水を少し頂いてもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Could I have a little water?
example_sentences.furigana: お水[みず]を少[すこ]し頂[いただ]いてもいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で親切な女性に地図を頂きました。
example_sentences.english: A kind woman at the station gave me a map.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で親[しん]切[せつ]な女[じょ]性[せい]に地[ち]図[ず]を頂[いただ]きました。

items.word_type: godan verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 喜（よろこ）＋ぶ.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) opening wide in joy: yorokobu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand someone the news they have been hoping for and watch them <kanji form="喜">rejoice</kanji>, all grin and thank-yous and a little bounce. That whole warm rush when something goes right for you is being <vocabulary form="喜ぶ">pleased</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hand your friend the news she has waited for and she bounces so hard she slops <reading>your cocoa</reading> everywhere, all grin and thank-yous: <reading>よろこぶ</reading>, to be <vocabulary form="喜ぶ">pleased</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は花をもらって喜びました。
example_sentences.english: My mother was delighted to receive the flowers.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は花[はな]をもらって喜[よろこ]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供はお菓子を食べて喜びました。
example_sentences.english: The child was happy eating the sweets.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]はお菓[か]子[し]を食[た]べて喜[よろこ]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は先生の話を聞いて喜んでいるようだ。
example_sentences.english: He seems pleased to hear the teacher's story.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は先[せん]生[せい]の話[はなし]を聞[き]いて喜[よろこ]んでいるようだ。

items.word_type: する verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 期（き）＋待（たい）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A period (期) awaited (待): to expect.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <kanji form="待">wait</kanji> out a fixed <kanji form="期">period</kanji>, sure the thing is coming, is to <vocabulary form="期待する">expect</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が私に期待するのは、試験の結果です。
example_sentences.english: What my father expects from me is exam results.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]が私[わたし]に期[き]待[たい]するのは、試[し]験[けん]の結[けっ]果[か]です。

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが期待する旅行だったのに、毎日雨でした。
example_sentences.english: Everyone was looking forward to the trip, but it rained every day.
example_sentences.furigana: みんなが期[き]待[たい]する旅[りょ]行[こう]だったのに、毎[まい]日[にち]雨[あめ]でした。

example_sentences.japanese: あまり期待すると、残念に思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you expect too much, you'll end up disappointed.
example_sentences.furigana: あまり期[き]待[たい]すると、残[ざん]念[ねん]に思[おも]いますよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 取（と）＋り＋替（か）＋える.
items.mnemonic_text: Taking (取り) and changing (替える): to swap.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="取">take</kanji> the worn part out by the ear, the rude fast way, and drop a fresh one into the gap it left. Swapping the old for the new like that is <vocabulary form="取り替える">to exchange / replace</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 台所の電気が暗くなったので、新しいのに取り替えました。
example_sentences.english: The kitchen light had gotten dim, so I replaced it with a new one.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[だい]所[どころ]の電[でん]気[き]が暗[くら]くなったので、新[あたら]しいのに取[と]り替[か]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: このシャツは小さすぎたので、店で大きいのと取り替えてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: This shirt was too small, so the shop swapped it for a bigger one.
example_sentences.furigana: このシャツは小[ちい]さすぎたので、店[みせ]で大[おお]きいのと取[と]り替[か]えてもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 汚いタオルは毎日取り替えるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I make a point of changing out dirty towels every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 汚[きたな]いタオルは毎[まい]日[にち]取[と]り替[か]えるようにしています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 溶（と）＋ける.
items.mnemonic_text: A shape softening away in water: tokeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Drop a sugar cube into hot tea and stir once. It loses its edges, goes cloudy, and spreads through the water until it is gone, and that is what <vocabulary form="溶ける">to melt / dissolve</vocabulary> looks like.
items.reading_mnemonic: You drop a sugar cube shaped like a little <reading>token</reading> into hot tea and stir once, and its edges blur until it is gone. That vanishing is <reading>とける</reading>, to <vocabulary form="溶ける">dissolve</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑かったので、かばんの中のお菓子が溶けていました。
example_sentences.english: It was so hot that the sweets in my bag had melted.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]かったので、かばんの中[なか]のお菓[か]子[し]が溶[と]けていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 春になったら、山の雪が溶けて川に流れます。
example_sentences.english: When spring comes, the snow on the mountains melts and flows into the river.
example_sentences.furigana: 春[はる]になったら、山[やま]の雪[ゆき]が溶[と]けて川[かわ]に流[なが]れます。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たいお茶に砂糖を入れたら、全然溶けませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I put sugar in cold tea, and it didn't dissolve at all.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たいお茶[ちゃ]に砂[さ]糖[とう]を入[い]れたら、全[ぜん]然[ぜん]溶[と]けませんでした。

items.word_type: godan verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 嘆（なげ）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: After the storm the old farmer stands in the flattened field and says the same low words about the lost year, over and over, to no one. Letting that grief out loud like that is what it means <vocabulary form="嘆く">to lament</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On a fence post in the flattened field sits <reading>a gecko</reading>, and the old farmer pours his low words about the lost year out to it, over and over: <reading>なげく</reading>, to <vocabulary form="嘆く">lament</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は財布をなくして、嘆いた。
example_sentences.english: He lost his wallet and lamented it.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は財[さい]布[ふ]をなくして、嘆[なげ]いた。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は時計を壊して、嘆いている。
example_sentences.english: She broke her watch and is lamenting it.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は時計[とけい]を壊[こわ]して、嘆[なげ]いている。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は病気になって、嘆いた。
example_sentences.english: My mother fell ill and lamented it.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は病[びょう]気[き]になって、嘆[なげ]いた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 腐（くさ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Flesh (肉) crumbling under a roof: kusaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Shove a tub of rice to the back of the fridge and forget it for three weeks. The smell hits before you see the domed, slimy lid, and food left to turn that far is what <vocabulary form="腐る">to rot / spoil</vocabulary> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: Three weeks on, you pry the slimy domed lid off the forgotten rice tub and find it grey and lumpy as old <reading>couscous</reading>. You gag <reading>くさる</reading>: the rice has begun to <vocabulary form="腐る">rot</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の間に、台所の果物が全部腐ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: While we were away on the trip, all the fruit in the kitchen went bad.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]の間[あいだ]に、台[だい]所[どころ]の果物[くだもの]が全[ぜん]部[ぶ]腐[くさ]ってしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: この卵は腐っているかもしれないから、食べないでください。
example_sentences.english: This egg might be rotten, so please don't eat it.
example_sentences.furigana: この卵[たまご]は腐[くさ]っているかもしれないから、食[た]べないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い橋は木が腐っているので、渡らないでください。
example_sentences.english: The wood on the old bridge has rotted, so please don't cross it.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い橋[はし]は木[き]が腐[くさ]っているので、渡[わた]らないでください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 頼（たの）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: Trusting your weight to a bundle: tanomu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You catch your neighbour at the gate, hold out your spare key, and ask her to feed the cat while you are gone. Putting a task in someone else's hands and counting on them to do it is what it means <vocabulary form="頼む">to request / rely on</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the gate you press your spare key into the neighbour's palm with a quick <reading>ta</reading>, and the cat she will feed gives <reading>no mew</reading> of protest: <reading>たのむ</reading>, to <vocabulary form="頼む">rely on</vocabulary> her.

example_sentences.japanese: 母に駅まで迎えに来てくれるように頼みました。
example_sentences.english: I asked my mother to come pick me up at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]に駅[えき]まで迎[むか]えに来[き]てくれるように頼[たの]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 喫茶店で、コーヒーを二つ頼みました。
example_sentences.english: I ordered two coffees at the café.
example_sentences.furigana: 喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]で、コーヒーを二[ふた]つ頼[たの]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越すとき、友達に荷物を運ぶのを頼みました。
example_sentences.english: When I moved, I asked my friends to help carry my things.
example_sentences.furigana: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]すとき、友[とも]達[だち]に荷[に]物[もつ]を運[はこ]ぶのを頼[たの]みました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — ご＋覧（らん）＋になる.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You set the photo album on a stand and step back with folded hands, offering it up the way a gallery presents its finest piece. Letting an honored person <vocabulary form="ご覧になる">see something, honorifically</vocabulary>, means presenting it to them like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がご覧になる前に、この絵を直しておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's fix this drawing before the teacher sees it.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]がご覧[らん]になる前[まえ]に、この絵[え]を直[なお]しておきましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 右の窓からご覧になる海は、とてもきれいですよ。
example_sentences.english: The sea you'll see from the window on your right is really beautiful.
example_sentences.furigana: 右[みぎ]の窓[まど]からご覧[らん]になる海[うみ]は、とてもきれいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: おばあさんは毎朝、庭の花をご覧になるのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: The old lady loves looking at the flowers in the garden every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: おばあさんは毎[まい]朝[あさ]、庭[にわ]の花[はな]をご覧[らん]になるのが好[す]きです。

items.word_type: godan verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 繰（く）＋り＋返（かえ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Reeling (繰り) something back (返す): to repeat.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You set the reel <kanji form="繰">winding</kanji> forward, it <kanji form="返">return</kanji>s to the very same mark, and your hand starts it winding again. Motion that keeps coming back to its start is <vocabulary form="繰り返す">to repeat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は同じ質問をもう一度繰り返しました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher repeated the same question one more time.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は同[おな]じ質[しつ]問[もん]をもう一[いち]度[ど]繰[く]り返[かえ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟はテレビで聞いた歌を何回も繰り返して歌っています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother keeps singing a song he heard on TV, over and over.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]はテレビで聞[き]いた歌[うた]を何[なん]回[かい]も繰[く]り返[かえ]して歌[うた]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 覚えるまで、声に出して繰り返しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's say it out loud again and again until it sticks.
example_sentences.furigana: 覚[おぼ]えるまで、声[こえ]に出[だ]して繰[く]り返[かえ]しましょう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 驚（おどろ）＋く.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You lift a plant pot to move it and the whole underside is crawling with woodlice spilling out at once. The jump in your chest and the step back you take before you can think is being <vocabulary form="驚く">surprised</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You tip up what looks like an <reading>odd rock</reading> by the step and it opens into a crab and runs across your foot. You are standing before you have decided to move, and that jolt at a thing you did not expect is 「<reading>おどろく</reading>」, <vocabulary form="驚く">to be surprised</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の声に驚きました。
example_sentences.english: I was startled by the dog's bark.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の声[こえ]に驚[おどろ]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 値段が安すぎて驚きました。
example_sentences.english: The price was so cheap it surprised me.
example_sentences.furigana: 値[ね]段[だん]が安[やす]すぎて驚[おどろ]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は驚いた顔をしました。
example_sentences.english: She had a surprised look on her face.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は驚[おどろ]いた顔[かお]をしました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 方（ほう）＋法（ほう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A direction's (方) rule (法): a method.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Which <kanji form="方">direction</kanji> you choose to come at a task from is your <vocabulary form="方法">method</vocabulary> for getting it done. Pick a different way in and you have a different method.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を覚えるいい方法を先生に聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked my teacher for a good way to memorize kanji.
example_sentences.furigana: 漢[かん]字[じ]を覚[おぼ]えるいい方[ほう]法[ほう]を先[せん]生[せい]に聞[き]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが壊れたので、直す方法をインターネットで探した。
example_sentences.english: My computer broke, so I looked online for a way to fix it.
example_sentences.furigana: パソコンが壊[こわ]れたので、直[なお]す方[ほう]法[ほう]をインターネットで探[さが]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 他に方法がないなら、タクシーで行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: If there's no other way, let's take a taxi.
example_sentences.furigana: 他[ほか]に方[ほう]法[ほう]がないなら、タクシーで行[い]きましょう。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 提（てい）＋案（あん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Presenting (提) a plan (案): a proposal.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="提">carry</kanji> a worked-out <kanji form="案">plan</kanji> in your hands to the meeting and lay it flat on the table for the room. Set out to be judged like that, it is a <vocabulary form="提案">proposal</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議で私の提案が選ばれました。
example_sentences.english: My proposal was chosen at the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]で私[わたし]の提[てい]案[あん]が選[えら]ばれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹から、夏にみんなで海へ行く提案がありました。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister suggested we all go to the beach this summer.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]から、夏[なつ]にみんなで海[うみ]へ行[い]く提[てい]案[あん]がありました。

example_sentences.japanese: その提案には、少し問題があると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think there's a bit of a problem with that proposal.
example_sentences.furigana: その提[てい]案[あん]には、少[すこ]し問[もん]題[だい]があると思[おも]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 機（き）＋会（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A mechanism's (機) meeting (会): a chance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="機">mechanism</kanji> of events turns, and for one moment a gap in it lines up with you. Step through and <kanji form="会">meet</kanji> it and you have taken an <vocabulary form="機会">opportunity</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人と英語で話す機会があまりありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't get many chances to speak English with people from abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]と英[えい]語[ご]で話[はな]す機[き]会[かい]があまりありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 社長に自分の計画を説明する機会をもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got the chance to explain my own plan to the company president.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]長[ちょう]に自[じ]分[ぶん]の計[けい]画[かく]を説[せつ]明[めい]する機[き]会[かい]をもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: こんないい機会はもう来ないかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: A chance this good might never come again.
example_sentences.furigana: こんないい機[き]会[かい]はもう来[こ]ないかもしれないよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 場（ば）＋合（あい）.
items.mnemonic_text: A place's (場) fit (合): a case.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take one <kanji form="場">place</kanji> and one particular way the details inside it <kanji form="合">fit</kanji> together. That exact arrangement is the <vocabulary form="場合">case / situation</vocabulary> you are talking about.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の場合は、公園ではなく図書館で会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: If it rains, let's meet at the library instead of the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の場[ば]合[あい]は、公[こう]園[えん]ではなく図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で会[あ]いましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 熱が下がらない場合は、すぐ病院に行ってください。
example_sentences.english: If your fever doesn't go down, go to the hospital right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねつ]が下[さ]がらない場[ば]合[あい]は、すぐ病[びょう]院[いん]に行[い]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 鍵を無くした場合、どうすればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: What should I do if I lose my key?
example_sentences.furigana: 鍵[かぎ]を無[な]くした場[ば]合[あい]、どうすればいいですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 事（じ）＋情（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <kanji form="事">matter</kanji> sitting at the centre of an event drags a whole knot of <kanji form="情">feelings</kanji> in behind it. That full tangle around it is the <vocabulary form="事情">circumstances</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族の事情で、来月引っ越すことになりました。
example_sentences.english: Because of family circumstances, I'll be moving next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[か]族[ぞく]の事[じ]情[じょう]で、来[らい]月[げつ]引[ひ]っ越[こ]すことになりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 事情を話すと、店員さんは切符を取り替えてくれた。
example_sentences.english: When I explained the situation, the clerk swapped my ticket.
example_sentences.furigana: 事[じ]情[じょう]を話[はな]すと、店[てん]員[いん]さんは切[きっ]符[ぷ]を取[と]り替[か]えてくれた。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が遅れた事情は、まだ誰も知らない。
example_sentences.english: Nobody knows yet what made him late.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]が遅[おく]れた事[じ]情[じょう]は、まだ誰[だれ]も知[し]らない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 感（かん）＋情（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The whole <kanji form="感">feeling</kanji> hitting you at once, with the head left out of it entirely, settles into one named <vocabulary form="感情">emotion</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は感情がすぐ顔に出る。
example_sentences.english: My little brother's feelings show on his face right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は感[かん]情[じょう]がすぐ顔[かお]に出[で]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 怒っても、お客さんの前では感情を見せないでください。
example_sentences.english: Even if you're angry, please don't show your emotions in front of customers.
example_sentences.furigana: 怒[おこ]っても、お客[きゃく]さんの前[まえ]では感[かん]情[じょう]を見[み]せないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫にも感情があると思いますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you think cats have emotions too?
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]にも感[かん]情[じょう]があると思[おも]いますか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 性（せい）＋格（かく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your inborn <kanji form="性">nature</kanji> gets worn over years into a fixed <kanji form="格">rank</kanji> of habits and set reactions. That settled shape is what others call your <vocabulary form="性格">personality</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は厳しい性格だけど、動物には優しい。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather has a strict personality, but he's gentle with animals.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は厳[きび]しい性[せい]格[かく]だけど、動[どう]物[ぶつ]には優[やさ]しい。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉の性格なら、きっと最後まで頑張るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Knowing my sister's personality, she'll surely keep at it to the end.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]の性[せい]格[かく]なら、きっと最[さい]後[ご]まで頑[がん]張[ば]るでしょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 性格は簡単には直せないものだ。
example_sentences.english: Your personality isn't something you can fix easily.
example_sentences.furigana: 性[せい]格[かく]は簡[かん]単[たん]には直[なお]せないものだ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 科（か）＋学（がく）＋者（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A science's (科学) person (者): a scientist.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="者">person</kanji> who spends every day turning pages in one narrow <kanji form="科">department</kanji> of <kanji form="学">study</kanji> is a <vocabulary form="科学者">scientist</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者になるのが娘の夢です。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a scientist is my daughter's dream.
example_sentences.furigana: 科[か]学[がく]者[しゃ]になるのが娘[むすめ]の夢[ゆめ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: その科学者は、毎晩星空を見ながら考える。
example_sentences.english: Every night, that scientist thinks things over while looking at the starry sky.
example_sentences.furigana: その科[か]学[がく]者[しゃ]は、毎[まい]晩[ばん]星[ほし]空[ぞら]を見[み]ながら考[かんが]える。

example_sentences.japanese: 有名な科学者でも、失敗することはある。
example_sentences.english: Even famous scientists fail sometimes.
example_sentences.furigana: 有[ゆう]名[めい]な科[か]学[がく]者[しゃ]でも、失[しっ]敗[ぱい]することはある。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 会（かい）＋議（ぎ）＋室（しつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A meeting's (会議) room (室): a meeting room.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every hallway in the building ends at one <kanji form="室">room</kanji> kept for people to <kanji form="会">meet</kanji> and <kanji form="議">debate</kanji> in. That is the <vocabulary form="会議室">meeting room</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議室は三階のエレベーターの隣です。
example_sentences.english: The meeting room is on the third floor, next to the elevator.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]室[しつ]は三[さん]階[かい]のエレベーターの隣[となり]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝、会議室を予約しておきます。
example_sentences.english: I'll book the meeting room for tomorrow morning ahead of time.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の朝[あさ]、会[かい]議[ぎ]室[しつ]を予[よ]約[やく]しておきます。

example_sentences.japanese: 誰もいない会議室から、声が聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: I can hear a voice coming from the empty meeting room.
example_sentences.furigana: 誰[だれ]もいない会[かい]議[ぎ]室[しつ]から、声[こえ]が聞[き]こえる。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 案（あん）＋内（ない）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A plan (案) leading inside (内): guidance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone who holds the whole <kanji form="案">plan</kanji> of a place in their head can lead you <kanji form="内">inside</kanji> it without a wrong turn, and that service is <vocabulary form="案内">guidance / information</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港の案内を見て、出口を探した。
example_sentences.english: I looked at the airport signs to find the exit.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]の案[あん]内[ない]を見[み]て、出[で]口[ぐち]を探[さが]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の案内のメールが、まだ届きません。
example_sentences.english: The email with the trip information still hasn't arrived.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]の案[あん]内[ない]のメールが、まだ届[とど]きません。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母の案内で、森の中を歩いた。
example_sentences.english: With my grandmother as our guide, we walked through the forest.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]の案[あん]内[ない]で、森[もり]の中[なか]を歩[ある]いた。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 案（あん）＋内（ない）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: To lead someone with a plan: annai suru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You walk ahead of the visitor with the floor <kanji form="案">plan</kanji> clear in your mind and name each room <kanji form="内">inside</kanji> as you open its door. Doing that for someone is <vocabulary form="案内する">to guide / show around</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、外国から来た友人に町を案内しました。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend, I showed a friend from abroad around town.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、外[がい]国[こく]から来[き]た友[ゆう]人[じん]に町[まち]を案[あん]内[ない]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 入ったばかりの社員に、会社の中を案内してあげて。
example_sentences.english: Show the new employee around the office, would you?
example_sentences.furigana: 入[はい]ったばかりの社[しゃ]員[いん]に、会[かい]社[しゃ]の中[なか]を案[あん]内[ない]してあげて。

example_sentences.japanese: 狐が僕を山の上まで案内してくれた。
example_sentences.english: A fox led me all the way to the top of the mountain.
example_sentences.furigana: 狐[きつね]が僕[ぼく]を山[やま]の上[うえ]まで案[あん]内[ない]してくれた。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 注（ちゅう）＋意（い）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Pouring (注) meaning (意): to be careful.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji form="注">Pour</kanji> your whole <kanji form="意">mind</kanji> onto one spot and hold it there. That single act is what it means <vocabulary form="注意する">to pay attention / warn</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 車に注意して道を渡ってください。
example_sentences.english: Watch out for cars when you cross the street.
example_sentences.furigana: 車[くるま]に注[ちゅう]意[い]して道[みち]を渡[わた]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館で電話していたら、知らない人に注意された。
example_sentences.english: I was on the phone in the movie theater, and a stranger told me off.
example_sentences.furigana: 映[えい]画[が]館[かん]で電[でん]話[わ]していたら、知[し]らない人[ひと]に注[ちゅう]意[い]された。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫は健康に注意して、毎朝走っている。
example_sentences.english: My husband takes care of his health and runs every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]は健[けん]康[こう]に注[ちゅう]意[い]して、毎[まい]朝[あさ]走[はし]っている。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 口（こう）＋座（ざ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth's (口) seat (座): an account.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the bank your money gets a reserved place to <kanji form="座">sit</kanji>, and a slot shaped like a <kanji form="口">mouth</kanji> in the counter is where you feed it in. That spot where your money sits is your <vocabulary form="口座">bank account</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料は毎月この口座に入ります。
example_sentences.english: My salary goes into this account every month.
example_sentences.furigana: 給[きゅう]料[りょう]は毎[まい]月[つき]この口[こう]座[ざ]に入[はい]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行の窓口で娘の口座を作りました。
example_sentences.english: I opened an account for my daughter at the bank counter.
example_sentences.furigana: 銀[ぎん]行[こう]の窓[まど]口[ぐち]で娘[むすめ]の口[こう]座[ざ]を作[つく]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 口座の番号を忘れてしまって、アプリが使えません。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my account number, so I can't use the app.
example_sentences.furigana: 口[こう]座[ざ]の番[ばん]号[ごう]を忘[わす]れてしまって、アプリが使[つか]えません。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 借（しゃっ）＋金（きん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 借 しゃく → しゃっ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="金">money</kanji> you <kanji form="借">borrow</kanji> today and keep putting off paying back, month after month, is your <vocabulary form="借金">debt</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は友達から借金をして、カメラを買いました。
example_sentences.english: My older brother borrowed money from a friend and bought a camera.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は友[とも]達[だち]から借[しゃっ]金[きん]をして、カメラを買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 借金があるうちは、新しい服は買わないようにしています。
example_sentences.english: While I still have debt, I try not to buy new clothes.
example_sentences.furigana: 借[しゃっ]金[きん]があるうちは、新[あたら]しい服[ふく]は買[か]わないようにしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 借金を返すために、父は夜も働いています。
example_sentences.english: My father works nights too, to pay back the debt.
example_sentences.furigana: 借[しゃっ]金[きん]を返[かえ]すために、父[ちち]は夜[よる]も働[はたら]いています。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: The name stamp used instead of a signature: hanko.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture your family name carved into a small red-inked <reading>hunk o'</reading> boxwood that you press onto every official form. That carved 「<reading>はんこ</reading>」 is your <vocabulary form="はんこ">personal seal (stamp)</vocabulary>, and it signs for you all over Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: はんこを家に置いてきたので、市役所で何もできませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I left my seal at home, so I couldn't do anything at city hall.
example_sentences.furigana: はんこを家[いえ]に置[お]いてきたので、市[し]役[やく]所[しょ]で何[なに]もできませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 引き出しの中に、はんこが三つも入っていました。
example_sentences.english: There were three seals sitting in the drawer.
example_sentences.furigana: 引[ひ]き出[だ]しの中[なか]に、はんこが三[みっ]つも入[はい]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 署名ではなくて、はんこでもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Can I use my seal, not a signature?
example_sentences.furigana: 署[しょ]名[めい]ではなくて、はんこでもいいですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 野（の）＋山（やま）.
items.mnemonic_text: Wide fields (野) and mountains (山): the countryside.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The open <kanji form="野">plains</kanji> the village never fenced, set against the <kanji form="山">mountain</kanji> at their back, are together the <vocabulary form="野山">fields and mountains</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 秋になると、野山が赤や黄色に変わります。
example_sentences.english: In autumn, the fields and hills turn red and yellow.
example_sentences.furigana: 秋[あき]になると、野[の]山[やま]が赤[あか]や黄[き]色[いろ]に変[か]わります。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父の趣味は、野山で鳥の声を聞くことです。
example_sentences.english: My uncle's hobby is listening to birdsong out in the fields and hills.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]の趣[しゅ]味[み]は、野[の]山[やま]で鳥[とり]の声[こえ]を聞[き]くことです。

example_sentences.japanese: 町の子供たちは、野山で遊んだことがあまりありません。
example_sentences.english: Kids from town have hardly ever played out in the hills and fields.
example_sentences.furigana: 町[まち]の子[こ]供[ども]たちは、野[の]山[やま]で遊[あそ]んだことがあまりありません。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 都（と）＋市（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The capital's (都) market (市): a city.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="都">metropolis</kanji> built up by constant new arrivals, with a <kanji form="市">market</kanji> square beating at its center, is a <vocabulary form="都市">city (urban)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界の色々な都市を旅行したいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to travel to all sorts of cities around the world.
example_sentences.furigana: 世[せ]界[かい]の色[いろ]々[いろ]な都[と]市[し]を旅[りょ]行[こう]したいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい都市ほど、部屋の値段が高くなります。
example_sentences.english: The bigger the city, the more expensive rooms get.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[おお]きい都[と]市[し]ほど、部屋[へや]の値[ね]段[だん]が高[たか]くなります。

example_sentences.japanese: この都市は地下鉄が便利なので、車は要りません。
example_sentences.english: The subway in this city is so convenient that you don't need a car.
example_sentences.furigana: この都[と]市[し]は地[ち]下[か]鉄[てつ]が便[べん]利[り]なので、車[くるま]は要[い]りません。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 首（しゅ）＋都（と）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The head (首) city (都): a capital.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single <kanji form="首">neck</kanji> that the whole <kanji form="都">metropolis</kanji> turns its head on, the city every decision has to pass through, is the <vocabulary form="首都">capital (city)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 首都の名前を全部覚えるのは大変です。
example_sentences.english: Memorizing the names of all the capitals is tough.
example_sentences.furigana: 首[しゅ]都[と]の名[な]前[まえ]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]覚[おぼ]えるのは大[たい]変[へん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 首都の朝の電車は人が多すぎて、座ることができません。
example_sentences.english: Morning trains in the capital are so packed you can't get a seat.
example_sentences.furigana: 首[しゅ]都[と]の朝[あさ]の電[でん]車[しゃ]は人[ひと]が多[おお]すぎて、座[すわ]ることができません。

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、首都に引っ越すことになりました。
example_sentences.english: It's been decided that I'm moving to the capital next year.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]年[ねん]、首[しゅ]都[と]に引[ひ]っ越[こ]すことになりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（ち）＋方（ほう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The ground's (地) direction (方): a region.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A stretch of <kanji form="地">ground</kanji> marked off by which <kanji form="方">direction</kanji> it lies from the capital is a <vocabulary form="地方">region / countryside</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この地方では、冬に雪がたくさん降ります。
example_sentences.english: In this region, it snows a lot in winter.
example_sentences.furigana: この地[ち]方[ほう]では、冬[ふゆ]に雪[ゆき]がたくさん降[お]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 地方によって、言葉が少し変わります。
example_sentences.english: The way people speak changes a little from region to region.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[ち]方[ほう]によって、言[こと]葉[ば]が少[すこ]し変[か]わります。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業した後で、彼女は地方の病院で医者になりました。
example_sentences.english: After graduating from university, she became a doctor at a regional hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]を卒[そつ]業[ぎょう]した後[あと]で、彼[かの]女[じょ]は地[ち]方[ほう]の病[びょう]院[いん]で医[い]者[しゃ]になりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 国（こっ）＋家（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 国 こく → こっ.
items.mnemonic_text: A country's (国) household (家): a nation.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Treat the whole <kanji form="国">country</kanji>, walls and shared jewel and all, as one <kanji form="家">house</kanji> that everyone inside it belongs to, and you have a <vocabulary form="国家">nation / state</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 国家の予算はどう決まるのですか。
example_sentences.english: How does a national budget get decided?
example_sentences.furigana: 国[こっ]家[か]の予[よ]算[さん]はどう決[き]まるのですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 公務員は国家のために働く人です。
example_sentences.english: Civil servants are people who work for the nation.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]務[む]員[いん]は国[こっ]家[か]のために働[はたら]く人[ひと]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい国家でも、自分の文化と伝統があります。
example_sentences.english: Even a small nation has its own culture and traditions.
example_sentences.furigana: 小[ちい]さい国[こっ]家[か]でも、自[じ]分[ぶん]の文[ぶん]化[か]と伝[でん]統[とう]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 文（ぶん）＋明（めい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a people's <kanji form="文">literature</kanji> grows <kanji form="明">bright</kanji> enough to light the road for everyone who comes after, that shared glow is a <vocabulary form="文明">civilization</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史の授業で、古い文明について習いました。
example_sentences.english: In history class, we learned about ancient civilizations.
example_sentences.furigana: 歴[れき]史[し]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]で、古[ふる]い文[ぶん]明[めい]について習[なら]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 川の近くに文明が生まれた理由は何でしょう。
example_sentences.english: Why do you think civilizations were born near rivers?
example_sentences.furigana: 川[かわ]の近[ちか]くに文[ぶん]明[めい]が生[う]まれた理[り]由[ゆう]は何[なに]でしょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母はアプリで晩ご飯を注文して、文明はすごいと笑いました。
example_sentences.english: My aunt ordered dinner through an app and laughed that civilization is amazing.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]はアプリで晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を注[ちゅう]文[もん]して、文[ぶん]明[めい]はすごいと笑[わら]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 習（しゅう）＋慣（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Learning (習) that becomes routine (慣): a habit.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Something you once had to <kanji form="習">practice</kanji> on purpose and are now so <kanji form="慣">accustomed</kanji> to that you do it without thinking has turned into a <vocabulary form="習慣">custom / habit</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝コーヒーを飲むのが、私の習慣です。
example_sentences.english: Having coffee every morning is a habit of mine.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]コーヒーを飲[の]むのが、私[わたし]の習[しゅう]慣[かん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 地方によって、習慣が変わります。
example_sentences.english: Customs change from region to region.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[ち]方[ほう]によって、習[しゅう]慣[かん]が変[か]わります。

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前にゲームをする習慣は、体に悪いですよ。
example_sentences.english: Gaming right before bed is a habit that is bad for your body.
example_sentences.furigana: 寝[ね]る前[まえ]にゲームをする習[しゅう]慣[かん]は、体[からだ]に悪[わる]いですよ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 日（にっ）＋記（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 日 にち → にっ.
items.mnemonic_text: A day's (日) record (記): a diary.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A written <kanji form="記">account</kanji> that breaks the usual rule and is only ever about your own <kanji form="日">day</kanji> is a <vocabulary form="日記">diary</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は英語で日記を書いています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother keeps his diary in English.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は英[えい]語[ご]で日[にっ]記[き]を書[か]いています。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い日記を読んで、少し恥ずかしくなりました。
example_sentences.english: I read my old diary and got a little embarrassed.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い日[にっ]記[き]を読[よ]んで、少[すこ]し恥[は]ずかしくなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の間に、日記を無くしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I lost my diary somewhere during the trip.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]の間[あいだ]に、日[にっ]記[き]を無[な]くしてしまいました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 行（おこな）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: Carrying an action all the way through: okonau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="行">go</kanji> from talking about a plan to running it for real. Taking a ceremony or a survey and actually staging it is what it means to <vocabulary form="行う">carry out / conduct</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi opens every konbini restock drill by clapping once and calling 「<reading>OK, now</reading>」. That is his cue to 「<reading>おこなう</reading>」 the plan, to <vocabulary form="行う">carry out / conduct</vocabulary> it exactly as written.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者は山の上で実験を行いました。
example_sentences.english: The scientist carried out an experiment at the top of the mountain.
example_sentences.furigana: 科[か]学[がく]者[しゃ]は山[やま]の上[うえ]で実[じっ]験[けん]を行[おこな]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 市役所では毎月、外国人のために日本語の授業を行っています。
example_sentences.english: Every month, the city office holds Japanese classes for foreign residents.
example_sentences.furigana: 市[し]役[やく]所[しょ]では毎[まい]月[つき]、外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]のために日本[にほん]語[ご]の授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]を行[おこな]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 今月、工場で安全の調査を行います。
example_sentences.english: This month we are running a safety inspection at the factory.
example_sentences.furigana: 今[こん]月[げつ]、工[こう]場[じょう]で安[あん]全[ぜん]の調[ちょう]査[さ]を行[おこな]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 参（さん）＋加（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
